sentences.zh: 25%◎突厥上

translations.literal: Scroll 215, Part 1 — Treatise 140, Part 1: The Turks, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Chapter 215, Part 1 — Biographies 140, Part 1: The Turks (Upper)

sentences.zh: 夷狄為中國患，尚矣。

translations.literal: The Yi and Di have been a affliction to China for a long time already.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian peoples have been a scourge upon China since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 在前世者，史家類能言之。

translations.literal: As for earlier ages, historians have generally been able to speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: For earlier periods, historians have for the most part been able to record these matters.

sentences.zh: 唐興，蠻夷更盛衰，嘗與中國亢衡者有四：突厥、吐蕃、回鶻、雲南是也。

translations.literal: When Tang arose, the Man and Yi waxed and waned in turn; four that once matched China in strength were the Turks, Tibet, the Uyghurs, and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang rose to power, the frontier peoples rose and fell in turn; four powers that at times rivaled China were the Turks, Tibet, the Uyghurs, and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 方其時，群臣獻議盈廷，或聽或置，班然可睹也。

translations.literal: At that time, the ministers' submitted opinions filled the court; some were heeded and some set aside—clearly visible in the records.
translations.idiomatic: In those years the court overflowed with counsel from the ministers; what was adopted and what was set aside can be plainly seen in the annals.

sentences.zh: 劉貺以為：

translations.literal: Liu Dian held that:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dian argued as follows:

sentences.zh: 嚴尤辯而未詳，班固詳而未盡，榷其至當，周得上策，秦得其中，漢無策。

translations.literal: Yan You was argumentative but not thorough; Ban Gu was thorough but not exhaustive. Weighing what is most fitting: Zhou obtained the superior policy, Qin the middling, and Han had no policy at all.
translations.idiomatic: Yan You argued keenly but left gaps; Ban Gu was exhaustive but did not go far enough. Judged at their best: Zhou had the superior strategy, Qin the middling one, and Han had no real strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How is this said?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

sentences.zh: 荒服之外，聲教所不逮，其叛不為之勞師，其降不為之釋備，嚴守禦，險走集，使其為寇不能也，為臣不得也。

translations.literal: Beyond the wild domains, where civilizing influence does not reach: if they rebel, do not weary the army for them; if they submit, do not relax defenses for them. Guard strictly, hold the passes, and gather at the defiles—so that they cannot raid and cannot become subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the outer marches, where imperial culture does not reach: when they rebel, do not exhaust the army pursuing them; when they submit, do not lower your guard. Hold the defenses, control the passes, and mass at the choke points—so they can neither raid effectively nor truly become vassals.

sentences.zh: 「惠此中夏，以綏四方」，周之道也，故曰周得上策。

translations.literal: "Bless this central Xia and pacify the four quarters"—this was the Way of Zhou; therefore it is said Zhou obtained the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: "Bring benefit to the Central States and thereby pacify the four quarters"—that was the Zhou approach; hence Zhou is said to have had the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：「王侯設險以固其國。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Kings and lords set up defenses to secure their states."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes states: "Kings and feudal lords establish defenses to secure their realms."

sentences.zh: 」築長城，脩障塞，所以設險也。

translations.literal: Building the Long Wall and repairing barrier passes—this is how defenses are set up.
translations.idiomatic: Building the Long Wall and repairing frontier barriers is precisely how such defenses are established.

sentences.zh: 趙簡子起長城備胡，燕、秦亦築長城限中外，益理城塹，城全國滅，人歸咎焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Jianzi raised the Long Wall to guard against the Hu; Yan and Qin also built the Long Wall to divide inner and outer; they further improved walls and moats—yet when the cities were intact the state perished, and people blamed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jianzi built the Long Wall against the northern tribes; Yan and Qin likewise raised walls to separate China from the steppe and strengthened ramparts and moats—yet their states fell while those walls still stood, and many blamed the policy.

sentences.zh: 後魏築長城，議者以為人治一步，方千里，役三十萬人，不旬朔而獲久逸，故曰秦得中策。

translations.literal: Later Wei built the Long Wall; debaters held that for one man to work one pace, a thousand li were secured, with three hundred thousand men levied—in less than a month and a half lasting ease was gained; therefore it is said Qin obtained the middling policy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wei built the Long Wall, advocates argued that one man's labor over a single pace secured a thousand li, with three hundred thousand men conscripted—yet in less than a month and a half they gained lasting security; hence Qin is credited with the middling strategy.

sentences.zh: 漢以宗女嫁匈奴，而高祖亦審魯元不能止趙王之逆謀，謂能息匈奴之叛，非也。

translations.literal: Han married imperial daughters to the Xiongnu, and Gaozu also knew that the Princess of Lu could not stop the King of Zhao's rebellious plot—yet held that this could quell Xiongnu rebellion; it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: The Han sent imperial princesses to marry Xiongnu chiefs, and even Gaozu knew that the Princess of Lu could not halt the King of Zhao's conspiracy—yet they still believed marriage alliance would quiet Xiongnu revolt; it did not.

sentences.zh: 且冒頓手弒其親，而冀其不與外祖爭強，豈不惑哉？

translations.literal: Moreover Modu personally slew his own father, yet they hoped he would not contend for power with his wife's grandfather—how is this not deluded?
translations.idiomatic: Modu had murdered his own father with his own hand, yet they hoped he would not strive against his wife's grandfather for dominance—was this not folly?

sentences.zh: 然則知和親非久安計而為之者，以天下初定，紓歲月之禍耳。

translations.literal: Thus knowing that marriage alliance was no long-term plan, they did it only because the realm was newly settled, to ease calamity for a time.
translations.idiomatic: They knew full well that marriage alliance was no lasting solution; they adopted it only because the empire had just been pacified, to buy a few years' respite from disaster.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，中國艾安，胡寇益希，疏而絕之，此其時也。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time, China was tranquil and at ease, and Hu raids grew rare—to keep them at a distance and cut them off was the moment for it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, the empire was secure and northern raids grew infrequent—the time had come to keep the barbarians at arm's length and sever ties altogether.

sentences.zh: 方更糜耗華夏，連兵積年，故嚴尤以為下策。

translations.literal: Just then they further wasted and exhausted the Central Lands, waging war year after year—therefore Yan You held this to be the inferior policy.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they further drained the heartland and fought year after year—hence Yan You judged this the worst policy of all.

sentences.zh: 然而漢至昭、宣，武士練習，斥候精明，匈奴收跡遠徙，猶襲奉春之過舉，傾府藏給西北，歲二億七十萬。

translations.literal: Yet by Han's Zhao and Xuan reigns, warriors were trained, scouts keen, and the Xiongnu withdrew far away—still they repeated Feng Chun's mistaken course, emptying the treasury for the northwest: two hundred and seventy million a year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even by the reigns of Zhao and Xuan, with trained soldiers and sharp scouts and the Xiongnu driven far away, the court still repeated Feng Chun's error, pouring the treasury into the northwest—two hundred and seventy million a year.

sentences.zh: 皇室淑女，嬪於穹廬；

translations.literal: Refined ladies of the imperial house became consorts in felt tents;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial daughters of fine breeding were given as brides to yurt-dwellers;

sentences.zh: 掖庭良人，降於沙漠。

translations.literal: worthy women of the inner palace were sent down to the desert.
translations.idiomatic: and palace women of rank were dispatched to the sands of the north.

sentences.zh: 夫貢子女方物，臣僕之職也。

translations.literal: To present sons and daughters and local products is the duty of subjects and servants.
translations.idiomatic: It is the duty of vassals to present sons, daughters, and tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "None dares not come to the audience; none dares not come to pay homage."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "None dares fail to come to court; none dares fail to acknowledge our sovereignty."

sentences.zh: 」荒服稱其來，不言往也。

translations.literal: For the wild domains it speaks of their coming, not of our going.
translations.idiomatic: For the outer marches the text speaks of their coming to us, not of our going to them.

sentences.zh: 公及吳盟，諱而不書。

translations.literal: The Duke's alliance with Wu is concealed and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke's treaty with Wu is passed over in silence and left unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 奈何以天子之尊，與匈奴約為兄弟，帝女之號，與胡媼並御；

translations.literal: How then, with the Son of Heaven's dignity, to covenant with the Xiongnu as brothers, and an imperial daughter's title to share the bed with a Hu chieftain's mother;
translations.idiomatic: How then could the Son of Heaven, in all his majesty, treat the Xiongnu as sworn brothers, and an imperial princess share a household with a barbarian chieftain's widow;

sentences.zh: 蒸母報子，從其汙俗？

translations.literal: a stepmother marrying her stepson, following their filthy custom?
translations.idiomatic: stepmothers marrying stepsons, conforming to their debased customs?

sentences.zh: 中國異於蠻夷者，有父子男女之別也。

translations.literal: What distinguishes China from the Man and Yi is the separation of father and son, male and female.
translations.idiomatic: What sets China apart from the barbarians is the distinction between father and son, man and woman.

sentences.zh: 婉冶之姿，毀節異類，垢辱甚矣。

translations.literal: Graceful and lovely forms, their integrity destroyed among alien peoples—filth and shame indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Women of grace and beauty, their virtue ruined among foreigners—the disgrace was profound.

sentences.zh: 漢之君臣，莫之恥也。

translations.literal: Among Han's rulers and ministers, none felt shame at this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither emperor nor minister of the Han felt shame at it.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉羌狄居塞垣，資奉逾昔。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin the Qiang and Di dwelt along the frontier walls, their stipends exceeding those of old.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin the Qiang and Di settled along the frontier, receiving support greater than ever before.

sentences.zh: 百人之酋，千口之長，賜金印紫綬，食王侯之俸。

translations.literal: Chiefs of a hundred men, leaders of a thousand mouths, were given gold seals and purple cords and received the salaries of kings and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs of a hundred households and leaders of a thousand clans were granted gold seals and purple ribbons and paid at the rate of kings and marquises.

sentences.zh: 牧馬之童，乘羊之隸，賫毳毼邀利者，相錯於路。

translations.literal: Boys who tended horses, slaves who rode sheep, bearing felt and furs to seek profit—crowded the roads in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-herding boys and sheep-riding servants, laden with furs and fleeces in pursuit of profit, thronged the highways without end.

sentences.zh: 耒耨之利，絲枲所生，散於數萬里之外。

translations.literal: The gains of plow and hoe, what silk and hemp produce, were scattered tens of thousands of li away.
translations.idiomatic: The fruits of the plow and the products of silk and hemp were dispersed tens of thousands of li beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 胡夷歲驕，華夏日蹙。

translations.literal: The Hu and Yi grew haughtier year by year; the Central Lands shrank day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes grew more arrogant each year while the heartland contracted daily.

sentences.zh: 方其強也，竭人力以征之；

translations.literal: When they were strong, all human strength was exhausted to campaign against them;
translations.idiomatic: When they were strong, the empire exhausted its manpower to fight them;

sentences.zh: 其服也，養之如初。

translations.literal: when they submitted, they were nourished as at first.
translations.idiomatic: when they submitted, they were sustained as generously as before.

sentences.zh: 病則受養，強則內攻，中國為羌胡服役且千載，可不悲哉！

translations.literal: When weak they received support; when strong they attacked within—China has served the Qiang and Hu for nearly a thousand years; is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: When weak they were fed; when strong they turned inward to attack—China has served the Qiang and Hu for nearly a millennium. What tragedy could be greater?

sentences.zh: 誠能移其財以賞戍卒，則民富；

translations.literal: If one could truly shift that wealth to reward garrison soldiers, the people would be rich;
translations.idiomatic: Had that wealth been redirected to reward frontier garrisons, the people would have prospered;

sentences.zh: 移其爵以餌守臣，則將良。

translations.literal: shift those ranks to entice frontier officials, and the generals would be good.
translations.idiomatic: and those titles used to reward border commanders, the generals would have been capable.

sentences.zh: 富利歸於我，危亡移於彼，無納女之辱，無傳送之勞。

translations.literal: Wealth and profit would return to us, peril and ruin shift to them—without the shame of giving daughters, without the toil of convoy.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth would stay at home and danger fall on them—without the humiliation of sending princesses, without the burden of endless convoys.

sentences.zh: 棄此而不為，故曰漢無策。

translations.literal: To abandon this and not act—therefore it is said Han had no policy.
translations.idiomatic: They abandoned this course and did nothing—hence Han is said to have had no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 嚴尤謂古無上策，謂不能臣妾之也，誠能之而不用耳。

translations.literal: Yan You said antiquity had no superior policy, meaning they could not make them subjects and concubines—yet they truly could have and simply did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan You claimed antiquity lacked a superior strategy because they could not reduce the barbarians to subjection—yet they could have; they simply chose not to.

sentences.zh: 秦無策，謂攘狄而亡國也。

translations.literal: Qin had no policy, meaning it expelled the Di and perished.
translations.idiomatic: He said Qin had no strategy because it drove out the Di and lost the realm.

sentences.zh: 秦亡，非攘狄也。

translations.literal: Qin's fall was not from expelling the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Qin did not fall because it expelled the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 漢得下策，謂伐胡而人病。

translations.literal: Han obtained the inferior policy, meaning it campaigned against the Hu and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He called Han's approach the inferior strategy—campaigning against the Hu until the people were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 人既病矣，又役人而奉之，無策也。

translations.literal: The people were already afflicted, yet they further conscripted men to support them—no policy at all.
translations.idiomatic: The people were already worn down, yet the court still levied men to sustain the barbarians—this was no policy whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 故曰嚴尤辯而未詳也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said Yan You was argumentative but not thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yan You is judged argumentative but incomplete.

sentences.zh: 班固謂「其來慕義，則接以禮讓。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said, "When they come admiring righteousness, receive them with ritual courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote, "When they come in admiration of our virtue, receive them with ritual courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this wrong?

sentences.zh: 禮讓以交君子，非所以接禽獸夷狄也。

translations.literal: Ritual courtesy is for dealing with gentlemen, not for receiving birds, beasts, and barbarian Yi and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual courtesy is for engaging with cultivated men, not for receiving beasts and barbarians.

sentences.zh: 纖麗外散，則戎羯之心生；

translations.literal: When fine splendor is displayed outward, the Rong and Jie take heart;
translations.idiomatic: When China's refinements are displayed abroad, the Rong and Jie grow bold;

sentences.zh: 戎羯之心生，則侵盜之本也。

translations.literal: when the Rong and Jie take heart, that is the root of invasion and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: and once they grow bold, raiding and plunder inevitably follow.

sentences.zh: 聖人飲食聲樂不與之共，來朝坐於門外，舌人體委以食之，不使知馨香嘉味也。

translations.literal: The sages did not share food, drink, or music with them; when they came to court they sat outside the gate, and interpreters relayed food set out for them—they were not allowed to know fragrant and fine flavors.
translations.idiomatic: The sages did not share food, drink, or music with them; when they came to court they sat outside the gate, and interpreters conveyed provisions to them—they were not permitted to taste China's finest flavors.

sentences.zh: 漢氏習玩驕虜，使其悅燕、趙之色，甘太官之珍，服以文綺羅紈，供之則增求，絕之則招怨，是飽豺狼以良肉，而縱其獵噬也。

translations.literal: The Han habitually indulged and pampered the proud barbarians, making them delight in Yan and Zhao beauties, savor the Grand Steward's delicacies, and dress in patterned silks and gauze—supply them and demands increase; cut them off and resentment is invited: this is feeding wolves fine meat and letting them hunt and devour.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court habitually coddled arrogant nomads, letting them enjoy the beauties of Yan and Zhao, savor imperial delicacies, and dress in brocade and gauze—feed them and their demands grew; cut them off and they turned hostile. This was feeding wolves the finest meat and then letting them hunt at will.

sentences.zh: 華人步卒利險阻，虜人騎兵利平地，堅守無與追奔競逐，來則杜險使不得進，去則閉險使不得還，沖以長戟，臨以強弩，非求勝也，譬諸蟲豸虺蜴，何禮讓之接哉？

translations.literal: Chinese infantry excel in rugged terrain; barbarian cavalry excel on level ground. Hold firm and do not chase in running pursuit—when they come, block the passes so they cannot advance; when they leave, shut the passes so they cannot return. Charge with long halberds, face them with strong crossbows—not seeking victory alone, but like insects, snakes, and lizards—what ritual courtesy is there to receive them with?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese foot soldiers excel in rugged country; nomad horsemen excel on open ground. Stand firm and do not pursue in open chase—when they come, seal the passes so they cannot advance; when they leave, close the passes so they cannot return. Meet them with long halberds and strong crossbows—not merely to win battles, but because they are like vermin and serpents. What place has ritual courtesy in receiving such foes?

sentences.zh: 故曰班固詳而未盡者，此也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that where Ban Gu was thorough but not exhaustive—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant when Ban Gu is said to have been thorough but not exhaustive.

sentences.zh: 杜佑謂：

translations.literal: Du You held that:
translations.idiomatic: Du You argued:

sentences.zh: 秦以區區關中滅六強國，今竭萬方之財，上奉京師，外有犬戎恁陵，陷城數百，內有兵革未寧，三紀矣。

translations.literal: Qin with its narrow Guanzhong destroyed six great states; now all the realm's wealth is exhausted to supply the capital, while outside the Quanrong wantonly encroach and have taken hundreds of cities, and within arms have not been quiet for three reign-periods.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, from the narrow confines of Guanzhong, overthrew six great powers; now the empire exhausts its wealth to feed the capital, while beyond the frontier the Tibetans raid at will and have captured hundreds of cities, and within the realm war has not ceased for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 豈制置異術，古今殊時乎？

translations.literal: Is it that institutions and methods differ, and ancient and modern times are not the same?
translations.idiomatic: Is this because institutions differ, and ancient and modern times are not comparable?

sentences.zh: 周制，步百為畝，畝百給一夫。

translations.literal: Under Zhou institutions, one hundred paces made a mu, and one hundred mu supported one man.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou system, one hundred paces made a mu, and one hundred mu supported one household.

sentences.zh: 商鞅佐秦，以為地利不盡，更以二百四十步為畝，百畝給一夫。

translations.literal: Shang Yang assisted Qin, holding that land's benefit was not fully used; he changed it so two hundred forty paces made a mu, and one hundred mu supported one man.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Yang aided Qin, arguing that land was not fully utilized; he redefined the mu as two hundred forty paces and assigned one hundred mu to each household.

sentences.zh: 又以秦地曠而人寡，晉地狹而人夥，誘三晉之人耕而優其田宅，復及子孫，使秦人應敵於外，非農與戰不得入官。

translations.literal: He also held that Qin lands were broad and people few, while Jin lands were narrow and people many; he lured the people of the Three Jin to farm and favored their fields and dwellings, with exemptions extending to descendants, so Qin men faced enemies abroad—none could enter office except through farming or fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Qin had vast lands and few people, while Jin was crowded; he enticed settlers from the Three Jin to farm, granting them favorable land and tax exemptions for their descendants, while Qin natives faced enemies abroad—office was open only to farmers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大率百人以五十人為農，五十人習戰，故兵強國富。

translations.literal: Roughly, of every hundred men fifty farmed and fifty trained for war—therefore the army was strong and the state rich.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly half of every hundred men farmed and half trained for war—hence Qin's armies were strong and its treasury full.

sentences.zh: 其後仕宦途多，末業日滋。

translations.literal: Afterward the paths to office multiplied, and secondary trades daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: Later the routes to office multiplied, and nonessential occupations proliferated.

sentences.zh: 今大率百人才十人為農，餘皆習佗技。

translations.literal: Now of every hundred men only about ten farm; the rest all practice other skills.
translations.idiomatic: Today only about ten in every hundred farm; the rest pursue other trades.

sentences.zh: 又秦、漢鄭渠溉田四萬頃，白渠溉田四千五百頃，永徽中，兩渠灌浸不過萬頃，大歷初，減至六千畝。

translations.literal: Moreover in Qin and Han the Zheng Canal irrigated forty thousand qing and the Bai Canal four thousand five hundred qing; in the Yonghui era the two canals irrigated no more than ten thousand qing; in early Dali this fell to six thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin and Han the Zheng Canal irrigated forty thousand qing and the Bai Canal four thousand five hundred qing; by the Yonghui era combined irrigation had fallen below ten thousand qing, and by early Dali to six thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 畝晙一斛，歲少四五百萬斛。

translations.literal: Per mu one hu less each year—four to five million hu less annually.
translations.idiomatic: At one hu less per mu, the annual shortfall amounts to four or five million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 地利耗，人力散，欲求強富，不可得也。

translations.literal: Land's benefit is exhausted, human strength scattered—to seek strength and wealth is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: With land productivity exhausted and manpower dispersed, strength and wealth cannot be attained.

sentences.zh: 漢時，長安北七百里即匈奴之地，侵掠未嘗暫息。

translations.literal: In Han times, seven hundred li north of Chang'an was Xiongnu territory; raids never ceased even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, seven hundred li north of Chang'an lay Xiongnu land, and raids never ceased even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 計其舉國之眾，不過漢一大郡，鼉錯請備障塞，故北邊妥安。

translations.literal: Counting their whole state's population, it did not exceed one large Han commandery; Chao Cuo asked to prepare barriers and passes, and so the northern border was secure and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Their entire population was no larger than a single Han commandery; Chao Cuo urged strengthening the frontier defenses, and the north remained secure.

sentences.zh: 今潼關之西，隴山之東，鄜坊之南，終南之北，十餘州之地，已數十萬家。

translations.literal: Now west of Tong Pass, east of Long Mountain, south of Fu and Fang, north of Zhongnan—more than ten prefectures' territory already holds hundreds of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: Today west of Tong Pass, east of Long Mountain, south of Fu and Fang, and north of Zhongnan—more than ten prefectures already hold hundreds of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃綿力薄材，食鮮藝拙，不及中國遠甚，誠能復兩渠之饒，誘農夫趣耕，擇險要，繕城壘，屯田蓄力，河、隴可復，豈唯自守而已。

translations.literal: Tibet's strength is soft and its talent thin; their food is raw and their crafts clumsy—far inferior to China. If one could truly restore the two canals' abundance, entice farmers to hurry to plow, choose strategic points, repair walls and ramparts, garrison fields and store strength—the He and Long regions could be recovered, and not only for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet's power is feeble and its skills crude; their diet is raw and their crafts clumsy—far inferior to China. Restore the two canals' fertility, encourage farmers to till, fortify strategic points, garrison the frontier, and the He and Long regions could be recovered—not merely held in defense.

sentences.zh: 至佑孫牧亦曰：

translations.literal: Du You's grandson Mu also said:
translations.idiomatic: Du You's grandson Du Mu likewise wrote:

sentences.zh: 天下無事時，大臣偷處榮逸，戰士離落，兵甲鈍弊，車馬刓弱，天下雜然盜發，則疾驅以戰，是謂宿敗之師。

translations.literal: When the realm is without affairs, great ministers steal ease in glory and comfort, warriors scatter and fall away, arms and armor grow dull and worn, chariots and horses weaken and waste—then when bandits rise everywhere in disorder, they are hurried to battle: this is called an army defeated in advance.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime ministers grow complacent in luxury, soldiers drift apart, arms rust, and horses weaken—then when rebellion erupts everywhere they are rushed into battle. Such troops are defeated before they march.

sentences.zh: 此不搜練之過，其敗一也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of not selecting and drilling troops—the first defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first cause of defeat: failure to recruit and train soldiers properly.

sentences.zh: 百人荷戈，仰食縣官，則挾千夫之名，大將小裨操其餘贏，以虜壯為幸，執兵者常少，糜食者常多，築壘未乾，公囊已虛。

translations.literal: A hundred men bear weapons and eat from the district offices, yet claim the name of a thousand; great generals and minor officers take the surplus for themselves, counting strong barbarians as good fortune—those who hold weapons are always few, those who waste provisions always many; before the rampart is dry, the public purse is empty.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred men bear arms on government rations yet claim credit for a thousand; generals and subordinates pocket the surplus and welcome strong enemies—fighters are always few, freeloaders many. Before the fortifications are finished, the treasury is empty.

sentences.zh: 此不責實之過，其敗二也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of not holding to facts—the second defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second cause of defeat: failure to enforce accountability.

sentences.zh: 戰小勝則張皇其功，奔走獻狀以邀賞，或一日再賜，一月累封，凱還未歌，書品已崇，爵命極矣，田宮廣矣，金繒溢矣，子孫官矣，肯外死勤於我哉？

translations.literal: After a small victory they inflate their merit, running to present reports to seek rewards—sometimes twice in one day, accumulated enfeoffments in one month; before the victory song is sung, their written rank is already raised, titles and commands at the limit, fields and mansions broad, gold and silks overflowing, sons and grandsons given office—would they die outside in earnest service to us?
translations.idiomatic: After minor victories they exaggerate their achievements and rush forward petitions for reward—sometimes twice in a single day, with multiple enfeoffments in a month. Before victory celebrations end, their ranks are raised, estates expanded, gold and silk overflowing, and sons and grandsons given office. Why would they risk their lives in earnest service?

sentences.zh: 此賞厚之過，其敗三也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of rewards too generous—the third defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third cause of defeat: rewards far too generous.

sentences.zh: 多喪兵士，顛翻大都，則跳身而來，刺邦而去，回視刀鋸、菜色甚安，一歲未更，已立於壇墀之上。

translations.literal: Having lost many soldiers and overturned a great metropolis, they leap forward to come, stab the state and leave, looking back at swords and saws with a very calm face—within a year, not yet changed, they already stand upon the altar terrace.
translations.idiomatic: After losing many troops and failing catastrophically, they leap to new commands, abandon their posts, and face execution with equanimity—within a year, without repentance, they stand again at court.

sentences.zh: 此輕罰之過，其敗四也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of punishments too light—the fourth defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth cause of defeat: punishments far too lenient.

sentences.zh: 大將將兵，柄不得專，一曰為偃月，一曰為魚麗，三軍萬夫，環旋翔佯，愰駭之間，虜騎乘之。

translations.literal: The great general commands troops but cannot hold sole authority—one day it is the crescent formation, one day the fish-scale formation; the three armies and ten thousand men wheel and circle in feigned maneuvers, and in a moment of confusion barbarian cavalry seize the chance.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders cannot exercise sole authority—one day the formation is crescent-shaped, the next fish-scale; tens of thousands wheel and feint in confusion, and in that moment nomad cavalry strike.

sentences.zh: 此不專任之過，其敗五也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of not entrusting sole responsibility—the fifth defeat.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth cause of defeat: failure to grant commanders full authority.

sentences.zh: 元和時，團兵數十萬以誅蔡，天下乾耗，四歲然後能取之，蓋五敗不去也。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, several hundred thousand regiment troops were used to punish Cai; the realm was drained dry, and only after four years could it be taken—because the five defeats were not removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era hundreds of thousands of troops were mobilized against Cai; the empire was exhausted, and victory took four years—because these five faults were never corrected.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，盜子若孫悉來走命，未幾而燕、趙亂，引師起將，五敗益甚，不能加威於反虜。

translations.literal: In early Changqing, bandits' sons and grandsons all came running to submit; before long Yan and Zhao were in turmoil—raising armies and appointing generals, the five defeats grew worse, and they could not impose authority on rebellious barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In early Changqing rebel heirs submitted in droves; soon Yan and Zhao erupted in revolt. Armies were raised and generals appointed, yet the five faults grew worse and the court could not impose its will on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 二杜之論如此。

translations.literal: The two Dus' arguments were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the arguments of the two Du ministers.

sentences.zh: 廣德、建中間，吐蕃再飲馬岷江，常以南詔為前鋒，操倍尋之戟，且戰且進，蜀兵折刃吞鏃，不能斃一戎。

translations.literal: Between Guangde and Jianzhong, Tibet again watered horses at the Min River, often using Nanzhao as vanguard, wielding halberds twice a man's height, fighting as they advanced—Shu soldiers broke blades swallowing arrowheads, unable to kill a single barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Guangde and Jianzhong reigns Tibet repeatedly crossed the Min River, often with Nanzhao as vanguard wielding halberds twice a man's height, advancing as they fought. Shu troops broke their blades and swallowed arrowheads yet could not kill a single enemy.

sentences.zh: 戎兵日深，疫死日眾，自度不能留，輒引去。

translations.literal: Barbarian troops pressed deeper daily; plague deaths grew daily—they judged they could not remain and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As the invaders pressed deeper and plague deaths mounted, they judged they could not hold and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蜀人語曰：「西戎尚可，南蠻殘我。

translations.literal: The people of Shu said: "The western Rong are still tolerable; the southern Man destroy us."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu had a saying: "The Tibetans we can endure; it is the southern tribes who destroy us."

sentences.zh: 」至韋臯鑿青溪道以和群蠻，使道蜀入貢，擇子弟習書算於成都，業成而去，習知山川要害。

translations.literal: When Wei Gao cut the Qingxi Road to pacify the various Man, he had them pass through Shu to offer tribute, selected sons and younger brothers to study writing and reckoning in Chengdu—when their studies were done they departed, having learned the mountains and rivers' strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao opened the Qingxi Road to pacify the southern tribes, routing their tribute missions through Shu and selecting their sons to study writing and reckoning in Chengdu. When they returned home, they knew every mountain pass and strategic point.

sentences.zh: 文宗時，大入成都，自越巂以北八百里，民畜為空，又敗卒貧民因緣掠殺，官不能禁。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wenzong's time they entered Chengdu on a great scale; from Yuexi northward eight hundred li, people and livestock were emptied; moreover defeated soldiers and poor people took occasion to plunder and kill—the officials could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong they sacked Chengdu on a vast scale; for eight hundred li north from Yuexi, people and livestock were wiped out. Defeated soldiers and the destitute joined in the slaughter, and officials could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 自是群蠻常有屠蜀之心，蜀民苦於重征者，亦欲啟之以幸非常。

translations.literal: From this the various Man often had the heart to slaughter Shu; Shu people suffering from heavy levies also wished to open the way to them, hoping for the extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the southern tribes often planned to devastate Shu, while Shu people crushed by heavy taxes were willing to open the passes, hoping for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 歲發戍卒，不習山川之險，緩步一舍，已呵然流汗。

translations.literal: Each year garrison soldiers were dispatched, unaccustomed to the mountains and rivers' dangers—at an easy pace of one stage they were already gasping and sweating.
translations.idiomatic: Each year garrison troops were sent who knew nothing of the mountain terrain—after a single easy day's march they were already gasping and drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 為將者刻薄自入，給帛則以疏易良，賦粟以沙參粒，故邊卒怨望而巴、蜀危憂。

translations.literal: Generals were harsh and kept gains for themselves—giving cloth they exchanged coarse for fine; levying grain they mixed sand with grain—therefore frontier soldiers resented and looked on in anger, and Ba and Shu were in peril and worry.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders were harsh and corrupt, substituting coarse cloth for fine and mixing sand with grain rations. Frontier soldiers grew resentful, and Ba and Shu lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 孫樵謂：「宜詔嚴道、沈黎、越巂三州，度要害，募卒以守。

translations.literal: Sun Qiao held: "It is fitting to decree the three prefectures of Yandao, Shenli, and Yuexi, survey strategic points, and recruit soldiers to guard them."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qiao urged: "The court should order the three prefectures of Yandao, Shenli, and Yuexi to survey strategic points and recruit local garrisons."

sentences.zh: 且兵籍於州則易役，卒出於邊則習險，相地分屯，春耕夏蠶以資衣食，秋冬嚴壁以俟寇。

translations.literal: Moreover, if soldiers are registered in the prefecture they are easy to levy; if troops come from the border they are accustomed to danger—survey the land and divide garrisons, plow in spring and raise silkworms in summer to supply food and clothing, in autumn and winter strengthen walls to await raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers registered locally are easy to mobilize; troops raised on the frontier know the terrain. Divide garrisons by terrain, farm in spring and raise silkworms in summer for provisions, and fortify in autumn and winter to await invasion.

sentences.zh: 歲遣廉吏視卒之有無，則官無饋運，吏無牟盜。

translations.literal: Each year send honest officials to inspect whether soldiers are present or absent—then the offices need no convoy supply, and clerks have no profit to steal.
translations.idiomatic: Send honest officials annually to verify troop strength, and the state need not ship supplies from afar nor will clerks profit from corruption.

sentences.zh: 」此其備禦之策可施行者，著之於篇。

translations.literal: These are the defense policies that can be put into practice—recorded in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Such defensive measures as these could actually be implemented; they are recorded here in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 凡突厥、吐蕃、回鶻以盛衰先後為次；

translations.literal: In general the Turks, Tibet, and the Uyghurs are ordered by the sequence of their rise and decline;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, Tibet, and the Uyghurs are treated in order of their rise and fall;

sentences.zh: 東夷、西域又次之，跡用兵之輕重也；

translations.literal: the Eastern Yi and the Western Regions come after, tracing the weight of military use;
translations.idiomatic: followed by the Eastern Yi and the Western Regions, reflecting the scale of military engagement;

sentences.zh: 終之以南蠻，記唐所繇亡云。

translations.literal: it ends with the southern Man, recording how Tang came to perish.
translations.idiomatic: and concluding with the southern tribes, recording how the Tang dynasty met its end.

sentences.zh: 突厥阿史那氏，蓋古匈奴北部也。

translations.literal: The Turks of the Ashina clan were probably the northern branch of the ancient Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks of the Ashina clan were descended from the northern branch of the ancient Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 居金山之陽，臣於蠕蠕，種裔繁衍。

translations.literal: They dwelt south of the Altai Mountains, submitted to the Rouran, and their lineage multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: They lived south of the Altai Mountains, submitted to the Rouran khans, and their clans multiplied.

sentences.zh: 至吐門，遂強大，更號可汗，猶單于也，妻曰可敦。

translations.literal: When Tumen came, they grew powerful, changed their title to khan—as with chanyu—and his wife was called khatun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tumen they grew powerful, adopted the title khan as equivalent to chanyu, and called his consort khatun.

sentences.zh: 其地三垂薄海，南抵大漠。

translations.literal: Their territory on three sides reached near the sea; to the south it reached the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands stretched on three sides nearly to the sea and southward to the great desert.

sentences.zh: 其別部典兵者曰設，子弟曰特勒，大臣曰葉護，曰屈律啜、曰阿波、曰俟利發、曰吐屯、曰俟斤、曰閻洪達、曰頡利發、曰達幹，凡二十八等，皆世其官而無員限。

translations.literal: Their separate divisions commanding troops were called she; sons and younger brothers were called tegin; great ministers were called yabghu, and also qulug chuo, apo, irbir, tutun, irkin, yen hongda, irbir, and tagin—in all twenty-eight grades, all hereditary offices without fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors of subordinate tribes were called she; princes were tegin; chief ministers yabghu, with twenty-eight ranks in all—including qulug chuo, apo, irbir, tutun, irkin, and tagin—all hereditary offices without fixed numbers.

sentences.zh: 衛士曰附離。

translations.literal: Guards were called fuli.
translations.idiomatic: Royal guards were called fuli.

sentences.zh: 可汗建廷都斤山，牙門樹金狼頭纛，坐常東向。

translations.literal: The khan established his court on Mount Dujin; at the gate he raised a golden wolf-head banner and always sat facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The khan established his court on Mount Dujin, raised a golden wolf-head banner at his gate, and always sat facing east.

sentences.zh: 隋大業之亂，始畢可汗咄吉嗣立，華人多往依之，契丹、室韋、吐谷渾、高昌皆役屬，竇建德、薛舉、劉武周、梁師都、李軌、王世充等倔起虎視，悉臣尊之。

translations.literal: In the disorders of Sui's Daye reign, Shibi Khan Tuji succeeded; many Chinese went to rely on him; Khitan, Shiwei, Tuyuhun, and Gaochang all served and submitted; Dou Jiande, Xue Ju, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, Wang Shichong, and others rose fiercely and watched like tigers—all submitted and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaos of the Sui's final years, Shibi Khan Tuji succeeded to power. Chinese refugees flocked to him; the Khitan, Shiwei, Tuyuhun, and Gaochang all submitted. Rebel leaders Dou Jiande, Xue Ju, Liu Wuzhou, Liang Shidu, Li Gui, and Wang Shichong all bowed to his authority.

sentences.zh: 控弦且百萬，戎狄熾強，古未有也。

translations.literal: Those who drew the bow numbered nearly a million; the Rong and Di blazed in strength such as antiquity had never seen.
translations.idiomatic: His bowmen numbered nearly a million—the northern peoples had never been so powerful.

sentences.zh: 高祖起太原，遣府司馬劉文靜往聘，與連和，始畢使特勒康稍利獻馬二千、兵五百來會。

translations.literal: Gaozu rose at Taiyuan and sent Prefecture Marshal Liu Wenjing to court them and ally; Shibi sent the tegin Kangshaoli with two thousand horses and five hundred troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, he sent Liu Wenjing to negotiate an alliance. Shibi dispatched the tegin Kangshaoli with two thousand horses and five hundred warriors to join him.

sentences.zh: 帝平京師，遂恃功，使者每來多橫驕。

translations.literal: After the Emperor pacified the capital, they relied on their merit; envoys who came were mostly arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor pacified the capital, the Turks grew arrogant over their contribution, and their envoys came with increasing insolence.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，骨咄祿特勒來朝，帝宴太極殿，為奏九部樂，引升御坐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, the tegin Kutlug came to court; the Emperor feasted him in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, had the nine orchestras play, and led him up to the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude the tegin Kutlug came to court. The emperor feasted him in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, ordered the nine court orchestras to perform, and seated him beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始畢牙帳自破，帝問內史令蕭瑀，瑀曰：「魏文帝幸許，城門無故壞，是年文帝崩，豈其類耶？

translations.literal: That year Shibi's camp broke apart by itself; the Emperor asked Internal Affairs Director Xiao Yu, who said: "When Emperor Wen of Wei visited Xu, the city gate broke for no reason—that year Emperor Wen died. Is this not of the same kind?"
translations.idiomatic: That year Shibi's camp collapsed on its own. The emperor asked Internal Affairs Director Xiao Yu, who replied: "When Emperor Wen of Wei visited Xu, the city gate broke without cause—and that year he died. Is this not a similar omen?"

sentences.zh: 」二年，始畢自將度河，至夏州，與賊梁師都合，又佐劉武周以五百騎入句註，將侵太原。

translations.literal: In the second year Shibi personally led troops across the river to Xia Prefecture, joined the rebel Liang Shidu, and also aided Liu Wuzhou with five hundred horsemen entering Gouzhu, about to invade Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Shibi personally crossed the Yellow River to Xia Prefecture, joined the rebel Liang Shidu, and sent five hundred horsemen with Liu Wuzhou through Gouzhu to threaten Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會病死，帝為發哀長樂門，詔群臣即館吊其使，遣使者持段物三萬賻之。

translations.literal: He happened to die of illness; the Emperor held mourning at Changle Gate, ordered the ministers to condole with his envoys at their lodging, and sent envoys with thirty thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness before the campaign could proceed. The emperor ordered mourning at Changle Gate, commanded ministers to condole with the Turkish envoys, and sent thirty thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子什缽幼，不克立，以為泥步設，使居東偏，立其弟俟利弗設，是為處羅可汗。

translations.literal: His son Shibo was young and could not be established; he was made Nibu she and sent to dwell in the eastern quarter; his younger brother Irbis she was established—this was Elui Khan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibo was too young to succeed and was made Nibu she in the eastern territories. His younger brother Irbis she was enthroned as Elui Khan.

sentences.zh: 處羅復妻隋義成公主，遣使來告，則又潛通王世充，潞州總管李襲譽擊斬其使，取牛羊萬餘。

translations.literal: Elui again married Princess Yicheng of Sui and sent envoys to announce it, yet secretly communicated with Wang Shichong; Luzhou Inspector Li Xiyu attacked and beheaded his envoys, taking more than ten thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Elui married Sui Princess Yicheng and sent envoys to announce the alliance, yet secretly communicated with Wang Shichong. Luzhou Inspector Li Xiyu ambushed and killed his envoys, seizing more than ten thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 處羅迎隋蕭皇后及齊王柬之子正道於竇建德所，因立正道為隋王，奉隋後，隋人沒者隸之，行其正朔，置百官，居定襄，眾萬人。

translations.literal: Elui welcomed Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao, son of Prince of Qi Yang You, from Dou Jiande's place; he thereupon established Zhengdao as King of Sui, served the Sui house, attached captured Sui people to him, used Sui calendar and rites, set up the hundred offices, dwelt at Dingxiang, with a following of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Elui received Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao, son of the Prince of Qi, from Dou Jiande's custody. He installed Zhengdao as King of Sui, restored Sui institutions and calendar, assigned captured Sui subjects to his court, and established a government of ten thousand followers at Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 秦王討武周也，處羅以弟步利設騎二千會并州三日，多掠城中婦人女子去，總管李仲文不能制，以俱儉特勒助屯。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin campaigned against Wuzhou, Elui sent his younger brother Buli she with two thousand horsemen to join at Bing Prefecture for three days, carrying off many women and girls from the city; Inspector Li Zhongwen could not control them and had the tegin Juqian assist in garrisoning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin campaigned against Liu Wuzhou, Elui sent his brother Buli she with two thousand horsemen to Bing Prefecture for three days. They abducted many women from the city. Inspector Li Zhongwen could not restrain them and assigned the tegin Juqian to assist in garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 明年，謀取并州置楊正道，卜之，不吉，左右諫止，處羅曰：「我先人失國，賴隋以存，今忘之，不祥。

translations.literal: The next year he plotted to take Bing Prefecture and install Yang Zhengdao; divination was inauspicious, and those at his side urged him to stop. Elui said: "Our forebears lost their state and relied on Sui to survive; to forget this now is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he plotted to seize Bing Prefecture for Yang Zhengdao. Divination proved inauspicious and his advisers urged caution. Elui said: "Our ancestors lost their kingdom and survived only through Sui's favor. To forget that debt now would be disastrous."

sentences.zh: 卜不吉，神詎無知乎？

translations.literal: If divination is inauspicious, do the spirits truly not know?
translations.idiomatic: If the oracle is unfavorable, do the spirits truly know nothing?

sentences.zh: 我自決之。

translations.literal: I myself will decide.
translations.idiomatic: I shall decide for myself.

sentences.zh: 」會天雨血三日，國中犬夜群號，求之不見，遂有疾，公主餌以五石，俄疽發死。

translations.literal: Then heaven rained blood for three days; dogs in the state howled in packs at night, sought but not seen—he thereupon fell ill; the princess fed him the Five-Stone Powder, and soon carbuncles broke out and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Blood rained from the sky for three days, and dogs howled in packs at night. He fell ill; the princess gave him the Five-Stone Powder, and he soon died of erupting sores.

sentences.zh: 主以子奧射設陋弱，棄不立，更取其弟咄嗣，是為頡利可汗。

translations.literal: The ruler held his son Aqishi she coarse and weak, abandoned him and did not establish him, and instead took his younger brother Tujue—this was Jieli Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming his son Aqishi she unfit, he passed him over and enthroned his younger brother Tujue as Jieli Khan.

sentences.zh: 頡利始為莫賀咄設，牙直五原北。

translations.literal: Jieli was first Moheduo she; his camp was due north of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli had first served as Moheduo she, with his camp directly north of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 薛舉陷平涼，與連和，帝患之，遣光祿卿宇文歆賂頡利，使與舉絕；

translations.literal: Xue Ju took Pingliang and allied with him; the Emperor was troubled, sent Palace Attendant Yuwen Xin to bribe Jieli and make him break with Ju;
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju captured Pingliang and allied with the Turks, the emperor sent Yuwen Xin to bribe Jieli into breaking with Xue Ju;

sentences.zh: 隋五原太守張長遜以所部五城附虜，歆並說還五原地。

translations.literal: Sui's Wuyuan prefect Zhang Changsun submitted his five cities to the barbarians; Xin also persuaded the return of Wuyuan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Sui prefect Zhang Changsun of Wuyuan had submitted five cities to the Turks; Xin also persuaded Jieli to return Wuyuan territory.

sentences.zh: 皆見聽，且發兵舉長遜所部會秦王軍。

translations.literal: All were accepted, and moreover troops were sent to raise Zhang Changsun's command and join the Prince of Qin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli agreed to both proposals and sent troops under Zhang Changsun to join the Prince of Qin's army.

sentences.zh: 太子建成議廢豐州，並割榆中地。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiancheng proposed abolishing Feng Prefecture and also ceding Yuzhong territory.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jiancheng proposed abolishing Feng Prefecture and ceding the Yuzhong region.

sentences.zh: 於是處羅子郁射設以所部萬帳入處河南，以靈州為塞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Elui's son Yugu she led his ten thousand tents to settle south of the river in Henan, with Ling Prefecture as the border.
translations.idiomatic: Elui's son Yugu she then led ten thousand tents to settle south of the desert, with Ling Prefecture as the frontier marker.

sentences.zh: 頡利又妻義成，以始畢子什缽為突利可汗，使居東。

translations.literal: Jieli again married Yicheng and made Shibi's son Shibo Tuli Khan, sending him to dwell in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli married Princess Yicheng and installed Shibi's son Shibo as Tuli Khan in the eastern territories.

sentences.zh: 義成，楊諧女也，其弟善經亦依突厥，與王世充使者王文素共說頡利曰：「往啟民兄弟爭國，賴隋得復位，子孫有國。

translations.literal: Yicheng was the daughter of Yang Xie; her younger brother Shanjing also relied on the Turks, and with Wang Shichong's envoy Wang Wensu together urged Jieli: "Formerly Qimin's brothers contended for the state; relying on Sui they regained their position, and descendants held the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng was the daughter of Yang Xie; her brother Shanjing also lived among the Turks. Together with Wang Shichong's envoy Wang Wensu they urged Jieli: "When Qimin's brothers fought for power, they regained their throne only through Sui's aid, and their descendants ruled thereafter."

sentences.zh: 今天子非文帝後，宜立正道以報隋厚德。

translations.literal: Today's Son of Heaven is not a descendant of Emperor Wen; it is fitting to establish Zhengdao to repay Sui's deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: Today's emperor is no descendant of Emperor Wen of Sui. You should install Yang Zhengdao to repay Sui's great kindness.

sentences.zh: 」頡利然之，故歲入寇。

translations.literal: Jieli approved this, and therefore each year invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli agreed, and henceforth raided the borders every year.

sentences.zh: 然倚父兄餘資，兵銳馬多，謷然驕氣，直出百蠻上，視中國為不足與，書辭悖嫚，多須求。

translations.literal: Yet relying on his father and elder brothers' remaining resources, with sharp troops and many horses, he bore a haughty arrogance, standing straight above the hundred barbarians, viewing China as unworthy to contend with; his letters were perverse and insulting, with many demands.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on his predecessors' accumulated strength, with sharp troops and abundant horses, he grew insufferably arrogant, ranking himself above all other peoples and treating China with contempt. His letters were insolent and full of demands.

sentences.zh: 帝方經略天下，故屈禮，多所舍貸，贈賫不貲，然而不厭無厓之求也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then securing the realm, and therefore bent ritual propriety, granting much and forgiving debts, bestowing gifts beyond measure—yet he was not sated with boundless demands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still consolidating the realm and therefore humbled himself, forgiving debts and lavishing gifts without measure—yet Jieli's demands knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 四年，頡利率萬騎與苑君璋合寇雁門，定襄王李大恩擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jieli led ten thousand horsemen and joined Yuan Junzhang to raid Yanmen; Prince of Dingxiang Li Da'en repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Jieli led ten thousand horsemen with Yuan Junzhang to raid Yanmen. Prince of Dingxiang Li Da'en drove them back.

sentences.zh: 頡利執我使者漢陽公瑰、太常卿鄭元璹、左驍衛大將軍長孫順德，帝亦囚其使與相當。

translations.literal: Jieli seized our envoys Duke of Hanyang Gui, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu, and Left Brave Guards General Zhangsun Shunde; the Emperor also imprisoned their envoys in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli seized the envoys Duke of Hanyang Gui, Zheng Yuanshu, and Zhangsun Shunde. The emperor retaliated by imprisoning Turkish envoys in equal number.

sentences.zh: 由是寇代州，敗行軍總管王孝基，略河東，犯原州，穿延州塞，諸將與戰，不能有所俘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raided Dai Prefecture, defeated Mobile Campaign General Wang Xiaoji, plundered Hedong, invaded Yuan Prefecture, broke through Yan Prefecture's passes—the generals fought but could capture nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided Dai Prefecture, defeated Wang Xiaoji, plundered Hedong, invaded Yuan and Yan prefectures, and fought Tang generals without suffering significant losses.

sentences.zh: 明年，還順德等，且請和，贄魚膠，紿云：「固二國之好也。

translations.literal: The next year he returned Shunde and others and moreover requested peace, presenting fish glue as tribute, deceitfully saying: "To solidify the good relations of the two states."
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned Shunde and the others and sought peace, presenting fish glue as tribute with the claim: "To strengthen friendship between our two states."

sentences.zh: 」帝雖未情，釋其使特勒熱寒等，厚與金還之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, though not in good faith, released their envoys the tegin Rehan and others, generously gave gold and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Though distrustful, the emperor released the tegin Rehan and other envoys and sent them back laden with gold.

sentences.zh: 大恩上言：「突厥饑，馬邑可圖也。

translations.literal: Da'en submitted: "The Turks are hungry; Mayi can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Li Da'en reported: "The Turks are starving. Mayi can be seized."

sentences.zh: 」詔殿中少監獨孤晟共擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Palace Supervisor Dugu Sheng to attack jointly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Palace Supervisor Dugu Sheng to join the attack.

sentences.zh: 晟後約，大恩不敢進，屯新城，頡利自將數萬騎與劉黑闥合圍之，大恩沒，士死者數千人。

translations.literal: Sheng was late to the rendezvous; Da'en dared not advance and encamped at New City. Jieli personally led tens of thousands of horsemen and joined Liu Heita to surround him; Da'en perished, and several thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng arrived late; Li Da'en hesitated to advance and encamped at New City. Jieli personally led tens of thousands of horsemen with Liu Heita to surround him. Li Da'en was killed and thousands of his men perished.

sentences.zh: 進擊忻州，為李高遷所破。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Xin Prefecture, he was defeated by Li Gaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Xin Prefecture but was defeated by Li Gaoqian.

sentences.zh: 黑闥以突厥萬人擾山東，又殘定州。

translations.literal: Heita used ten thousand Turks to harass Shandong and also ravaged Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Heita deployed ten thousand Turkish troops to ravage Shandong and laid waste to Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頡利未得志，乃率十五萬騎入雁門，圍并州，深鈔汾、潞，取男女五千，分數千騎轉掠原、靈間。

translations.literal: Jieli, not having achieved his aim, then led one hundred fifty thousand horsemen into Yanmen, besieged Bing Prefecture, raided deeply in Fen and Lu, took five thousand men and women, and divided several thousand horsemen to turn and plunder between Yuan and Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated, Jieli led one hundred fifty thousand horsemen through Yanmen, besieged Bing Prefecture, raided deeply along the Fen and Lu rivers, seized five thousand captives, and sent thousands of horsemen to plunder Yuan and Ling prefectures.

sentences.zh: 於是太子建成將兵出豳州道，秦王將兵出蒲州道擊之；

translations.literal: Thereupon Crown Prince Jiancheng led troops out by the Binzhou route and the Prince of Qin led troops out by the Puzhou route to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jiancheng marched out by the Binzhou route and the Prince of Qin by the Puzhou route to attack them;

sentences.zh: 李子和以兵趨雲中，掩可汗後；

translations.literal: Li Zihe led troops toward Yunzhong to strike the khan's rear;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zihe advanced toward Yunzhong to strike the khan's rear;

sentences.zh: 段德操出夏州，狙其歸。

translations.literal: Duan Decao came out from Xia Prefecture to ambush their return.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Decao marched from Xia Prefecture to ambush their retreat.

sentences.zh: 并州總管襄邑王神符戰汾東，斬虜五百首，取馬二千；

translations.literal: Bing Prefecture Inspector Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu fought east of the Fen, beheaded five hundred barbarians, and took two thousand horses;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu fought east of the Fen River, killing five hundred Turks and capturing two thousand horses;

sentences.zh: 汾州刺史蕭顗獻俘五千。

translations.literal: Fen Prefecture Inspector Xiao Yi presented five thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Fen Prefecture Inspector Xiao Yi presented five thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 虜陷大震關，縱兵掠弘州，總管宇文歆、靈州楊師道拒之，獲馬、橐它數千。

translations.literal: The barbarians took Dazhen Pass and let troops plunder Hong Prefecture; Inspectors Yuwen Xin and Yang Shidao of Ling Prefecture resisted them and captured several thousand horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks captured Dazhen Pass and raided Hong Prefecture. Yuwen Xin and Yang Shidao of Ling Prefecture repelled them and seized several thousand horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 頡利聞秦王且至，引出塞，王師還。

translations.literal: Jieli heard the Prince of Qin was about to arrive, led his forces out beyond the passes, and the royal army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Prince of Qin was approaching, Jieli withdrew beyond the frontier and the Tang armies returned.

sentences.zh: 又明年，與黑闥、君璋等小小入寇定、匡、原、朔等州，與屯將相勝負。

translations.literal: The next year again, with Heita, Junzhang, and others they made small incursions into Ding, Kuang, Yuan, Shuo, and other prefectures, trading victories with the garrison generals.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jieli joined Heita and Junzhang in minor raids on Ding, Kuang, Yuan, and Shuo prefectures, trading victories with Tang garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 帝遣太子建成復屯北邊、秦王屯并州備虜，久乃罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Crown Prince Jiancheng again to garrison the northern border and the Prince of Qin to garrison Bing Prefecture against the barbarians; only after a long time were they dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stationed Crown Prince Jiancheng on the northern frontier and the Prince of Qin at Bing Prefecture against Turkish raids. They remained there for a long time before being recalled.

sentences.zh: 俄又破代地一屯，進擊渭、豳二州，取馬邑，不有也，復請和，歸我馬邑。

translations.literal: Soon they again broke a camp in Dai territory, advanced to attack Wei and Bin prefectures, took Mayi but could not hold it, again requested peace, and returned Mayi to us.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they destroyed a garrison in Dai territory, attacked Wei and Bin prefectures, briefly seized Mayi but could not hold it, then sued for peace and returned Mayi.

sentences.zh: 七年，攻原、朔二州，入代地，不勝，更與君璋合攻隴州及陰般城，分擊並地，秦王與齊王元吉屯豳州道以備胡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they attacked Yuan and Shuo prefectures, entered Dai territory without victory, then again joined Junzhang to attack Long Prefecture and Yinyan city, divided forces to strike Bing territory; the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi Yuanji garrisoned the Binzhou route to guard against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they attacked Yuan and Shuo, entered Dai territory without success, then joined Junzhang to attack Long Prefecture and Yinyan. The Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi Yuanji garrisoned the Binzhou route against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 君璋與虜出入原、朔、忻、並地，剽繋騷然，數為諸將驅逐。

translations.literal: Junzhang and the barbarians came and went through Yuan, Shuo, Xin, and Bing territories, raiding and binding captives in turmoil, and were repeatedly driven off by the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Junzhang and the Turks raided Yuan, Shuo, Xin, and Bing prefectures, carrying off captives in waves, and were repeatedly driven back by Tang generals.

sentences.zh: 其八月，頡利與突利兵悉起，自原州連營而南，所在震恐，秦王、齊王拒之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Jieli and Tuli raised all their troops, camped in succession south from Yuan Prefecture, and wherever they went terror spread; the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Jieli and Tuli mobilized all their forces, advancing south from Yuan Prefecture in successive camps. Terror spread before them; the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi met them in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，關中霖潦，餉道絕，軍次豳州，可汗萬騎奄至，陣五龍阪，以數百騎挑戰，舉軍失色。

translations.literal: At first Guanzhong suffered floods; supply routes were cut; the army halted at Bin Prefecture when the khan's ten thousand horsemen suddenly arrived, formed battle lines at Wulong Slope, and with several hundred horsemen offered challenge—the whole army lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Floods had cut supply lines in Guanzhong. The army halted at Bin Prefecture when the khan's ten thousand horsemen suddenly appeared at Wulong Slope. Several hundred horsemen rode forward to challenge the Tang lines, and the whole army turned pale.

sentences.zh: 秦王馳百騎掠陣，大言曰：「國家於突厥無負，何為深入？

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin galloped with a hundred horsemen skirting the formation and cried loudly: "The state has done the Turks no wrong—why penetrate so deep?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin galloped forward with a hundred horsemen and shouted: "The empire has done the Turks no wrong. Why do you penetrate so deep into our lands?"

sentences.zh: 我，秦王也，故來自與可汗決，若固戰，我才百騎耳，徒廣殺傷，無益也。

translations.literal: I am the Prince of Qin; I have come to settle matters with the khan myself. If you insist on battle, I have only a hundred horsemen—fighting would only widen the killing to no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: I am the Prince of Qin. I have come to settle this with the khan in person. If you insist on battle, I have only a hundred horsemen—fighting would only multiply the dead to no purpose."

sentences.zh: 」頡利笑不答。

translations.literal: Jieli laughed and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli laughed and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 又馳騎語突利曰：「爾往與我盟，急難相助，今無香火情邪？

translations.literal: He again galloped to speak to Tuli: "You once swore alliance with me to aid each other in urgent need—have you now no bond of sworn brotherhood?"
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to Tuli and said: "You once swore alliance with me to aid each other in need. Have you forgotten our bond of sworn brotherhood?"

sentences.zh: 能一決乎？

translations.literal: Can you settle this in one stroke?
translations.idiomatic: Will you not decide this now?"

sentences.zh: 」突利亦不對。

translations.literal: Tuli also did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli made no reply.

sentences.zh: 王將絕水前，頡利見兵少，又聞與突利語，陰相忌，即遣使者來曰：「王毋苦，我固不戰，將與王議事耳。

translations.literal: As the Prince was about to cross the water forward, Jieli saw few troops and also heard him speak with Tuli—they secretly suspected each other—and immediately sent an envoy saying: "Prince, do not trouble yourself; I truly will not fight; I only wish to discuss affairs with the Prince."
translations.idiomatic: As the prince prepared to ford the river, Jieli saw how few troops he had and overheard his words with Tuli. Suspicious of his brother, Jieli sent an envoy: "Do not trouble yourself, Prince. I do not intend to fight—I wish only to discuss matters with you."

sentences.zh: 」於是引卻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秦王縱反間，突利乃歸心，不欲戰，頡利亦無以強之，乃遣突利及夾畢特勒思摩請和，帝許之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin deployed counter-intelligence; Tuli thereupon gave his heart to him and did not wish to fight; Jieli also had no means to compel him, and therefore sent Tuli and the Jabiy tegin Simo to request peace—the Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sowed discord between the brothers. Tuli turned toward the Tang and refused to fight; Jieli could not compel him. They sent Tuli and the tegin Simo to sue for peace, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 突利遂自托於王為昆弟。

translations.literal: Tuli thereupon entrusted himself to the Prince as sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli pledged himself to the prince as a sworn brother.

sentences.zh: 帝見思摩，引升御榻，思摩頓首辭，帝曰：「我見若猶頡利也。

translations.literal: The Emperor received Simo, led him up to the imperial couch; Simo bowed his head and declined. The Emperor said: "When I see you it is as if I see Jieli."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Simo and seated him on the imperial couch. Simo prostrated himself in refusal. The emperor said: "When I see you, it is as though I see Jieli himself."

sentences.zh: 」乃聽命。

translations.literal: He then accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Simo then accepted.

sentences.zh: 突厥既歲盜邊，或說帝曰：「虜數內寇者，以府庫子女所在，我能去長安，則戎心止矣。

translations.literal: Since the Turks yearly raided the border, someone urged the Emperor: "The barbarians repeatedly invade because the treasury and women are here. If we can leave Chang'an, the Rong heart will stop."
translations.idiomatic: Because the Turks raided annually, someone urged the emperor: "They invade because the treasury and imperial women are at Chang'an. Move the capital and their ambitions will cease."

sentences.zh: 」帝使中書侍郎宇文士及逾南山，按行樊、鄧，將徙都焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Secretariat Vice-Director Yuwen Shiji south over the mountains to survey Fan and Deng, intending to move the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuwen Shiji south of the mountains to survey Fan and Deng as sites for relocating the capital.

sentences.zh: 群臣贊遷，秦王獨曰：「夷狄自古為中國患，未聞周、漢為遷也。

translations.literal: The ministers approved the move; the Prince of Qin alone said: "Barbarians have been China's affliction since antiquity—I have never heard of Zhou or Han moving their capitals for this."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers approved the move. The Prince of Qin alone objected: "Barbarians have troubled China since antiquity, yet Zhou and Han never moved their capitals on their account."

sentences.zh: 願假數年，請取可汗以報。

translations.literal: Grant me a few years; I ask to take the khan in return.
translations.idiomatic: Give me a few years, and I will capture the khan in recompense."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 頡利已和，亦會甚雨，弓矢皆弛惡，遂解而還。

translations.literal: Jieli had already made peace, and moreover encountered heavy rain; bows and arrows all went slack and spoiled, and he disbanded and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli had already made peace, and heavy rain had ruined his bows and arrows. He disbanded his army and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝會群臣問所以備邊者，將作大匠於筠請五原、靈武置舟師於河，扼其入。

translations.literal: The Emperor assembled the ministers to ask how to guard the border; Master of Works Yu Yun requested placing a river fleet at Wuyuan and Lingwu on the river to choke their entry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened his ministers to discuss frontier defense. Master of Works Yu Yun proposed stationing a river fleet at Wuyuan and Lingwu to block Turkish crossings.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎溫彥博曰：「魏為長塹遏匈奴，今可用。

translations.literal: Secretariat Vice-Director Wen Yanbo said: "Wei built the long rampart to hold back the Xiongnu—it can be used now."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo said: "Wei built the long rampart against the Xiongnu. We can do the same now."

sentences.zh: 」帝使桑顯和塹邊大道，召江南船工大發卒治戰艦。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Sang Xianhe trench the frontier highways, summoned shipwrights from south of the Yangtze, and greatly mobilized troops to build warships.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Sang Xianhe to trench the frontier highways, summoned shipwrights from the south, and mobilized troops to build warships.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣使來，願款北樓關請互市，帝不能拒。

translations.literal: Jieli sent envoys requesting to submit at Beilou Pass and seek mutual markets; the Emperor could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli sent envoys requesting trade at Beilou Pass. The emperor could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 帝始兼天下，罷十二軍，尚文治，至是以虜患方張，乃復置之，以練卒搜騎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first united the realm he abolished the Twelve Armies and favored civil governance; now because barbarian trouble was rising he restored them, to drill soldiers and scout cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first united the realm he had abolished the Twelve Armies in favor of civil rule. Now, with the Turkish threat resurgent, he restored them to train soldiers and scout cavalry.

sentences.zh: 八年，頡利攻靈、朔，與代州都督藺謩戰新城，謩敗績。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jieli attacked Ling and Shuo, fought Dai Prefecture Inspector Lin Mo at New City, and Mo was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jieli attacked Ling and Shuo prefectures and defeated Lin Mo at New City.

sentences.zh: 於是張瑾兵屯石嶺，李高遷屯大谷，秦王屯蒲州道。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Jin's troops garrisoned Shiling, Li Gaoqian garrisoned Dagu, and the Prince of Qin garrisoned the Puzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin garrisoned Shiling, Li Gaoqian Dagu, and the Prince of Qin the Puzhou route.

sentences.zh: 初，帝待突厥用敵國禮，及是，怒曰：「往吾以天下未定，厚於虜以紓吾邊。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor treated the Turks with the rites due an equal state; now he angrily said: "Formerly, because the realm was not yet settled, I treated the barbarians generously to ease our borders."
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had treated the Turks as an equal power. Now he declared in anger: "When the realm was unsettled, I treated the Turks generously to ease our borders."

sentences.zh: 今卒敗約，朕將擊滅之，毋須姑息。

translations.literal: Now they have finally broken the covenant; I will strike and destroy them—no need for indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have broken faith. I will destroy them—no more indulgence."

sentences.zh: 」命有司更所與書為詔若敕。

translations.literal: He ordered the offices to change letters sent to them into edicts or commands.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that all correspondence to the Turks be rewritten as imperial edicts or commands.

sentences.zh: 瑾未至屯，虜已逾石嶺，圍并州，攻靈州，轉擾潞、沁。

translations.literal: Before Jin reached his garrison, the barbarians had already crossed Shiling, besieged Bing Prefecture, attacked Ling Prefecture, and turned to harass Lu and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhang Jin reached his post, the Turks had crossed Shiling, besieged Bing Prefecture, attacked Ling, and raided Lu and Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 李靖以兵出潞州道，行軍總管任瑰屯太行。

translations.literal: Li Jing led troops out by the Luzhou route; Mobile Campaign General Ren Gui garrisoned Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing marched by the Luzhou route while Ren Gui garrisoned Taihang.

sentences.zh: 瑾戰大谷，敗績，中書侍郎溫彥博陷於賊，鄆州都督張德政死之。

translations.literal: Jin fought at Dagu and was defeated; Secretariat Vice-Director Wen Yanbo fell into the rebels' hands; Yan Prefecture Inspector Zhang Dezheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin was defeated at Dagu. Wen Yanbo was captured and Zhang Dezheng of Yan Prefecture was killed.

sentences.zh: 遂攻廣武，為任城王道宗破。

translations.literal: They then attacked Guangwu and were defeated by Prince of Rencheng Daozong.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked Guangwu but were defeated by Prince of Rencheng Daozong.

sentences.zh: 其欲谷設掠綏州，請和去。

translations.literal: His Yugu she plundered Sui Prefecture, requested peace, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Yugu she raided Sui Prefecture, then sued for peace and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敗并州數縣，入蘭、鄯、彭州諸屯，或小勝，不能制。

translations.literal: They defeated several counties of Bing Prefecture, entered garrisons of Lan, Shan, and Peng prefectures, sometimes won small victories, but could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: They ravaged several Bing Prefecture counties and raided garrisons in Lan, Shan, and Peng prefectures. Tang forces won minor victories but could not contain them.

sentences.zh: 俄寇原州，折威將軍楊屯擊之，且發士屯大谷。

translations.literal: Soon they raided Yuan Prefecture; General of Broken Might Yang Tun struck them and moreover dispatched troops to garrison Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they raided Yuan Prefecture. Yang Tun repelled them and sent troops to garrison Dagu.

sentences.zh: 九年，攻原、靈，又圍涼州，進犯涇、原，李靖與戰靈州，虜引去。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they attacked Yuan and Ling, again besieged Liang Prefecture, advanced to invade Jing and Yuan; Li Jing fought them at Ling Prefecture and the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year they attacked Yuan and Ling, besieged Liang Prefecture, and advanced on Jing and Yuan. Li Jing fought them at Ling Prefecture and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 寇西會州，圍烏城，翔徉隴、渭間，平道將軍柴紹破之於秦州，斬一特勒、三大將，虜千級。

translations.literal: They raided West Huizhou, besieged Wucheng, and roamed between Long and Wei; General of the Level Road Chai Shao defeated them at Qin Prefecture, beheading one tegin and three great generals and capturing a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Huizhou in the west, besieged Wucheng, and ranged between Long and Wei prefectures. Chai Shao defeated them at Qin Prefecture, killing a tegin, three senior commanders, and a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 大抵虜得志則深入，負則請和，不恥也。

translations.literal: In general when the barbarians had their way they penetrated deep; when defeated they requested peace—and felt no shame.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule the Turks pressed deep when victorious and sued for peace when beaten, without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 其七月，頡利自將十萬騎襲武功，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jieli personally led a hundred thousand horsemen to strike Wugong; the capital was placed under martial law.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jieli led a hundred thousand horsemen against Wugong, and Chang'an went on alert.

sentences.zh: 攻高陵，尉遲敬德與戰涇陽，獲俟斤烏沒啜，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: They attacked Gaoling; Yuchi Jingde fought them at Jingyang, captured the irkin Wumochuo, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Gaoling. Yuchi Jingde met them at Jingyang, captured the irkin Wumochuo, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣謀臣執失思力入朝以覘我，因誇說曰：「二可汗兵百萬，今至矣！

translations.literal: Jieli sent his strategist Zhishi Sili to court to spy on us, and he boastfully said: "The two khans' troops number a million—they have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Jieli sent his strategist Zhishi Sili to court to reconnoiter. He boasted: "The two khans command a million warriors—they are here!"

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「我與可汗嘗面約和，爾則背之。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I once made a face-to-face covenant of peace with the khan, and you have betrayed it."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied: "I once pledged peace with the khan face to face, and you have broken that pledge."

sentences.zh: 且義師之初，爾父子身從我，遺賜玉帛多至不可計，何妄以兵入我都畿，自誇盛強耶？

translations.literal: Moreover at the start of the righteous army your father and you followed me in person; gifts of silk and treasure were bestowed beyond counting—why do you rashly bring troops into our capital region and boast of your strength?
translations.idiomatic: When I first raised my banner, your father and you rode with me. I lavished gifts of silk and treasure on you beyond reckoning. Why do you dare march on the capital and boast of your power?

sentences.zh: 今我當先戮爾矣！

translations.literal: Now I ought to execute you first!
translations.idiomatic: I ought to execute you on the spot!"

sentences.zh: 」思力懼，請命，蕭瑀、封德彜諫帝，不如禮遣之，帝不許，繋於門下省。

translations.literal: Sili was afraid and begged for his life; Xiao Yu and Feng Deyi remonstrated that the Emperor should rather send him away with courtesy—the Emperor did not agree and bound him in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sili was terrified and pleaded for his life. Xiao Yu and Feng Deyi urged the emperor to release him with courtesy; the emperor refused and had him imprisoned at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乃與侍中高士廉、中書令房玄齡、將軍周範等馳六騎出玄武門，幸渭上，與可汗隔水語，且責其負約。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Attendant-in-Ordinary Gao Shilian, Secretariat Director Fang Xuanling, General Zhou Fan, and others he galloped with six riders out the Xuanwu Gate, proceeded to the Wei River, spoke with the khan across the water, and reproached him for breaking the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with Gao Shilian, Fang Xuanling, Zhou Fan, and others, he rode out the Xuanwu Gate with only six horsemen to the Wei River. Across the water he spoke with the khan and rebuked him for breaking faith.

sentences.zh: 群酋見帝，皆驚，下馬拜。

translations.literal: When the chieftains saw the Emperor they were all startled, dismounted, and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkish chiefs were astonished to see the emperor. They dismounted and prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 俄而眾軍至，旗鎧光明，部隊靜嚴，虜大駭。

translations.literal: Soon the mass of armies arrived; banners and armor gleamed; ranks stood silent and stern—the barbarians were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tang armies appeared, banners and armor blazing, ranks motionless and disciplined. The Turks were utterly unnerved.

sentences.zh: 帝與頡利按轡，即麾軍卻而陣焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Jieli held their reins; he immediately commanded the army to withdraw and form battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Jieli held their horses while he signaled his troops to fall back and form ranks.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀以帝輕敵，叩馬諫，帝曰：「我思熟矣，非爾所知也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, deeming the Emperor had underrated the enemy, seized his horse's bridle to remonstrate; the Emperor said: "I have thought this through—it is not for you to know."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the emperor had underestimated the enemy, Xiao Yu grabbed his bridle to protest. The emperor said: "I have weighed this carefully. You would not understand."

sentences.zh: 夫突厥掃地入寇，以我新有內難，謂不能師。

translations.literal: The Turks swept in to raid because we had just had internal troubles and they thought we could not field an army.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks swept south because they thought our recent civil strife left us unable to fight."

sentences.zh: 我若闔城，彼且大掠吾境，故我獨出，示無所畏，又盛兵使知必戰，不意我能沮其始謀。

translations.literal: If I had shut the city they would have plundered our territory on a grand scale; therefore I came out alone to show I feared nothing, and also displayed strong troops so they would know battle was certain—I did not expect I could thwart their initial plan.
translations.idiomatic: Had I shut the gates, they would have ravaged the countryside. I came out alone to show I was unafraid and massed troops to show we would fight. I never expected to break their plan so easily.

sentences.zh: 彼入吾地既深，懼不能返，故與戰則克，和則固，制賊之命，在此舉矣！

translations.literal: They had entered our land so deep that they feared they could not return; therefore if we fought we would conquer, if we made peace it would hold—the enemy's fate was decided in this move!
translations.idiomatic: They had penetrated too deep to retreat safely. Fight and we would win; make peace and it would hold. The enemy's fate turned on this single gesture."

sentences.zh: 」是日，頡利果請和，許之。

translations.literal: That day Jieli indeed requested peace, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That day Jieli sued for peace, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，刑白馬，與頡利盟便橋上，突厥引還。

translations.literal: The next day a white horse was sacrificed; he allied with Jieli on Bian Bridge, and the Turks withdrew.
