translations.idiomatic: The next day they sacrificed a white horse and sealed the alliance with Jieli on Bian Bridge. The Turks withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀曰：「頡利之來，諸將多請與戰，陛下不聽，既而虜自退，其策奈何？

translations.literal: Xiao Yu said: "When Jieli came many generals asked to fight, but Your Majesty would not listen; afterward the barbarians withdrew on their own—what was the strategy?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu asked: "When Jieli came, many generals urged battle, but Your Majesty refused. The Turks withdrew on their own—what was your strategy?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「突厥眾而不整，君臣惟利是視，可汗在水西，而酋帥皆來謁我，我醉而縛之，其勢易甚。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Turks were numerous but not disciplined; ruler and subjects looked only to profit. The khan was west of the river while the chieftains all came to pay court to me—if I got them drunk and bound them, the thing would be very easy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The Turks were numerous but disordered; ruler and subjects cared only for gain. The khan sat west of the river while his chiefs came to pay me homage. Had I gotten them drunk and bound them, it would have been easy."

sentences.zh: 又我敕長孫無忌、李靖潛師幽州以須，若大軍躡其後，伏邀諸前，取之反覆掌耳。

translations.literal: Moreover I ordered Zhangsun Wuji and Li Jing to move troops secretly to Youzhou to wait; if the main army followed their rear and ambushes blocked them in front, taking them would be like turning one's hand.
translations.idiomatic: I had also ordered Zhangsun Wuji and Li Jing to move secretly toward Youzhou. With our main force on their heels and ambushes ahead, capturing them would have been as easy as turning one's hand.

sentences.zh: 然我新即位，為國者要在安靜，一與虜校，殺傷必多，彼敗未及亡，懼而脩德，與我為怨，其可當耶？

translations.literal: Yet I had just ascended the throne; for governing a state the key is tranquility. Once we matched forces with the barbarians casualties would surely be heavy; though defeated they would not yet perish, and fearing this they would cultivate virtue and bear enmity toward us—could we withstand that?
translations.idiomatic: But I had just taken the throne, and a state needs peace above all. Battle would mean heavy losses. Defeated but not destroyed, they would reform and become our lasting enemy. Could we afford that?

sentences.zh: 今僕械卷鎧，啖以玉帛，虜志必驕，驕則亡之端也，故曰『將欲取之，必固與之』。

translations.literal: Now I have laid aside weapons and rolled up armor and fed them with silk and treasure; the barbarians' will must grow arrogant, and arrogance is the beginning of ruin—thus it is said, 'If you wish to take something, first be sure to give to it.'
translations.idiomatic: Now I have sheathed our swords and showered them with silk and treasure. They will grow arrogant, and arrogance is the road to ruin—as the saying goes, 'To take, one must first give abundantly.'"

sentences.zh: 瑀再拜曰：「非臣愚所逮也！

translations.literal: Yu bowed twice and said: "This is beyond my dull understanding!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu bowed deeply. "This is beyond my understanding!"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔殿中監豆盧寬、將軍趙綽護送突厥，頡利獻馬三千匹、羊萬頭，帝不納，詔歸所俘於我。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Palace Supervisor Dou Lu Kuan and General Zhao Chuo to escort the Turks; Jieli presented three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep—the Emperor did not accept them and decreed the return of captives taken from us.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Dou Lu Kuan and Zhao Chuo to escort the Turks home. Jieli offered three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep, but the emperor refused them and ordered the return of Tang captives.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，薛延陀、回紇、拔野古諸部皆叛，使突利討之，不勝，輕騎走，頡利怒，囚之，突利由是怨望。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan the Xueyantuo, Uyghur, Bayegu, and other divisions all rebelled; he sent Tuli to suppress them; Tuli did not prevail and fled with light cavalry; Jieli was angry and imprisoned him—Tuli therefore nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 the Xueyantuo, Uyghurs, Bayegu, and other tribes rebelled. Jieli sent Tuli against them; Tuli was defeated and fled with a small escort. Jieli imprisoned him, and Tuli turned resentful.

sentences.zh: 是歲大雪，羊馬多凍死，人饑，懼王師乘其敝，即引兵入朔州地，聲言會獵。

translations.literal: That year heavy snow fell; many sheep and horses froze to death and the people went hungry; fearing imperial troops would exploit their weakness, they immediately led troops into Shuo Prefecture territory, claiming they had come to hunt together.
translations.idiomatic: That year heavy snow killed countless sheep and horses and brought famine. Fearing Tang armies would strike while they were weak, the Turks entered Shuo Prefecture under the pretense of a hunting expedition.

sentences.zh: 議者請責其敗約，因伐之，帝曰：「匹夫不可為不信，況國乎？

translations.literal: Counselors asked to hold them accountable for breaking the covenant and attack them; the Emperor said: "A common man must not be untrustworthy—how much more a state?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged punishing them for breaking the treaty and launching an attack. The emperor said: "Even a common man must keep his word—how much more a state?"

sentences.zh: 我既與之盟，豈利其災，邀險以取之耶？

translations.literal: Since I have already allied with them, how could I profit from their disaster and seize them by exploiting their peril?
translations.idiomatic: I have sworn alliance with them. How could I exploit their disaster and ambush them in distress?"

sentences.zh: 須其無禮於我，乃伐之。

translations.literal: We must wait until they are discourteous toward us, then attack.
translations.idiomatic: We will strike only when they give us cause."

sentences.zh: 明年，突利自陳為頡利所攻，求救。

translations.literal: The next year Tuli reported himself attacked by Jieli and requested rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tuli reported that Jieli was attacking him and begged for aid.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕與頡利盟，又與突利有昆弟約，不可不救，奈何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am allied with Jieli and also have a sworn-brother bond with Tuli—I cannot fail to rescue him; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I am allied with Jieli, yet I am sworn brothers with Tuli. I cannot refuse to help him. What should we do?"

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書杜如晦曰：「夷狄無信，我雖如約，彼常負之，今亂而擊之，侮亡之道也。

translations.literal: Minister of War Du Ruhui said: "The Yi and Di are faithless; though we keep our covenants they often betray them. Now to strike them while they are in disorder is the way to insult the dying."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Du Ruhui said: "Barbarians are faithless. Though we keep our word, they break theirs. To strike them now while they are in turmoil is to kick a man when he is down."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔將軍周範壁太原經略之，頡利亦擁兵窺邊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered General Zhou Fan to fortify Taiyuan and conduct operations; Jieli also massed troops to watch the border.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhou Fan to fortify Taiyuan and prepare for action. Jieli also massed troops along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 或請築古長城，發民乘塞。

translations.literal: Some asked to rebuild the old Long Wall and mobilize the people to man the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged rebuilding the old Great Wall and drafting peasants to garrison the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「突厥盛夏而霜，五日並出，三月連明，赤氣滿野，彼見災而不務德，不畏天也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Turks had frost in midsummer, five suns appeared together, three months ran continuously bright, and red vapor filled the wilds—they saw calamities yet did not cultivate virtue; they do not fear Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Turks had frost in midsummer, five suns rose together, three months of unbroken daylight, and red mists covered the steppe. They saw these omens yet did not mend their ways—they do not fear Heaven."

sentences.zh: 遷徙無常，六畜多死，不用地也。

translations.literal: They wander without fixed abode; the six kinds of livestock mostly die—they do not use the land.
translations.idiomatic: They wander without settling; their herds die in droves—they do not know how to use the land."

sentences.zh: 俗死則焚，今葬皆起墓，背父祖命，謾鬼神也。

translations.literal: By custom the dead are burned; now they all raise tombs for burial, going against fathers' and ancestors' commands—this deceives the ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Their custom is to burn the dead, yet now they build tombs—defying their fathers and ancestors and deceiving the spirits."

sentences.zh: 與突利不睦，內相攻殘，不和於親也。

translations.literal: They are not harmonious with Tuli and attack each other internally—there is no harmony among kin.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli and Tuli are at odds, tearing each other apart—there is no harmony among kin."

sentences.zh: 有是四者，將亡矣，當為公等取之，安在築障塞乎？

translations.literal: With these four things they are about to perish; I ought to take them for you—why build barriers and passes?
translations.idiomatic: With these four failings they are doomed to fall. We should conquer them for ourselves—why bother building walls?"

sentences.zh: 」突厥俗素質略，頡利得華士趙德言，才其人，委信之，稍專國；

translations.literal: Turkish custom was plain and rough; Jieli obtained the Chinese scholar Zhao Deyan, valued his talent, entrusted him, and gradually monopolized state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were plain and rough by nature. Jieli took the Chinese adviser Zhao Deyan into his trust and gradually concentrated power in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 又委政諸胡，斥遠宗族不用，興師歲入邊，下不堪苦。

translations.literal: he also entrusted government to various Hu, pushed away and did not employ his clansmen, and raised armies yearly to enter the border—the subordinates could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted government to foreign advisers, pushed aside his own clansmen, and launched annual raids. His people could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 胡性冒沓，數翻覆不信，號令無常。

translations.literal: The Hu nature is rash and grasping; they repeatedly reversed themselves and were faithless; orders had no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign advisers were reckless and greedy, shifting loyalties constantly. Orders changed without warning.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，裒斂苛重，諸部愈貳。

translations.literal: That year famine was severe; exactions were harsh and heavy; the various divisions grew ever more disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck that year, and exactions grew harsh. The tribes grew ever more restive.

sentences.zh: 又明年，屬部薛延陀自稱可汗，以使來。

translations.literal: Again the next year a subordinate division, the Xueyantuo, proclaimed its own khan and sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Xueyantuo, a subordinate tribe, proclaimed their own khan and sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 詔兵部尚書李靖擊虜馬邑，頡利走，九俟斤以眾降，拔野古、仆骨、同羅諸部、習奚渠長皆來朝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of War Li Jing to strike the barbarians at Mayi; Jieli fled; the nine irkin submitted with their hosts; the Bayegu, Pugu, Tongluo divisions and Xi chieftains all came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Jing to attack the Turks at Mayi. Jieli fled. Nine irkin submitted with their followers, and the Bayegu, Pugu, Tongluo, and Xi chiefs all came to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 於是詔并州都督李世勣出通漠道，李靖出定襄道，左武衛大將軍柴紹出金河道，靈州大都督任城王道宗出大同道，幽州都督衛孝節出恒安道，營州都督薛萬淑出暢武道，凡六總管，師十餘萬，皆授靖節度以討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon edicts ordered Bingzhou Inspector Li Shiji out by the Tongmo route, Li Jing out by the Dingxiang route, Left Martial Guard General Chai Shao out by the Jinhe route, Lingzhou Grand Protector Prince of Rencheng Daozong out by the Datong route, Youzhou Inspector Wei Xiaojie out by the Heng'an route, and Yingzhou Inspector Xue Wanshu out by the Changwu route—in all six supreme commanders with more than a hundred thousand troops, all placed under Li Jing's command to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched six commanders with more than a hundred thousand men under Li Jing's overall command: Li Shiji by the Tongmo route, Li Jing by Dingxiang, Chai Shao by Jinhe, Prince Daozong by Datong, Wei Xiaojie by Heng'an, and Xue Wanshu by Changwu.

sentences.zh: 道宗戰靈州，俘人畜萬計，突利及郁射設、蔭奈特勒帥所部來奔，捷書日夜至，帝謂群臣曰：「往國家初定，太上皇以百姓故，奉突厥，詭而臣之，朕常痛心病首，思一刷恥於天下，今天誘諸將，所向輒克，朕其遂有成功乎！

translations.literal: Daozong fought at Ling Prefecture, capturing people and livestock by the tens of thousands; Tuli and the shes Yushe and Yinnai tegin led their divisions to flee and submit; victory reports arrived day and night; the Emperor told the ministers: "When the state was first settled the retired Emperor, for the people's sake, submitted to the Turks and feigned vassalage—I have always ached at this in my heart and head, thinking to wash away the shame under Heaven once; now Heaven guides the generals and wherever they go they conquer—shall I at last succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Daozong fought at Ling Prefecture and captured tens of thousands of people and livestock. Tuli and the shes Yushe and Yinnai tegin defected with their followers. Victory reports poured in day and night. The emperor told his ministers: "When the dynasty was young, the retired emperor submitted to the Turks for the people's sake—a humiliation that has gnawed at me ever since. Now Heaven favors our generals and every campaign succeeds. At last we may redeem our honor!"

sentences.zh: 四年正月，靖進屯惡陽嶺，夜襲頡利，頡利驚，退牙磧口，大酋康蘇蜜等以隋蕭皇后、楊正道降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Jing advanced and encamped at Eyang Ridge, raided Jieli by night; Jieli was startled and withdrew his camp to Qikou; the great chieftain Kang Sumi and others surrendered with Sui Empress Xiao and Yang Zhengdao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Li Jing encamped at Eyang Ridge and attacked Jieli by night. Jieli fled to Qikou. The chieftain Kang Sumi surrendered with Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao.

sentences.zh: 或言中國人嘗密通書於後，中書舍人陽文瓘請劾治。

translations.literal: Some said Chinese had secretly sent letters to the empress; Secretariat Draftsman Yang Wenguan asked to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed Chinese subjects had secretly corresponded with the empress. Yang Wenguan urged an investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下未一，人或當思隋，今反側既安，何足治耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The realm was not yet unified; people might still think of Sui; now the restless are already settled—what need to investigate?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The realm was not yet united; some still looked back to Sui. Now the disloyal are pacified—why pursue this?"

sentences.zh: 」置勿劾。

translations.literal: He set the matter aside and did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 頡利窘，走保鐵山，兵猶數萬，令執失思力來，陽為哀言謝罪，請內屬，帝詔鴻臚卿唐儉、將軍安脩仁等持節慰撫。

translations.literal: Jieli was hard pressed, fled to hold Tieshan, and still had tens of thousands of troops; he sent Zhishi Sili with feigned words of grief to apologize and request to submit internally; the Emperor ordered Chief Minister of Guests Tang Jian, General An Xiuren, and others to go bearing credentials to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Jieli fled to Tieshan with tens of thousands of men. He sent Zhishi Sili with feigned remorse to sue for submission. The emperor dispatched Tang Jian and An Xiuren with credentials to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 靖知儉在虜所，虜必安，乃襲擊之，盡獲其眾，頡利得千里馬，獨奔沙缽羅，行軍副總管張寶相禽之。

translations.literal: Jing knew that with Jian among the barbarians they would surely feel secure, and therefore raided them, capturing their entire host; Jieli obtained a thousand-li horse and fled alone to Shabolu; Mobile Campaign Deputy Commander Zhang Baoxiang seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing knew the Turks would relax while Tang Jian was negotiating. He attacked and captured the entire force. Jieli escaped on a swift horse toward Shabolu, but Zhang Baoxiang captured him.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅設、蘇尼失以眾降，其國遂亡，復定襄、恒安地，斥境至大漠矣。

translations.literal: The she Shabolu and Sunishi submitted with their hosts; their state then perished; Dingxiang and Heng'an territories were recovered and the frontier was pushed to the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: The shes Shabolu and Sunishi submitted with their followers. The Turkish state was destroyed. Tang recovered Dingxiang and Heng'an, and the frontier reached the great desert.

sentences.zh: 頡利至京師，告俘太廟，帝御順天樓，陳仗衛，士民縱觀，吏執可汗至，帝曰：「而罪有五：而父國破，賴隋以安，不以一鏃力助之，使其廟社不血食，一也；

translations.literal: Jieli arrived at the capital; captives were announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Emperor ascended Shuntian Tower, arrayed guards and armor, and commoners were allowed to watch; officials led the khan forward; the Emperor said: "Your crimes are five: your father's state was broken and relied on Sui for safety—you did not lend the force of a single arrowhead to help, causing their ancestral temples to go without blood offerings—first;
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was brought to the capital and presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple. The emperor mounted Shuntian Tower with full guard while the people looked on. Officials led the khan forward. The emperor said: "You are guilty of five crimes. First: when your father's state was broken, Sui restored you, yet you never lifted a finger to aid them, leaving Sui's ancestral temples without sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 與我鄰而棄信擾邊，二也；

translations.literal: bordering us yet abandoning faith and harassing the frontier—second;
translations.idiomatic: Second: though we were neighbors, you broke faith and raided our borders."

sentences.zh: 恃兵不戢，部落攜怨，三也；

translations.literal: relying on troops and not restraining them, tribes bore resentment—third;
translations.idiomatic: Third: you relied on force and would not restrain your troops, earning your tribes' hatred."

sentences.zh: 賊華民，暴禾稼，四也；

translations.literal: plundering Chinese people and ravaging grain crops—fourth;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: you preyed on Chinese subjects and destroyed our harvests."

sentences.zh: 許和親而遷延自遁，五也。

translations.literal: promising marriage alliance yet delaying and slipping away on your own—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: you promised alliance by marriage, then delayed and slipped away."

sentences.zh: 朕殺爾非無名，顧渭上盟未之忘，故不窮責也。

translations.literal: If I kill you it is not without cause, but remembering the covenant on the Wei I have not forgotten, therefore I do not press the charge to the end.
translations.idiomatic: I would be justified in executing you, but I have not forgotten our covenant on the Wei River, and so I will not press the matter further."

sentences.zh: 」乃悉還其家屬，館於太僕，稟食之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned all his family members, lodged them with the Imperial Stud, and supplied their food.
translations.idiomatic: He returned Jieli's family, housed them under the Imperial Stud, and provided for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 思結俟斤以四萬眾降，可汗弟欲谷設奔高昌，既而亦來降。

translations.literal: The Sijie irkin submitted with forty thousand followers; the khan's younger brother Yugu she fled to Gaochang and afterward also came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Sijie irkin submitted with forty thousand followers. Jieli's brother Yugu she fled to Gaochang but later surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 伊吾城之長素臣突厥，舉七城以獻，因其地為西伊州。

translations.literal: The chief of Yiwu city had long submitted to the Turks; he offered seven cities in surrender, and on that territory Western Yizhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Yiwu, long a Turkish vassal, surrendered seven cities. Tang established Western Yizhou on that territory.

sentences.zh: 制詔：突厥往逢癘疫，長城之南，暴骨如丘，有司其以酒脯祭，為瘞藏之。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed: "The Turks formerly encountered pestilence; south of the Long Wall exposed bones lay like hills—the responsible offices shall offer wine and dried meat in sacrifice and bury them properly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "During past epidemics Turkish dead lay unburied south of the Great Wall, bones heaped like hills. Let the authorities offer wine and meat in sacrifice and give them proper burial."

sentences.zh: 又詔：隋亂，華民多沒於虜，遣使者以金帛贖男女八萬口，還為平民。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "In Sui's disorders many Chinese were lost to the barbarians—send envoys to redeem eighty thousand men and women with gold and silk and restore them as common people."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "During the Sui collapse countless Chinese were taken captive. Send envoys to redeem eighty thousand men and women with gold and silk and restore them to civilian life."

sentences.zh: 頡利不室處，常設穹廬廷中，久郁郁不自憀，與家人悲歌相泣下，狀貌羸省。

translations.literal: Jieli would not dwell indoors; he always pitched a felt tent in the courtyard; for long he was depressed and ill at ease, singing mournfully with his family and weeping together; his appearance grew gaunt and wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli refused to live indoors and kept a yurt pitched in the courtyard. He grew despondent, singing mournfully with his family and weeping together until he was gaunt and wasted.

sentences.zh: 帝見憐之，以虢州負山多麕麋，有射獵之娛，乃拜為刺史，辭不往，遂授右衛大將軍，賜美田宅。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him with pity; because Guo Prefecture backed mountains rich in roe deer and had the pleasure of hunting, he appointed him inspector—but he declined to go; thereupon he was made Right Guard General and granted fine fields and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him. Guo Prefecture, mountainous and rich in game, would have suited his love of the hunt, and the emperor offered him the post of inspector. Jieli declined, so he was made Right Guard General and given a fine estate.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔啟民失國，隋文帝不恡粟帛，興士眾，營護而存立之，至始畢稍強，則以兵圍煬帝雁門，今其滅者，殆背德忘義致然耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Formerly when Qimin lost his state, Emperor Wen of Sui did not stint grain and silk, raised soldiers and people, sheltered and preserved him—yet when Shibi grew somewhat strong he besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen with troops; now that they are destroyed, is it perhaps because they turned their backs on virtue and forgot righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked: "When Qimin lost his kingdom, Emperor Wen of Sui spent grain and treasure and sent armies to restore him. Yet when Shibi grew strong he besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen. Perhaps their destruction came from betraying those who had saved them."

sentences.zh: 」頡利子疊羅支，有至性，既舍京師，諸婦得品供，羅支預焉；

translations.literal: Jieli's son Dieluozhi had utmost filial nature; after leaving the capital the various wives received ranked provisions, and Luozhi was included;
translations.idiomatic: Jieli's son Dieluozhi was deeply filial. After leaving the capital, the wives received ranked rations, and Luozhi was among them.

sentences.zh: 其母最後至，不得給，羅支不敢嘗品肉。

translations.literal: his mother arrived last and received no allotment; Luozhi dared not taste the ranked meat.
translations.idiomatic: His mother arrived last and received no share. Luozhi would not touch his ration until she was served.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，嘆曰：「天稟仁孝，詎限華夷哉！

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard he sighed and said: "Heaven-bestowed benevolence and filial piety—how could it be limited to Chinese and barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he sighed: "Heaven bestows filial piety without regard for Chinese or barbarian!"

sentences.zh: 」厚賜之，遂給母肉。

translations.literal: He richly rewarded him and then provided meat for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Luozhi generously and saw that his mother received her share.

sentences.zh: 八年，頡利死，贈歸義王，謚曰荒，詔國人葬之，從其禮，火屍，起冢灞東。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jieli died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Returning Righteousness with posthumous title Disordered; an edict ordered countrymen to bury him according to their rites—burning the corpse and raising a tomb east of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jieli died. He was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Returning Righteousness with the temple name Disordered. By edict his countrymen buried him in their custom: the body was burned and a tomb raised east of Ba.

sentences.zh: 其臣胡祿達官吐谷渾邪者，頡利母婆施之媵臣也，頡利始生，以授渾邪，至是哀慟，乃自殺。

translations.literal: His minister the Hu official Tuyuhun Xie was a attendant-concubine's servant of Jieli's mother Boshi; when Jieli was first born he was entrusted to Hunye—now he grieved and mourned and therefore killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: His minister Tuyuhun Xie, a retainer of Jieli's mother Boshi, had nursed Jieli from birth. Grief-stricken, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，贈中郎將，命葬頡利冢旁，詔中書侍郎岑文本刻其事於頡利、渾邪之墓碑。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at this, posthumously awarded him Gentleman of the Palace Guard, ordered burial beside Jieli's tomb, and decreed Secretariat Vice-Director Cen Wenben inscribe the affair on the tomb stele of Jieli and Hunye.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved, posthumously made him a Gentleman of the Palace Guard, and ordered him buried beside Jieli's tomb. Cen Wenben was commanded to inscribe the story on their stele.

sentences.zh: 俄蘇尼失亦以死殉。

translations.literal: Soon Sunishi also died in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sunishi also died in loyalty to his lord.

sentences.zh: 尼失者，啟民可汗弟也。

translations.literal: Sunishi was the younger brother of Khan Qimin.
translations.idiomatic: Sunishi was the younger brother of Qimin Khan.

sentences.zh: 始畢以為沙缽羅設，帳部五萬，牙直靈州西北，姿雄趫，以仁惠御下，人多歸之；

translations.literal: Shibi made him she Shabolu; his camp division numbered fifty thousand; his headquarters stood northwest of Ling Prefecture; his bearing was bold and swift; he governed subordinates with benevolence and grace, and many people rallied to him;
translations.idiomatic: Shibi had made him she Shabolu over fifty thousand tents, headquartered northwest of Ling Prefecture. Bold and swift, he ruled with kindness, and many rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 頡利政亂，其部獨不貳。

translations.literal: when Jieli's government fell into disorder his division alone did not waver in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli's rule collapsed, his tribe alone remained loyal.

sentences.zh: 突利降，頡利以為小可汗。

translations.literal: When Tuli submitted Jieli made him lesser khan.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuli defected, Jieli made him lesser khan.

sentences.zh: 頡利已敗，乃舉眾來，漠南地遂空，授北寧州都督、右衛大將軍，封懷德王云。

translations.literal: After Jieli was defeated he then led all his people to come; the lands south of the desert were thus emptied; he was appointed Grand Protector of North Ningzhou and Right Guard General, enfeoffed as King of Cherishing Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat he brought his entire following to Tang. The steppe south of the desert lay empty. He was made Grand Protector of North Ningzhou and Right Guard General, enfeoffed as King of Cherishing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 頡利之亡，其下或走薛延陀，或入西域，而來降者尚十餘萬，詔議所宜，鹹言：「突厥擾中國久，今天喪之，非慕義自歸，請悉籍降俘，內兗、豫閑處，使習耕織，百萬之虜，可化為齊人，是中國有加戶，而漠北遂空也。

translations.literal: When Jieli perished his subordinates either fled to the Xueyantuo or entered the Western Regions, yet those who came to submit still numbered more than a hundred thousand; an edict sought counsel on what was fitting—all said: "The Turks have troubled China long; now Heaven has ended them—they have not returned from admiration of righteousness; please register all surrendered captives and settle them within Yan and Yu in vacant places, have them learn plowing and weaving—a million barbarians can be transformed into Qi people; China would gain households and the north of the desert would be emptied."
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's fall his followers fled to the Xueyantuo or westward, yet more than a hundred thousand surrendered. The court debated their disposition. Many argued: "The Turks have plagued China for generations. They surrender from weakness, not loyalty. Register them all and settle them in vacant lands in Yan and Yu, teach them farming and weaving—a million barbarians could become ordinary subjects, China would gain population, and the northern steppe would lie empty."

sentences.zh: 」中書令溫彥博請：「如漢建武時，置降匈奴留五原塞，全其部落，以為捍蔽，不革其俗，因而撫之，實空虛之地，且示無所猜。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Wen Yanbo requested: "As in Han's Jianwu era, when surrendered Xiongnu were settled to remain at Wuyuan Pass, preserving their tribes as a shield and barrier, not changing their customs but soothing them thereby—this would truly fill empty lands and also show we suspect nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Wen Yanbo argued: "As Emperor Guangwu of Han settled surrendered Xiongnu at Wuyuan Pass, keeping their tribes intact as a buffer without changing their customs—we would fill empty lands and show we do not distrust them."

sentences.zh: 若內兗、豫，則乖本性，非函育之道。

translations.literal: If settled within Yan and Yu it would go against their native nature—not the way of nurturing and sheltering.
translations.idiomatic: Settling them deep in Yan and Yu would violate their nature—it is not the way of humane governance."

sentences.zh: 」秘書監魏征建言：「突厥世為中國仇，今其來降，不即誅滅，當遣還河北。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Wei Zheng offered counsel: "The Turks have for generations been China's enemies; now that they come to submit, if we do not immediately exterminate them we should send them back north of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Wei Zheng objected: "The Turks have been China's enemies for generations. Now that they surrender, if we do not destroy them outright we should at least send them back north of the Yellow River."

sentences.zh: 彼鳥獸野心，非我族類，弱則伏，強則叛，其天性也。

translations.literal: Their hearts are those of birds and beasts; they are not our kind—when weak they submit, when strong they rebel; such is their inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: They have the hearts of wolves. They are not our kind. Weak, they submit; strong, they rebel—that is their nature."

sentences.zh: 且秦、漢以銳師猛將擊取河南地為郡縣者，以不欲使近中國也。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin and Han used sharp troops and fierce generals to seize Henan territory and make it commanderies and counties precisely because they did not wish them near China.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han conquered the lands south of the desert and made them commanderies precisely to keep barbarians away from the heartland."

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何以河南居之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, how can you settle them in Henan?
translations.idiomatic: Why would Your Majesty settle them in Henan?"

sentences.zh: 且降者十萬，若令數年，孳息略倍，而近在畿甸，心腹疾也。

translations.literal: Moreover the submitters number a hundred thousand; if allowed several years to breed their numbers would roughly double—and placed close to the capital region this would be a disease of the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand have surrendered. In a few years their numbers could double. Placed near the capital, they would become a disease in our very vitals."

sentences.zh: 」彥博曰：「不然，天子於四夷，若天地養萬物，覆載全安之，今突厥破滅，余種歸命，不加哀憐而棄之，非天地蒙覆之義，而有阻四夷之嫌。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Not so—the Son of Heaven toward the four barbarians is like Heaven and Earth nourishing the ten thousand things, covering and carrying them to complete their safety; now the Turks are broken and destroyed and the remnant seed submits—if we do not show pity and compassion but abandon them, this is not the meaning of Heaven and Earth's sheltering cover and would arouse suspicion among the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo replied: "Not so. The Son of Heaven treats the four barbarians as Heaven and Earth nurture all things—with shelter and care. The Turks are broken; their remnants submit. To abandon them without compassion violates the way of Heaven and will alienate all foreign peoples."

sentences.zh: 臣謂處以河南，蓋死而生之，亡而存之，彼世將懷德，何叛之為？

translations.literal: Your servant holds that settling them in Henan is precisely giving life to the dead and preserving the perished—they for generations will cherish virtue; why would they rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Settling them in Henan means giving life to the dying and saving the lost. Grateful for generations, why would they rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「魏時有胡落分處近郡，晉已平吳，郭欽、江統勸武帝逐出之，不能用。

translations.literal: Zheng said: "In Wei times Hu tribes were distributed among nearby commanderies; after Jin had pacified Wu, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them out—he could not use the advice."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng countered: "In Wei times barbarian tribes were settled in nearby commanderies. After Jin conquered Wu, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to expel them—but he did not listen."

sentences.zh: 劉、石之亂，卒傾中夏。

translations.literal: The disorders of the Liu and Shi clans ultimately overturned central China.
translations.idiomatic: The uprisings of Liu Yuan and Shi Le ultimately overturned the heartland."

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲引突厥居河南，所謂養虎自遺患者也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty insists on bringing the Turks to dwell in Henan, this is what is called rearing a tiger and bequeathing future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on settling Turks in Henan, you will be rearing a tiger to plague your descendants."

sentences.zh: 」彥博曰：「聖人之道無不通，故曰『有教無類』。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "The way of the sage has nothing it cannot penetrate—thus it is said, 'In teaching there are no classes.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo replied: "The sage's way embraces all—'In education there are no distinctions of kind.'"

sentences.zh: 彼創殘之餘，以窮歸我，我援護之，收處內地，將教以禮法，職以耕農，又選酋良入宿衛，何患之恤？

translations.literal: They are the remnant after wounds and ruin, coming to us in extremity—we aid and protect them, gather and settle them within the interior, will teach them rites and law, assign them farming duties, and also select worthy chiefs to enter palace guard service—what worry need we spare?
translations.idiomatic: They come to us broken and destitute. We shelter them, settle them inland, teach them rites and law, set them to farming, and select worthy chiefs for palace guard—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 且光武置南單于，卒無叛亡。

translations.literal: Moreover when Emperor Guangwu established the Southern Chanyu, in the end none rebelled or fled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Emperor Guangwu established the Southern Chanyu, none ultimately rebelled or fled."

sentences.zh: 」於是中書侍郎顏師古、給事中杜楚客、禮部侍郎李百藥等皆勸帝不如使處河北，樹首長，俾統部落，視地多少，令不相臣，國小權分，終不得亢衡中國，長轡遠馭之道也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Secretariat Vice-Director Yan Shigu, Attendant-in-Ordinary Du Chuke, Vice-Minister of Rites Li Baiyao, and others all urged the Emperor that it would be better to settle them north of the river, establish chieftains, have them govern tribes, apportion lands by size, make them not subject to one another, keep states small and power divided—they would never be able to stand equal to China; this was the way of long reins and distant control.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Vice-Director Yan Shigu, Du Chuke, Li Baiyao, and others urged settling the Turks north of the Yellow River instead. Install chieftains to govern their tribes, divide their lands, and keep them from uniting under one ruler. Small states with divided power could never challenge China—this was the way of governing from afar with loose reins.

sentences.zh: 帝主彥博語，卒度朔方地，自幽州屬靈州，建順、祐、化、長四州為都督府，剖頡利故地，左置定襄都督、右置雲中都督二府統之。

translations.literal: The Emperor upheld Yanbo's view; he finally measured out Shuofang territory from Youzhou to Ling Prefecture, established the four prefectures Shun, You, Hua, and Chang as a grand protectorate office, divided Jieli's former lands, and placed Dingxiang Protectorate on the left and Yunzhong Protectorate on the right to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Wen Yanbo. He mapped out Shuofang territory from Youzhou to Ling Prefecture, established the four prefectures Shun, You, Hua, and Chang under a grand protectorate, and divided Jieli's former lands between the Dingxiang and Yunzhong protectorates.

sentences.zh: 擢酋豪為將軍、郎將者五百人，奉朝請者且百員，入長安自籍者數千戶。

translations.literal: Five hundred tribal chiefs were promoted to generals and commandants; nearly a hundred received court attendance appointments; several thousand households registered themselves in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred tribal leaders were made generals and commandants, nearly a hundred received court attendance appointments, and several thousand households registered in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 乃以突利可汗為順州都督，令率其下就部。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tuli Khan was made Grand Protector of Shun Prefecture and ordered to lead his followers to their assigned territory.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli Khan was appointed Grand Protector of Shun Prefecture and ordered to lead his people to their assigned lands.

sentences.zh: 突利初為泥步設，得隋淮南公主以為妻。

translations.literal: Tuli was first made she Nibu and obtained Princess Huainan of Sui as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli was first made she Nibu and married Princess Huainan of Sui.

sentences.zh: 頡利之立，用次弟為延陀設，主延陀部，步利設主霫部，統特勒主胡部，斛特勒主斛薛部，以突利可汗主契丹、靺鞨部，樹牙南直幽州，東方之眾皆屬焉。

translations.literal: When Jieli was established he used his next younger brother as she Xueyantuo to govern the Xueyantuo division, she Buli to govern the Mohe division, tegin Tong to govern the Hu division, tegin Hu to govern the Huxue division, and made Tuli Khan govern the Khitan and Mohe divisions; his headquarters stood south facing Youzhou—all eastern peoples submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli took power he assigned his brothers to govern the tribes: Xueyantuo, Mohe, Hu, and Huxue. Tuli Khan ruled the Khitan and Mohe, with his headquarters south of Youzhou. All eastern tribes fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 突利斂取無法，下不附，故薛延陀、奚、霫等皆內屬，頡利遣擊之，又大敗，眾騷離，頡利囚捶之，久乃赦。

translations.literal: Tuli taxed without restraint; subordinates would not attach themselves; therefore the Xueyantuo, Xi, and Mohe all submitted internally; Jieli sent troops to strike them and was again greatly defeated; the host grew restless and scattered; Jieli imprisoned and beat him, and only after long time pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli taxed his people harshly and lost their loyalty. The Xueyantuo, Xi, and Mohe submitted to Tang. Jieli sent troops against them and suffered another crushing defeat. His forces scattered in turmoil. Jieli imprisoned and beat Tuli, releasing him only after a long time.

sentences.zh: 突利嘗自結於太宗，及頡利衰，驟追兵於突利，不肯從，因起相攻。

translations.literal: Tuli had once allied himself with Taizong; when Jieli declined he suddenly pressed troops on Tuli, who refused to obey, and therefore they rose to attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli had once allied with Taizong. As Jieli's power waned, he suddenly pressed Tuli with troops. Tuli refused, and the two brothers came to blows.

sentences.zh: 突利請入朝，帝謂左右曰：「古為國者勞己以憂人，則系祚長；

translations.literal: Tuli requested to enter court; the Emperor told those beside him: "In antiquity those who governed states labored themselves to care for others, and their line endured long;"
translations.idiomatic: Tuli asked to come to court. The emperor told his attendants: "Ancient rulers who toiled for their people's sake enjoyed long reigns;"

sentences.zh: 役人以奉己，則亡。

translations.literal: those who used people to serve themselves perished.
translations.idiomatic: those who used their people for personal gain perished."

sentences.zh: 今突厥喪亂，由可汗不君，突利雖至親，不自保而來。

translations.literal: Now the Turks are in ruin and disorder because the khan did not govern properly; though Tuli is a close kinsman, he could not preserve himself and has come.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are in chaos because their khan failed to rule. Tuli, though a close kinsman, could not protect himself and has come to us.

sentences.zh: 夷狄弱則邊境安，然觀彼亡，我不可以無懼，有不逮者，禍可紓乎！

translations.literal: When the Yi and Di are weak the border is secure, yet watching them perish I cannot be without fear—if there are things I have not attained, can disaster be eased!
translations.idiomatic: Weak barbarians mean a secure frontier, yet watching them collapse I cannot be complacent. If we fall short anywhere, how can we avert disaster?"

sentences.zh: 」突利至，禮見良厚，輟膳以賜之，拜右衛大將軍，封北平郡王，食戶七百。

translations.literal: When Tuli arrived he was received with excellent courtesy; the Emperor set aside his own meal to bestow it; Tuli was appointed Right Guard General, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping Commandery, with seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli was received with great honor. The emperor shared his own meal with him, made him Right Guard General, enfeoffed him as Prince of Beiping Commandery, and granted seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及為都督，太宗敕曰：「而祖啟民破亡，隋則復之，棄德不報，而父始畢反為隋敵。

translations.literal: When he became grand protector Taizong issued an edict: "Your grandfather Qimin was broken and destroyed; Sui restored him; he abandoned virtue and did not repay; your father Shibi in turn became Sui's enemy."
translations.idiomatic: When Tuli became grand protector, Taizong wrote: "Your grandfather Qimin was destroyed, and Sui restored him—but he betrayed that kindness. Your father Shibi then made himself Sui's enemy."

sentences.zh: 爾今窮來歸我，所以不立爾為可汗，鑒前敗也。

translations.literal: You now come in extremity to submit to me; the reason I do not establish you as khan is to take warning from past failures.
translations.idiomatic: You come to me in desperation. I do not make you khan, taking warning from these past failures.

sentences.zh: 我欲中國安，爾宗族不亡，故授爾都督，毋相侵掠，長為我北藩。

translations.literal: I wish China to be secure and your clan not to perish; therefore I appoint you grand protector—do not raid each other; be my northern frontier guard forever.
translations.idiomatic: I want China secure and your clan preserved. I appoint you grand protector. Do not raid one another. Serve forever as my northern bulwark."

sentences.zh: 」突利頓首聽命。

translations.literal: Tuli bowed his head and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli prostrated himself and accepted.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，死并州道中，年二十九，帝為舉哀，亦詔文本文其墓，子賀邏鶻嗣。

translations.literal: Later he entered court and died on the road in Bing Prefecture at age twenty-nine; the Emperor mourned him and also ordered Wenben compose his tomb inscription; his son Heluoge succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to court he died on the road in Bing Prefecture at twenty-nine. The emperor mourned him and had Cen Wenben compose his epitaph. His son Heluoge succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸九成宮，突利弟結社率以郎將宿衛，陰結種人謀反，劫賀邏鶻北還，謂其黨曰：「我聞晉王丁夜得辟仗出，我乘間突進，可犯行在。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Jiucheng Palace; Tuli's younger brother Jieshelu served as commandant on palace guard; he secretly allied with tribesmen to plot rebellion, seize Heluoge and return north, and told his partisans: "I hear the Prince of Jin at midnight obtains imperial arms and goes out—I can seize the moment and burst in to strike the traveling palace."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Jiucheng Palace, Tuli's brother Jieshelu, a commandant on palace guard, secretly plotted rebellion with tribal allies. He planned to seize Heluoge and flee north, telling his followers: "I hear the Prince of Jin takes up arms at midnight—I can burst in and strike the imperial camp."

sentences.zh: 」是夕，大風冥，王不出，結社率恐謀漏，即射中營，噪而殺人，衛十等共擊之，乃走，殺廄人盜馬，欲度渭，僥邏禽斬之，赦賀邏鶻，投嶺外。

translations.literal: That evening great wind and darkness; the prince did not go out; Jieshelu feared the plot had leaked and immediately shot into the central camp, raised a clamor and killed people; guards Shi and others jointly struck him; he fled, killed stable men and stole horses, wished to cross the Wei; he was captured and beheaded at Yaoluo; Heluoge was pardoned and sent beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: That night a fierce wind blew and darkness fell; the prince did not emerge. Fearing discovery, Jieshelu shot into the camp, raised a clamor, and began killing. Guards repelled him. He fled, killed stable hands, and stole horses to cross the Wei River, but was captured and executed at Yaoluo. Heluoge was pardoned and exiled beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣更言處突厥中國非是，帝亦患之，乃立阿史那思摩為乙彌泥孰俟利可汗，賜氏李，樹牙河北，悉徙突厥還故地。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers again said settling Turks within China was wrong; the Emperor also was troubled by it; he therefore established Ashina Simo as Yimi Nishu Irli Khan, granted the surname Li, set his headquarters north of the river, and moved all Turks back to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers again argued that settling Turks in China was a mistake, and the emperor agreed. He established Ashina Simo as Yimi Nishu Irli Khan, granted him the surname Li, set his headquarters north of the river, and moved all Turks back to their former lands.

sentences.zh: 思摩，頡利族人也，父曰咄六設。

translations.literal: Simo was of Jieli's clan; his father was called she Zhuoliu.
translations.idiomatic: Simo was of Jieli's clan. His father was she Zhuoliu.

sentences.zh: 始，啟民奔隋，磧北諸部奉思摩為可汗，啟民歸國，乃去可汗號。

translations.literal: At first when Qimin fled to Sui the tribes north of the desert made Simo khan; when Qimin returned to his state Simo relinquished the khan title.
translations.idiomatic: When Qimin fled to Sui, the tribes north of the desert made Simo khan. When Qimin returned, Simo relinquished the title.

sentences.zh: 性開敏，善占對，始畢、處羅皆愛之。

translations.literal: His nature was open and quick; he was skilled at divination and reply; Shibi and Chuluo both loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and eloquent, he was favored by both Shibi and Chuluo.

sentences.zh: 然以貌似胡，疑非阿史那種，故但為夾畢特勒，而不得為設。

translations.literal: Yet because his appearance resembled a Hu they suspected he was not of Ashina stock; therefore he was only made Jabiy tegin and could not become she.
translations.idiomatic: Because he looked like a foreigner, some doubted he was true Ashina blood. He was made only Jabiy tegin and never promoted to she.

sentences.zh: 武德初，數以使者來，高祖嘉其誠，封和順郡王。

translations.literal: At the start of Wude he repeatedly came as envoy; Gaozu praised his sincerity and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heshun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wude era he came repeatedly as envoy. Gaozu praised his sincerity and enfeoffed him as Prince of Heshun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及諸部納款，思摩獨留，與頡利俱禽，太宗以為忠，授右武候大將軍、化州都督，統頡利故部居河南，徙懷化郡王。

translations.literal: When the various divisions submitted Simo alone remained and was captured with Jieli; Taizong considered him loyal, appointed him Right Martial Guard General and Grand Protector of Hua Prefecture, governing Jieli's former division dwelling south of the river, and transferred his title to Prince of Huaihua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes submitted, Simo alone stayed with Jieli and was captured. Taizong deemed him loyal, made him Right Martial Guard General and Grand Protector of Hua Prefecture over Jieli's former followers settled south of the river, and transferred his title to Prince of Huaihua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及是將徙，內畏薛延陀，不敢出塞。

translations.literal: When they were about to move he inwardly feared the Xueyantuo and dared not leave the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to move north, he feared the Xueyantuo and dared not leave the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝詔司農卿郭嗣本持節賜延陀書，言：「中國禮義，未始滅人國，以頡利暴殘，伐而取之，非貪其地與人也。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister of Agriculture Guo Siben to go bearing credentials and bestow a letter on the Xueyantuo, saying: "China's rites and righteousness have never sought to destroy people's states; because Jieli was violent and cruel we attacked and took him—not from greed for his land and people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Guo Siben with credentials and a letter to the Xueyantuo: "China's way of rites never seeks to destroy nations. We attacked Jieli because he was cruel—not from greed for land or people."

sentences.zh: 故處降部於河南，薦草美泉，利其畜牧，眾日孳蕃，今復以思摩為可汗，還其故疆。

translations.literal: Therefore we settled the surrendered divisions south of the river where grass was fine and springs sweet, benefiting their herding—the host daily multiplied; now again we make Simo khan and return their former territory.
translations.idiomatic: We settled the surrendered tribes south of the river where pasture and water were good, and their herds multiplied. Now we restore Simo as khan and return them to their former lands.

sentences.zh: 延陀受命在前，長於突厥，舉磧以北，延陀主之；

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo received their mandate first and are senior to the Turks; all north of the desert the Xueyantuo shall rule;
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo received their mandate first and rank above the Turks. All lands north of the desert belong to the Xueyantuo;

sentences.zh: 其南，突厥保之。

translations.literal: to the south the Turks shall hold.
translations.idiomatic: to the south the Turks shall hold."

sentences.zh: 各守而境，無相鈔犯，有負約，我自以兵誅之。

translations.literal: Each shall guard its border without mutual raiding; whoever breaks the covenant I myself shall punish with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each shall guard its own border without raiding the other. Whoever breaks this covenant, I shall punish with arms."

sentences.zh: 」思摩乃行，帝為置酒，引思摩前曰：「蒔一草一木，見其溺廡以為喜，況我養爾部人，息爾馬羊，不減昔乎！

translations.literal: Simo then departed; the Emperor set out wine, drew Simo forward and said: "Plant a single blade of grass or tree and rejoice to see it flourish—how much more I who nurture your tribal people and let your horses and sheep rest, no less than before!"
translations.idiomatic: Simo then departed. The emperor held a farewell feast and drew Simo forward: "One rejoices to see a single plant flourish—how much more should you rejoice that I nurture your people and rest your herds as before!"

sentences.zh: 爾父母墳墓在河北，今復舊廷，故宴以慰行。

translations.literal: Your parents' graves are north of the river; now you return to your old court—therefore I feast to comfort your journey.
translations.idiomatic: Your parents' graves lie north of the river. Now you return to your old domain—I feast to comfort your journey."

sentences.zh: 」思摩泣下，奉觴上萬歲壽，且言：「破亡之餘，陛下使存骨舊鄉，願子孫世世事唐，以報厚德。

translations.literal: Simo wept, raised his cup to toast long life, and said: "We are the remnant after ruin; Your Majesty lets our bones live in our old homeland—we wish our descendants to serve Tang for generations to repay deep grace."
translations.idiomatic: Simo wept, raised his cup to toast the emperor's long life, and said: "We are the remnant of a broken people. Your Majesty restores us to our homeland. May our descendants serve Tang forever to repay your grace."

sentences.zh: 」於是趙郡王孝恭、鴻臚卿劉善就思摩部，築壇場河上，拜受冊，賜鼓纛，又詔左屯衛將軍阿史那忠為左賢王，左武衛將軍阿史那泥孰為右賢王，相之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong and Chief Minister of Guests Liu Shan went to Simo's division, built an altar on the riverbank, and he received investiture with drums and banners; an edict also made Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Zhong Left Wise King and Left Martial Guard General Ashina Nishu Right Wise King to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Zhao and Liu Shan went to Simo's camp, built an altar on the riverbank, and invested him with drums and banners. Ashina Zhong was made Left Wise King and Ashina Nishu Right Wise King to assist him.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀聞突厥之北，恐其眾奔亡度磧，勒兵以待。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo heard the Turks were moving north and feared their host would flee across the desert; they marshaled troops to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the Turks were moving north, the Xueyantuo feared their people would flee across the desert and marshaled troops to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 及使者至，乃謝曰：「天子詔毋相侵，謹頓首奉詔。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived they apologized and said: "The Son of Heaven decreed no mutual invasion—we respectfully bow and accept the decree."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived they apologized: "The Son of Heaven has forbidden mutual invasion. We bow and accept his decree."

sentences.zh: 然突厥酣亂翻覆，其未亡時殺中國人如麻，陛下滅其國，謂宜收種落皆為奴婢，以償唐人。

translations.literal: Yet the Turks are drunken, disorderly, and treacherous; before they perished they killed Chinese like hemp; Your Majesty destroyed their state—we hold that their tribes should all be taken as slaves and maidservants to repay the Tang people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Turks are drunken, disorderly, and treacherous. Before their fall they killed Chinese by the thousands. Your Majesty destroyed their state—we believe their tribes should all be enslaved to repay Tang.

sentences.zh: 乃養之如子，而結社率竟反，此不可信明甚。

translations.literal: Yet you nurture them like sons, and Jieshelu still rebelled—this shows they cannot be trusted, clearly and greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you nurture them like sons, and Jieshelu still rebelled. Their untrustworthiness could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 後有亂，請終為陛下誅之。

translations.literal: If disorder comes later, we ask to execute them for Your Majesty in the end.
translations.idiomatic: If they rebel again, we ask leave to destroy them for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」十五年，思摩帥眾十餘萬、勝兵四萬、馬九萬匹始度河，牙於故定襄城，其地南大河，北白道，畜牧廣衍，龍荒之最壤，故突厥爭利之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Simo led a host of more than a hundred thousand, forty thousand battle-ready troops, and ninety thousand horses to cross the river for the first time; his headquarters stood at old Dingxiang city—south the great river, north the White Road, pasture broad and spreading, the finest soil of the dragon wilderness, which the Turks had therefore contested for profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Simo crossed the river with more than a hundred thousand followers, forty thousand warriors, and ninety thousand horses. He established his headquarters at old Dingxiang city—south lay the great river, north the White Road. Its vast pastures were the finest on the northern steppe, which the Turks had long contested.

sentences.zh: 思摩遣使謝曰：「蒙恩立為落長，實望世世為國一犬，守吠天子北門，有如延陀侵逼，願入保長城。

translations.literal: Simo sent envoys to give thanks: "Receiving grace to be established as tribal chief, I truly hope to be the state's hound for generations, guarding and barking at the Son of Heaven's northern gate; if the Xueyantuo press and invade, I wish to enter and shelter within the Long Wall."
translations.idiomatic: Simo sent envoys in gratitude: "By your grace I am made tribal chief. I hope to serve as your watchdog at the northern gate for generations. If the Xueyantuo attack, I ask shelter within the Great Wall."

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 居三年，不能得其眾，下多攜背，思摩慚，因入朝願留宿衛，更拜右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: After three years' residence he could not win his host; subordinates mostly turned disloyal; Simo was ashamed and therefore entered court wishing to remain on palace guard, and was again appointed Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he could not hold his people together. Many followers turned away. Ashamed, Simo came to court and asked to remain on palace guard. He was made Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 從伐遼，中流矢，帝為吮血，其顧厚類此。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Liaodong he was struck by an arrow; the Emperor sucked the blood for him—his care and generosity were like this.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he was struck by an arrow. The emperor sucked the blood from his wound. Such was his care for Simo.

sentences.zh: 還，卒京師，贈兵部尚書、夏州都督，陪葬昭陵，築墳象白道山，為刊其勞，碑於化州。

translations.literal: Returning, he died in the capital; posthumously awarded Minister of War and Grand Protector of Xia Prefecture; buried with Zhaoling; his tomb mound was built in the likeness of White Road Mountain; his merits were inscribed on a stele at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital on his return. Posthumously made Minister of War and Grand Protector of Xia Prefecture, he was buried at Zhaoling. His tomb was shaped like White Road Mountain, and a stele recording his service was erected at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 右賢王阿史那泥孰，蘇尼失子也。

translations.literal: Right Wise King Ashina Nishu was Sunishi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Right Wise King Ashina Nishu was the son of Sunishi.

sentences.zh: 始歸國，妻以宗女，賜名忠。

translations.literal: When he first submitted to the state a clanswoman was given him in marriage and the name Zhong was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first submitted, an imperial clanswoman was given him in marriage and he was granted the name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 及從思摩出塞，思慕中國，見使者必流涕求入侍，許之。

translations.literal: When he followed Simo beyond the passes he yearned for China; seeing envoys he always wept and begged to enter service; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Simo beyond the frontier he yearned for China. Whenever he saw Tang envoys he wept and begged to enter court service. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 思摩既不能國，殘眾稍稍南度河，分處勝、夏二州。

translations.literal: Since Simo could not maintain his state, remnant followers gradually crossed the river south and were distributed between Sheng and Xia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to maintain his state, Simo's remnant followers gradually crossed south of the river and were settled in Sheng and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 帝伐遼，或言突厥處河南，邇京師，請帝無東。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Liaodong some said the Turks dwelt south of the river near the capital and urged the Emperor not to go east.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, some warned that Turks settled south of the river were too close to the capital and urged him not to go east.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「夫為君者，豈有猜貳哉！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "For one who is ruler, how could there be suspicion and division!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Should a ruler harbor suspicion and division?"

sentences.zh: 湯、武化桀、紂之民，無不遷善，有隋無道，舉天下皆叛，非止夷狄也。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu transformed the people of Jie and Zhou—none failed to turn toward goodness; Sui was without the Way and all under Heaven rebelled—not only the Yi and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu transformed the people of Jie and Zhou, and all turned toward virtue. Sui lost the Way and all under Heaven rebelled—not barbarians alone."

sentences.zh: 朕閔突厥之亡，內河南以振贍之，彼不近走延陀而遠歸我，懷我深矣，朕策五十年中國無突厥患。

translations.literal: We pity the Turks' destruction and settled them south of the river to nourish and support them—they did not flee nearby to the Xueyantuo but returned to us from afar; they cherish us deeply; we calculate that for fifty years China will have no Turkish trouble.
translations.idiomatic: We pity the Turks' fall and settled them south of the river to sustain them. They did not flee to the Xueyantuo but came to us from afar—they cherish us deeply. I calculate that China will have no Turkish trouble for fifty years."

sentences.zh: 」思摩眾既南，車鼻可汗乃盜有其地。

translations.literal: Once Simo's host had moved south Chebi Khan then seized his lands by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Once Simo's people moved south, Chebi Khan seized the vacated lands.

sentences.zh: 車鼻，亦阿史那族，而突利部人也，名斛勃，世為小可汗。

translations.literal: Chebi was also of the Ashina clan and of Tuli's division; his name was Hubo; for generations he had been lesser khan.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi was also Ashina, from Tuli's division. His name was Hubo. His family had held the title of lesser khan for generations.

sentences.zh: 頡利敗，諸部欲共君長之，會薛延陀稱可汗，乃往歸焉。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated the various divisions wished jointly to make him their lord; it happened the Xueyantuo proclaimed a khan, and he therefore went to submit to them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat the tribes wished to make him their leader, but the Xueyantuo had proclaimed a khan, so he submitted to them instead.

sentences.zh: 其為人沈果有智數，眾頗便附，延陀畏逼，將殺之，乃率所部遯去，騎數千尾追，不勝。

translations.literal: As a man he was deep, resolute, and resourceful; many readily attached themselves to him; the Xueyantuo feared and pressed him and were about to kill him; he therefore led his division and fled; several thousand horsemen pursued but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Deep, resolute, and cunning, he drew many followers. The Xueyantuo, fearing his rise, moved to kill him. He fled with his tribe. Thousands of horsemen pursued but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 竄金山之北，三垂斗絕，惟一面可容車騎，壤土夷博，即據之，勝兵三萬，自稱乙註車鼻可汗，距長安萬里，西葛邏祿，北結骨，皆並統之，時時出掠延陀人畜。

translations.literal: He hid north of the Altai Mountains where three sides rose sheer and only one could admit chariots and horsemen; the soil was level and broad—he seized it; battle-ready troops numbered thirty thousand; he proclaimed himself Yizhu Chebi Khan; ten thousand li from Chang'an; west the Geluolu, north the Kirghiz—all were jointly governed by him; from time to time he raided Xueyantuo people and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He fled north of the Altai Mountains to a plateau accessible from only one side. With thirty thousand warriors he proclaimed himself Yizhu Chebi Khan, ten thousand li from Chang'an. He ruled the Geluolu to the west and the Kirghiz to the north, and raided the Xueyantuo whenever he could.

sentences.zh: 延陀後衰，車鼻勢益張。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo later declined and Chebi's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: As the Xueyantuo declined, Chebi's power grew.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遣子沙缽羅特勒獻方物，且請身入朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he sent his son Shabolu tegin to present local products and also requested to enter court in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he sent his son Shabolu tegin with tribute and asked to come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 帝遣雲麾將軍安調遮、右屯衛郎將韓華往迎之，至則車鼻偃然無入朝意，華謀與葛邏祿共劫之，車鼻覺，華與車鼻子陟特勒鬥死，調遮被殺。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Cloud Standard General An Diaozhe and Right Garrison Guard Commandant Han Hua to welcome him; when they arrived Chebi showed no intention of entering court; Hua plotted with the Geluolu jointly to seize him; Chebi discovered it; Hua and Chebi's son Zhi tegin fought to the death; Diaozhe was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent An Diaozhe and Han Hua to escort him. Chebi showed no intention of coming to court. Han Hua plotted with the Geluolu to seize him, but Chebi discovered the plan. Han Hua and Chebi's son Zhi tegin killed each other in the fight, and Diaozhe was slain.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣右驍衛郎將高偘發回紇、仆骨兵擊之，其大酋長歌邏祿泥孰闕俟利發、處木昆莫賀咄俟斤等以次降。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent Right Martial Guard Commandant Gao Kan to mobilize Uyghur and Pugu troops to attack him; the great chieftains Geluolu Nishu Que Irli Fa, Chumukun Moheduo Irkin, and others submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor sent Gao Kan with Uyghur and Pugu troops. The great chiefs Geluolu Nishu Que Irli Fa, Chumukun Moheduo Irkin, and others surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 偘師攻阿息山，部落不肯戰，車鼻攜愛妾，從數百騎走；

translations.literal: Kan's army attacked Mount Axi; the tribes would not fight; Chebi took his beloved concubine and fled with several hundred horsemen;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan attacked Mount Axi, but the tribes refused to fight. Chebi fled with his favorite concubine and a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 追至金山，獲之，獻京師。

translations.literal: pursued to the Altai Mountains, captured, and presented at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued to the Altai Mountains, he was captured and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高宗責曰：「頡利敗，爾不輔，無親也；

translations.literal: Gaozong reproached him: "When Jieli was defeated you did not assist—there was no kinship;"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong rebuked him: "When Jieli fell you did not aid him—you lacked loyalty to kin."

sentences.zh: 延陀破，爾遯亡，不忠也。

translations.literal: when the Xueyantuo were broken you fled and hid—there was no loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xueyantuo fell you fled and hid—you lacked loyalty to your lord."

sentences.zh: 而罪當死，然朕見先帝所獲酋長必宥之，今原而死。

translations.literal: Your crime deserves death, yet We see that chieftains captured by the former Emperor were always pardoned—now We pardon and spare you.
translations.idiomatic: Your crimes deserve death, yet my father always pardoned captured chieftains. I pardon you now."

sentences.zh: 」乃釋縛，數俘社廟，又見昭陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon bonds were released; captives were counted at the state altars; he was also presented at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His bonds were removed. Captives were presented at the ancestral temple and at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 拜左武衛將軍，賜居第，處其眾郁督軍山，詔建狼山都督府統之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Martial Guard General, granted a residence, his host was settled at Mount Yudu, and an edict established Langshan Protectorate to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Martial Guard General and given a residence. His people were settled at Mount Yudu under the newly established Langshan Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 初，其子羯漫陀泣諫車鼻，請歸國，不聽。

translations.literal: At first his son Jieman tuo wept and remonstrated with Chebi, begging to return to the state; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jieman tuo had wept and urged Chebi to submit to Tang, but Chebi refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣子庵鑠入朝，後來降，拜左屯衛將軍，建新黎州，使領其眾。

translations.literal: He therefore sent his son Anshuo to court; later he came to submit; appointed Left Garrison Guard General; Xinli Prefecture was established for him to lead his host.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi had sent another son, Anshuo, to court. Anshuo later surrendered, was made Left Garrison Guard General, and given Xinli Prefecture to govern his followers.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥盡為封疆臣矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turks all became frontier subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were now all subjects of the Tang frontier.

sentences.zh: 始置單于都護府領狼山雲中桑乾三都督、蘇農等二十四州，瀚海都護府領金微新黎等七都督、仙萼賀蘭等八州。

translations.literal: The Chanyu Grand Protectorate was first established governing the three protectorates Langshan, Yunzhong, and Sanggan and twenty-four prefectures including Sunong; the Hanhai Grand Protectorate governed seven protectorates including Jinwei and Xinli and eight prefectures including Xian'e and Helan.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu Grand Protectorate was established over the Langshan, Yunzhong, and Sanggan protectorates and twenty-four prefectures including Sunong. The Hanhai Grand Protectorate governed seven protectorates including Jinwei and Xinli and eight prefectures including Xian'e and Helan.

sentences.zh: 即擢領酋為都督、刺史。

translations.literal: Tribal chiefs were immediately promoted to grand protectors and prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal chiefs were promoted to grand protectors and prefectural governors.

sentences.zh: 麟德初，改燕然為瀚海都護府，領回紇，徙故瀚海都護府於古雲中城，號雲中都護府，磧以北蕃州悉隸瀚海，南隸雲中。

translations.literal: At the start of Linde Yanran was changed to Hanhai Grand Protectorate governing the Uyghurs; the former Hanhai Grand Protectorate was moved to old Yunzhong city and titled Yunzhong Grand Protectorate; all frontier prefectures north of the desert submitted to Hanhai, those south to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Linde 1 Yanran was renamed Hanhai Grand Protectorate over the Uyghurs. The former Hanhai protectorate moved to old Yunzhong city as the Yunzhong Grand Protectorate. Frontier prefectures north of the desert fell under Hanhai; those south under Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 雲中者，義成公主所居也，頡利滅，李靖徙突厥羸破數百帳居之，以阿史德為之長，眾稍盛，即建言願以諸王為可汗，遙統之。

translations.literal: Yunzhong was where Princess Yicheng had dwelt; when Jieli was destroyed Li Jing moved several hundred weak and broken Turkish tents to dwell there; Ashina De was made their chief; the host gradually grew strong and immediately offered counsel wishing to use imperial princes as khans to govern them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong was where Princess Yicheng had lived. After Jieli's fall Li Jing settled several hundred broken Turkish tents there under Ashina De. As their numbers grew, they proposed that Tang princes be made khans to rule them from afar.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今可汗，古單于也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Today's khan is the ancient Chanyu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Today's khan is the ancient Chanyu."

sentences.zh: 」乃改雲中府為單于大都護府，以殷王旭輪為單于都護。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yunzhong Protectorate was changed to Chanyu Supreme Protectorate and Prince Yin Xulun was made Chanyu Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong Protectorate was renamed the Chanyu Supreme Protectorate, and Prince Yin Xulun was made Chanyu Protector.

sentences.zh: 帝封禪，都督葛邏祿叱利等三十餘人皆從至泰山下，已封，詔勒名於封禪碑云。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed the feng and shan rites more than thirty grand protectors including Geluolu Chili all followed to the foot of Mount Tai; after the rite an edict ordered their names carved on the fengshan stele.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's feng and shan rites at Mount Tai, more than thirty grand protectors including Geluolu Chili accompanied him. After the ceremony their names were carved on the stele.

sentences.zh: 凡三十年北方無戎馬警。

translations.literal: For thirty years in all the north had no alarm of war-horses.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years the north knew no alarm of war-horses.

sentences.zh: 調露初，單于府大酋溫傅、奉職二部反，立阿史那泥孰匐為可汗，二十四州酋長皆叛應之。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiaolu the Chanyu Protectorate's great chiefs Wenfu and Fengzhi in two divisions rebelled, established Ashina Nishufu as khan, and chieftains of twenty-four prefectures all rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiaolu the great chiefs Wenfu and Fengzhi of the Chanyu Protectorate rebelled, enthroned Ashina Nishufu as khan, and chieftains of twenty-four prefectures rose with them.

sentences.zh: 乃以鴻臚卿單于大都護府長史蕭嗣業、左領軍衛將軍苑大智、右千牛衛將軍李景嘉討之，恃勝不設備，會雨雪，士皸寒，反為虜襲，大敗，殺略萬餘人，大智等收餘卒，行且戰，乃免。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of Guests and Chanyu Supreme Protectorate Chief Administrator Xiao Siye, Left Army Guard General Yuan Dazhi, and Right Thousand-Ox Guard General Li Jingjia were sent to suppress them; relying on victory they made no preparations; encountering rain and snow soldiers' skins cracked with cold; they were in turn raided by the barbarians and greatly defeated; more than ten thousand were killed or captured; Dazhi and others gathered remnant troops and fought as they withdrew—only then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Siye, Yuan Dazhi, and Li Jingjia were sent against them. Overconfident, they made no preparations. Rain and snow struck; soldiers froze. The rebels attacked and routed them, killing or capturing more than ten thousand. Dazhi and the others gathered survivors and fought their way out.

sentences.zh: 於是嗣業流桂州，余坐免官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Siye was exiled to Guizhou; the rest were dismissed from office by punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Siye was exiled to Guizhou; the others were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 更拜禮部尚書裴行儉為定襄道行軍大總管，率太僕少卿李思文、營州都督周道務、西軍程務挺、東軍李文柬，士無慮三十萬，捕擊反者。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Pei Xingjian was again appointed Mobile Campaign Supreme Commander of the Dingxiang route, leading Vice Minister of Imperial Stud Li Siwen, Yingzhou Inspector Zhou Daowu, Western Army Cheng Wuting, and Eastern Army Li Wenjian—troops numbering no less than three hundred thousand—to pursue and strike the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian was made supreme commander of the Dingxiang route with Li Siwen, Zhou Daowu, Cheng Wuting, and Li Wenjian. With some three hundred thousand men they pursued the rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔右金吾將軍曹懷舜屯井陘，右武衛將軍崔獻屯絳、龍門。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Right Golden Guard General Cao Huaishun to encamp at Jingxing and Right Martial Guard General Cui Xian to encamp at Jiang and Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Huaishun was ordered to garrison Jingxing and Cui Xian to garrison Jiang and Longmen.

sentences.zh: 明年，行儉戰黑山，大破之，其下斬泥孰匐，以首降，禽溫傅、奉職以還，餘眾保狼山。

translations.literal: The next year Xingjian fought at Black Mountain and greatly defeated them; his subordinates beheaded Nishufu and surrendered with the head; Wenfu and Fengzhi were captured and brought back; remnant followers held Langshan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Pei Xingjian routed them at Black Mountain. His men beheaded Nishufu and surrendered with the head. Wenfu and Fengzhi were captured. The remnants held out at Langshan.

sentences.zh: 始虜未叛，鳴鵽群飛入塞，吏曰：「所謂突厥雀者，南飛，胡必至。

translations.literal: Before the barbarians rebelled flocks of screaming pheasants flew into the passes; officials said: "What are called Turkish sparrows—when they fly south the Hu must arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Before the rebellion flocks of screaming pheasants flew into the frontier passes. Officials said: "These 'Turkish sparrows' fly south when barbarians are coming."

sentences.zh: 」比春還，悉墮靈、夏間，率無首，泥孰果亡。

translations.literal: When spring returned they all fell between Ling and Xia—mostly headless; Nishu indeed perished.
translations.idiomatic: When spring came they fell dead between Ling and Xia—mostly headless. Nishufu indeed perished."

sentences.zh: 狼山眾掠雲州，都督竇懷哲、右領軍中郎將程務挺逐出之。

translations.literal: The Langshan host raided Yun Prefecture; Inspector Dou Huaizhe and Right Army Guard Commandant Cheng Wuting drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: The Langshan rebels raided Yun Prefecture. Dou Huaizhe and Cheng Wuting drove them out.

sentences.zh: 永隆中，溫傅部又迎頡利族子伏念於夏州，走度河，立為可汗，諸部響應。

translations.literal: In Yonglong Wenfu's division again welcomed Jieli's clansman Funian at Xia Prefecture; he fled across the river and was established as khan; the various divisions responded in echo.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong Wenfu's faction welcomed Jieli's kinsman Funian at Xia Prefecture. Funian fled across the river and was made khan. Tribes rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂寇原、慶二州。

translations.literal: The next year they then raided Yuan and Qing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they raided Yuan and Qing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 復詔行儉為大總管，以右武衛將軍曹懷舜、幽州都督李文柬副之。

translations.literal: An edict again made Xingjian supreme commander with Right Martial Guard General Cao Huaishun and Youzhou Inspector Li Wenjian as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian was again made supreme commander, with Cao Huaishun and Youzhou Inspector Li Wenjian as deputies.

sentences.zh: 諜者紿言伏念、溫傅保黑沙，饑甚，可輕騎取也。

translations.literal: Spies falsely reported Funian and Wenfu held Black Sand, were extremely hungry, and could be taken with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported falsely that Funian and Wenfu held Black Sand, were starving, and could be taken with a light cavalry raid.

sentences.zh: 懷舜獨信之，輕兵倍道至黑沙，乃不見虜，得薛延陀餘部，降之；

translations.literal: Huaishun alone believed it; light troops marched by double stages to Black Sand but saw no barbarians; they obtained Xueyantuo remnant divisions and accepted their surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun alone believed the report and rushed light troops to Black Sand. They found no rebels, only Xueyantuo remnants, whom they accepted in surrender.

sentences.zh: 引還至長城，遇溫傅與戰，所殺相當。

translations.literal: returning as far as the Long Wall they encountered Wenfu and fought; kills on both sides were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march at the Great Wall they met Wenfu in battle. Casualties were roughly equal on both sides.

sentences.zh: 行儉兵壁代之陘口，縱反間，故伏念、溫傅相貳，因遣兵擊伏念，敗之。

translations.literal: Xingjian's army fortified at Daizhou's pass mouth, deployed counter-intelligence, and therefore Funian and Wenfu grew mutually suspicious; he then sent troops to strike Funian and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian fortified at the Daizhou pass, sowed discord between Funian and Wenfu, then attacked Funian and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 伏念走，與懷舜遇，行且戰一日，為伏念所破，棄軍奔雲中，士為虜所乘，死不可算，皆南首仆。

translations.literal: Funian fled and met Huaishun; they fought as they marched for a day; Huaishun was defeated by Funian, abandoned his army and fled to Yunzhong; soldiers were overtaken by the barbarians and deaths were beyond counting—all lay faced south.
translations.idiomatic: Funian fled and encountered Huaishun. They fought a running battle for a day before Huaishun was routed. He abandoned his army and fled to Yunzhong. Tang soldiers were overrun; the dead were beyond count, all lying faced south.

sentences.zh: 懷舜殺牲與伏念盟，乃免。

translations.literal: Huaishun sacrificed livestock and allied with Funian, and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun sacrificed livestock to seal an alliance with Funian and escaped.

sentences.zh: 伏念益北，留輜重妻子保金牙山，以輕騎將襲懷舜，會行儉遣部將掩得其輜重，比還，無所歸，乃北走保細沙。

translations.literal: Funian pressed further north, leaving baggage, wives, and children at Mount Jinyá while he led light cavalry to raid Huaishun; Xingjian sent a subordinate to seize the baggage; when Funian returned he had nowhere to go and fled north to hold Xisha.
translations.idiomatic: Funian marched north, leaving family and supplies at Mount Jinyá. He led light cavalry against Huaishun, but Pei Xingjian's detachments captured his baggage. With nowhere to turn, Funian fled north to Xisha.

sentences.zh: 行儉縱單于鎮兵躡之，伏念意王師不能遠，不設備，及兵至，惶駭不得戰，遂遣使間道詣行儉，執溫傅降，行儉虜之，送京師，斬東市。

translations.literal: Xingjian sent Chanyu garrison troops to follow; Funian thought imperial armies could not come far and made no preparations; when troops arrived he was terrified and could not fight; he sent envoys by hidden routes to Xingjian, seized Wenfu and submitted; Xingjian captured him, sent him to the capital, and executed him at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian sent Chanyu garrison troops in pursuit. Funian assumed Tang armies could not march so far and took no precautions. When they arrived he panicked. He sent envoys to Xingjian, handed over Wenfu, and surrendered. Xingjian sent him to the capital and executed him at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，骨咄祿又反。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Kutlug rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun 1 Kutlug rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿，頡利族人也，雲中都督舍利元英之部酋，世襲吐屯。

translations.literal: Kutlug was of Jieli's clan, a division chief of Yunzhong Protectorate's Sheli Yuanying, holding the tutun office by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug was of Jieli's clan, a division chief under Sheli Yuanying of Yunzhong Protectorate, hereditary tutun.

sentences.zh: 伏念敗，乃嘯亡散，保總材山，又治黑沙城，有眾五千，盜九姓畜馬，稍強大，乃自立為可汗，以弟默啜為殺，咄悉匐為葉護。

translations.literal: When Funian was defeated he gathered scattered fugitives, held Mount Zongcai, also fortified Black Sand city, had a host of five thousand, stole livestock and horses of the Nine Surnames, gradually grew strong, and established himself as khan, making his brother Mokchur she and Tuxibo yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: After Funian's defeat Kutlug rallied fugitives, held Mount Zongcai, and fortified Black Sand city. With five thousand men he stole Nine Surname herds, grew strong, and proclaimed himself khan, making his brother Mokchur she and Tuxibo yabghu.

sentences.zh: 時單于府檢校降戶部落阿史德元珍者，為長史王本立所囚。

translations.literal: At that time Ashina Yuanzhen, inspector of surrendered-household tribes of the Chanyu Protectorate, was imprisoned by Chief Administrator Wang Benli.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Yuanzhen, inspector of surrendered tribes under the Chanyu Protectorate, was imprisoned by Chief Administrator Wang Benli.

sentences.zh: 會骨咄祿來寇，元珍請諭還諸部贖罪，許之。

translations.literal: When Kutlug came to raid, Yuanzhen asked to be sent to summon the tribes back to redeem his crime; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Kutlug raided, Yuanzhen offered to summon the tribes back in exchange for pardon. The offer was accepted.

sentences.zh: 至即降骨咄祿，與為謀，遂以為阿波達幹，悉屬以兵。
