translations.literal: Upon arrival he immediately submitted to Kutlug and plotted with him; Kutlug therefore made him Apo Taghan and entrusted him with all troops.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he defected to Kutlug and became his strategist. Kutlug made him Apo Taghan and entrusted him with all troops.

sentences.zh: 乃寇單于府北鄙，遂攻并州，殺嵐州刺史王德茂，分掠定州，北平刺史霍王元軌擊卻之。

translations.literal: They then raided the Chanyu Protectorate's northern border, attacked Bing Prefecture, killed Lan Prefecture Inspector Wang Demao, divided forces to plunder Ding Prefecture, and were driven back by Beiping Prefecture Inspector Prince of Huo Yuan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: They raided the Chanyu Protectorate's northern frontier, attacked Bing Prefecture, and killed Lan Prefecture Inspector Wang Demao. They plundered Ding Prefecture but were repelled by Prince Yuan Gui of Huo, inspector of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 又攻媯州，圍單于都護府，殺司馬張行師，攻蔚州，殺刺史李思儉，執豐州都督崔知辯。

translations.literal: They again attacked Ji Prefecture, besieged the Chanyu Protectorate, killed Administrator Zhang Xingshi, attacked Yu Prefecture, killed Prefect Li Sijian, and captured Feng Prefecture Protector Cui Zhibian.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Ji Prefecture, besieged the Chanyu Protectorate, and killed Administrator Zhang Xingshi. They attacked Yu Prefecture, killed Prefect Li Sijian, and captured Feng Prefecture Protector Cui Zhibian.

sentences.zh: 詔右武衛將軍程務挺為單于道安撫大使備邊。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Right Martial Guard General Cheng Wuting Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu route to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting was appointed Right Martial Guard General and Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu route to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖、垂拱間，連寇朔、代，掠吏士。

translations.literal: Between the Sisheng and Chuigong reigns they repeatedly raided Shuo and Dai and plundered officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Between Sisheng and Chuigong they repeatedly raided Shuo and Dai and preyed on officials and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 左玉鈴衛中郎將淳于處平為陽曲道總管，將擊賊總材山，至忻州與賊遇，鏖戰不利，死者五千人。

translations.literal: Left Jade Bell Guard Commandant Chunyu Chuping was made supreme commander of the Yangqu route to strike the bandits at Mount Zongcai; reaching Xin Prefecture he met the bandits; after fierce fighting he was unsuccessful and five thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Chuping was made supreme commander of the Yangqu route to attack the rebels at Mount Zongcai. At Xin Prefecture he met them in fierce battle and lost five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 更以天官尚書韋待價為燕然道大總管討之。

translations.literal: Minister of Heaven Wei Daijia was again made supreme commander of the Yanran route to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Daijia was made supreme commander of the Yanran route to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 明年，入昌平，右鷹揚衛大將軍黑齒常之擊卻之。

translations.literal: The next year they entered Changping; Right Hawk-Banner Guard General Heichi Changzhi drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they entered Changping. Heichi Changzhi drove them back.

sentences.zh: 復入朔州地，常之與戰黃花堆，虜敗，追奔四十里，遯過磧。

translations.literal: They again entered Shuo Prefecture territory; Changzhi fought them at Yellow Flower Mound; the barbarians were defeated; pursuit ran forty li; they fled across the desert.
translations.idiomatic: They entered Shuo Prefecture again. Changzhi defeated them at Yellow Flower Mound and pursued them forty li until they fled across the desert.

sentences.zh: 右監門衛中郎將爨寶璧當追，意虜即破，欲幸取功，乃募諜出塞二千里，間虜無備，趨襲之。

translations.literal: Right Gate Guard Commandant Cuan Baobi was to pursue; thinking the barbarians were already broken and wishing to seize merit for himself, he recruited spies to go two thousand li beyond the passes; learning the barbarians were unprepared he rushed to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Baobi was ordered to pursue. Assuming the enemy was already broken, he recruited spies to scout two thousand li beyond the frontier, found the Turks unprepared, and rushed to attack.

sentences.zh: 將至，漏言於軍，虜得整眾出，皆死戰，大敗，寶璧跳還，舉軍沒。

translations.literal: As they were about to arrive word leaked in the army; the barbarians mustered and came out, all fought to the death, and he was greatly defeated; Baobi leaped back alone and the entire army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Word leaked before he arrived. The Turks mustered and fought to the death. Baobi was routed; he escaped alone while his entire force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 武後怒，誅寶璧，改骨咄祿曰不卒祿。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was angry, executed Baobi, and changed Kutlug's name to Buzulu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu executed Baobi and renamed Kutlug Buzulu.

sentences.zh: 俄而元珍攻突騎施，戰死。

translations.literal: Soon Yuanzhen attacked the Turgesh and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanzhen attacked the Turgesh and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 天授初，骨咄祿死，其子幼，不得立。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshou Kutlug died; his son was young and could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianshou Kutlug died. His son was too young to succeed.

sentences.zh: 默啜自立為可汗，篡位數年，始攻靈州，多殺略士民。

translations.literal: Mokchur established himself as khan; after usurping power for several years he first attacked Ling Prefecture and killed and plundered many officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur seized the khanship. After several years he attacked Ling Prefecture and killed and plundered widely.

sentences.zh: 武後以薛懷義為朔方道行軍大總管，內史李昭德為行軍長史，鳳閣鸞臺平章事蘇味道為司馬，率朔方道總管契明、雁門道總管王孝傑、威化道總管李多祚、豐安道總管陳令英、瀚海道總管田揚名等凡十八將軍兵出塞，雜華蕃步騎擊之，不見虜，還。

translations.literal: Empress Wu made Xue Huaiyi supreme commander of the Shuofang mobile campaign route, Internal Affairs Director Li Zhaode chief administrator, and Co-Equalizing Grand Counselor Su Weidao marshal, leading Shuofang route supreme commander Qiming, Yanmen route supreme commander Wang Xiaojie, Weihua route supreme commander Li Duozuo, Feng'an route supreme commander Chen Lingying, Hanhai route supreme commander Tian Yangming, and eighteen generals in all with mixed Chinese and barbarian infantry and cavalry beyond the passes to strike them; they saw no barbarians and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent Xue Huaiyi as supreme commander of the Shuofang route with Li Zhaode and Su Weidao, leading eighteen generals including Qiming, Wang Xiaojie, Li Duozuo, Chen Lingying, and Tian Yangming with mixed Chinese and tribal forces beyond the frontier. They found no enemy and returned.

sentences.zh: 俄詔孝傑為朔方道行軍總管備邊。

translations.literal: Soon an edict made Xiaojie supreme commander of the Shuofang route to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaojie was soon made supreme commander of the Shuofang route to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 契丹李盡忠等反，默啜請擊賊自效，詔可。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong and others rebelled Mokchur requested to strike the bandits to prove his loyalty; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled, Mokchur offered to attack the rebels. The empress agreed.

sentences.zh: 授左衛大將軍、歸國公，以左豹韜衛將軍閻知微即部冊拜遷善可汗。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Guard General and Duke of Returning State; Left Leopard-Bow Guard General Yan Zhiwei went to his division to invest him as Qianshan Khan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Guard General and Duke of Returning State. Yan Zhiwei invested him as Qianshan Khan at his camp.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃引兵擊契丹，會盡忠死，襲松漠部落，盡得孫萬榮妻子輜重，酋長崩潰。

translations.literal: Mokchur then led troops to attack the Khitan; when Jinzhong died he raided the Songmo tribe, seized all of Sun Wanrong's wives, baggage, and chieftains collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur attacked the Khitan. When Jinzhong died he raided the Songmo tribe, seized Sun Wanrong's wives and baggage, and shattered their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 後美其攻，復詔知微持節冊默啜為特進、頡跌利施大單于、立功報國可汗。

translations.literal: Later praising his attack an edict again ordered Zhiwei bearing credentials to invest Mokchur as Special Grand Master, Elteber Great Chanyu, and Khan Who Establishes Merit and Serves the State.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his campaign, the court again sent Yan Zhiwei to invest Mokchur as Special Grand Master, Elteber Great Chanyu, and Khan Who Establishes Merit and Serves the State.

sentences.zh: 未及命，俄攻靈、勝二州，縱殺略，為屯將所敗。

translations.literal: Before the commission arrived he soon attacked Ling and Sheng prefectures, wantonly killed and plundered, and was defeated by garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Before the commission arrived he attacked Ling and Sheng prefectures, ravaged the countryside, and was defeated by garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 又遣使者謝，請為後子，復言有女，願女諸王，且求六州降戶。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to apologize, asked to become an adopted son, also said he had a daughter and wished to marry her to an imperial prince, and moreover requested the six prefectures' surrendered households.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to apologize, asked to become the empress's adopted son, offered his daughter for marriage to an imperial prince, and demanded the six prefectures' surrendered households.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥內屬者分處豐、勝、靈、夏、朔、代間，謂之河曲六州降人。

translations.literal: At first internally submitted Turks were distributed among Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai—called the six prefectures' surrendered people of the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: Internally submitted Turks had been settled among Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai—the six river-bend prefectures of surrendered peoples.

sentences.zh: 默啜又請粟田種十萬斛，農器三千具，鐵數萬斤，後不許，宰相李嶠亦言不可。

translations.literal: Mokchur also requested a hundred thousand bushels of seed grain, three thousand farming implements, and tens of thousands of pounds of iron; the empress refused and Chancellor Li Jiao also said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur also demanded a hundred thousand bushels of seed grain, three thousand farming tools, and tens of thousands of pounds of iron. The empress refused, and Chancellor Li Jiao agreed.

sentences.zh: 默啜怨，為慢言，執使者司賓卿田歸道。

translations.literal: Mokchur resented this, spoke insolently, and seized the envoy Chief Minister of Guests Tian Guidao.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur was enraged, spoke insolently, and seized the envoy Tian Guidao.

sentences.zh: 於是納言姚璹等建請與之，乃歸粟、器、降人數千帳，繇是突厥遂強。

translations.literal: Thereupon Remonstrance Counselor Yao Shuang and others urged granting his requests; grain, implements, and several thousand tents of surrendered people were returned—thereby the Turks grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Yao Shuang and others urged compliance. Grain, tools, and thousands of surrendered tents were sent—and the Turks grew strong.

sentences.zh: 詔淮陽王武延秀聘其女為妃，詔知微攝春官尚書，與司賓卿楊鸞莊持節護送。

translations.literal: An edict betrothed Prince of Huaiyang Wu Yanxiu to his daughter as consort and ordered Zhiwei acting Minister of Spring Office with Chief Minister of Guests Yang Luanzhuang bearing credentials to escort her.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Yanxiu of Huaiyang was betrothed to Mokchur's daughter. Yan Zhiwei and Yang Luanzhuang were sent to escort her.

sentences.zh: 默啜猥曰：「我以女嫁唐天子子，今乃後家子乎！

translations.literal: Mokchur rudely said: "I marry my daughter to the Son of Heaven's son—now it is a empress-clan son!"
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur sneered: "I offered my daughter to the Son of Heaven's son—and you send a Wu clan prince!"

sentences.zh: 且我世附唐，今聞其子孫獨二人在，我當立之。

translations.literal: Moreover we have submitted to Tang for generations; now I hear only two of their descendants remain—I ought to install one."
translations.idiomatic: We have served Tang for generations. I hear only two Tang descendants survive—I ought to install one of them."

sentences.zh: 」即囚延秀等，妄號知微為可汗，自將十萬騎南向擊靜難、平狄、清夷等軍，靜難軍使慕容玄崱以兵五千降。

translations.literal: He immediately imprisoned Yanxiu and others, falsely proclaimed Zhiwei khan, and personally led a hundred thousand horsemen south to strike the Jingnan, Pingdi, and Qingyi armies; Jingnan Army Commissioner Murong Xuankuo surrendered with five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Yanxiu and the others, proclaimed Yan Zhiwei khan, and led a hundred thousand horsemen south against the Jingnan, Pingdi, and Qingyi armies. Murong Xuankuo surrendered with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 虜入圍媯、檀，後詔司屬卿武重規為天兵中道大總管，右武威衛將軍沙咤忠義為天兵西道總管，幽州都督張仁亶為天兵東道總管，兵凡三十萬擊之；

translations.literal: The barbarians entered and besieged Ji and Tan; the empress ordered Director of Retainers Wu Chonggui supreme commander of the central Celestial Army route, Right Martial Guard General Shazha Zhongyi supreme commander of the western Celestial Army route, and Youzhou Protector Zhang Renyan supreme commander of the eastern Celestial Army route—in all three hundred thousand troops to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: The Turks besieged Ji and Tan. Wu Chonggui was made supreme commander of the central Celestial Army route, Shazha Zhongyi of the western route, and Zhang Renyan of the eastern route—three hundred thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 右羽林大將軍閻敬容、李多祚為天兵西道後軍總管，兵亦十五萬。

translations.literal: Right Forest Guard General Yan Jingrong and Li Duozuo were rear-army supreme commanders of the western Celestial Army route—also a hundred fifty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingrong and Li Duozuo commanded a hundred fifty thousand as rear guard of the western route.

sentences.zh: 默啜破蔚州飛狐，進殘定州，殺刺史孫彥高，焚廬舍，鄉聚為空。

translations.literal: Mokchur broke through Feihu in Yu Prefecture, advanced to ravage Ding Prefecture, killed Prefect Sun Yangao, burned dwellings, and villages were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur broke through Feihu in Yu Prefecture, ravaged Ding Prefecture, killed Prefect Sun Yangao, burned settlements, and emptied the countryside.

sentences.zh: 後怒，下詔購斬默啜者王之，更號曰斬啜。

translations.literal: The empress was angry and decreed that whoever beheaded Mokchur would be enfeoffed as king; his name was changed to Zhanchuo.
translations.idiomatic: The empress offered kingship to whoever beheaded Mokchur and renamed him Zhanchuo.

sentences.zh: 虜圍趙州，長史唐波若應之，入殺刺史高睿，進攻相州。

translations.literal: The barbarians besieged Zhao Prefecture; Chief Administrator Tang Boruo colluded with them, entered and killed Prefect Gao Rui, and advanced to attack Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks besieged Zhao Prefecture. Chief Administrator Tang Boruo colluded with them, entered the city, killed Prefect Gao Rui, and advanced on Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔沙咤忠義為河北道前軍總管，李多祚為後軍總管，將軍嵎夷公福富順為奇兵總管，擊虜。

translations.literal: An edict made Shazha Zhongyi front-army supreme commander of the Hebei route, Li Duozuo rear-army supreme commander, and General Yiyi Gong Fufushun odd-army supreme commander to strike the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Shazha Zhongyi was made front-army commander of the Hebei route, Li Duozuo rear-army commander, and Fufushun odd-army commander.

sentences.zh: 時中宗還自房陵，為皇太子，拜行軍大元帥，以納言狄仁傑為副，文昌右丞宋玄爽為長史，左肅政臺御史中丞霍獻可為司馬，右肅政臺御史中丞吉頊為監軍使，將軍扶余文宣等六人為子總管。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongzong had returned from Fangling as crown prince and was appointed grand marshal of the campaign; Remonstrance Counselor Di Renjie was deputy, Co-Equalizing Director Song Xuanshuang chief administrator, Left Censorate Censor-in-Chief Huo Xianke marshal, Right Censorate Censor-in-Chief Ji Xu army inspector, and Generals Fuyu Wenxuan and six others sub-commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhongzong, recently returned from exile, was made grand campaign marshal with Di Renjie as deputy, Song Xuanshuang as chief administrator, Huo Xianke as marshal, Ji Xu as inspector, and Fuyu Wenxuan and six others as sub-commanders.

sentences.zh: 未行，默啜聞之，取趙、定所掠男女八九萬悉坑之，出五回道去，所過人畜、金幣、子女盡剽有之，諸將皆顧望不敢戰，獨狄仁傑以兵追之，不及。

translations.literal: Before they marched Mokchur heard of it, took eighty or ninety thousand men and women plundered from Zhao and Ding and buried them alive, departed by the Wuhui route, plundering all people, livestock, gold, coins, and children along the way; generals all looked on and dared not fight—only Di Renjie pursued but could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Before they marched Mokchur heard the news. He buried alive eighty or ninety thousand captives from Zhao and Ding, withdrew by the Wuhui route, plundering everything in his path. Generals dared not fight; only Di Renjie pursued but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 默啜負勝輕中國，有驕志，大抵兵與頡利時略等，地縱廣萬里，諸蕃悉往聽命。

translations.literal: Mokchur, buoyed by victory and underestimating China, had an arrogant will; his troops were roughly equal to Jieli's era and his territory stretched ten thousand li—all barbarian peoples went to obey his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Confident after victory and contemptuous of China, Mokchur's armies rivaled Jieli's and his domain stretched ten thousand li. All tribal peoples obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 復立咄悉匐為左察，骨咄祿子默矩為右察，皆統兵二萬；

translations.literal: He again established Tuxibo as Left Overseer and Kutlug's son Moju as Right Overseer, each commanding twenty thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: He made Tuxibo Left Overseer and Kutlug's son Moju Right Overseer, each commanding twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 子匐俱為小可汗，位兩察上，典處木昆等十姓兵四萬，號拓西可汗。

translations.literal: His son Fuju was lesser khan, ranking above the two overseers, governing forty thousand troops of the ten surnames including Chumukun—styled Elteber Khan of the West.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuju became lesser khan above the two overseers, commanding forty thousand men of the ten surnames including Chumukun as Elteber Khan of the West.

sentences.zh: 歲入邊，戍兵不得休，乃高選魏元忠檢校并州長史為天兵軍大總管，婁師德副之，按屯以待。

translations.literal: Yearly border raids gave garrison troops no rest; Wei Yuanzhong was highly selected as inspector-general of Bingzhou chief administrator and supreme commander of the Celestial Army, with Lou Shide as deputy, to inspect encampments and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Annual raids gave frontier garrisons no rest. Wei Yuanzhong was made inspector-general of Bingzhou and supreme commander of the Celestial Army, with Lou Shide as deputy, to organize defenses.

sentences.zh: 又徙元忠靈武道行軍大總管，備虜。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was again moved to supreme commander of the Lingwu mobile campaign route to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was transferred to supreme commander of the Lingwu route.

sentences.zh: 默啜剽隴右牧馬萬匹去，俄復盜邊，詔安北大都護相王為天兵道大元帥，率并州長史武攸宜、夏州都督薛訥與元忠擊虜，兵未出，默啜去。

translations.literal: Mokchur plundered ten thousand horses from Longyou pastures and departed; soon he raided the border again; an edict made Grand Protector of the Pacified North Prince of Xiang supreme commander of the Celestial Army route, leading Bingzhou Chief Administrator Wu Youyi, Xia Prefecture Protector Xue Ne, and Yuanzhong to strike the barbarians; before troops marched Mokchur withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur stole ten thousand horses from Longyou pastures. He raided again soon after. Prince of Xiang was made supreme commander with Wu Youyi, Xue Ne, and Yuanzhong—but Mokchur withdrew before they marched.

sentences.zh: 明年，寇鹽、夏，掠羊馬十萬，攻石嶺，遂圍并州。

translations.literal: The next year he raided Yan and Xia, plundered a hundred thousand sheep and horses, attacked Shiling, and besieged Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he raided Yan and Xia, seized a hundred thousand sheep and horses, attacked Shiling, and besieged Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以雍州長史薛季昶為持節山東防禦大使，節度滄、瀛、幽、易、恒、定、媯、檀、平等九州之軍，以瀛州都督張仁亶統諸州及清夷、障塞軍之兵，與季昶掎角，又以相王為安北道行軍元帥，監諸將，王留不行。

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture Chief Administrator Xue Jichang was made defense commissioner of Shandong bearing credentials, commanding armies of nine prefectures; Ying Prefecture Protector Zhang Renyan commanded those prefectures plus Qingyi and barrier garrison troops to coordinate with Jichang; Prince of Xiang was also made mobile-campaign grand marshal of the Pacified North route supervising generals—the prince remained and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jichang was made Shandong defense commissioner over nine prefectures. Zhang Renyan commanded Qingyi and barrier garrisons in support. Prince of Xiang was named Pacified North grand marshal but did not take the field.

sentences.zh: 虜入代、忻，仍殺略。

translations.literal: The barbarians entered Dai and Xin and continued killing and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks entered Dai and Xin and continued to kill and plunder.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，遣使者莫賀達幹請進女女皇太子子，後使平恩郡王重俊、義興郡王重明盛服立諸朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an Mokchur sent envoy Mohedagan requesting to offer his daughter to the crown prince; the empress had Princes Chongjun of Ping'en and Chongming of Yixing stand in full regalia at court.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 3 Mokchur sent Mohedagan to offer his daughter to the crown prince. Empress Wu had Princes Chongjun and Chongming appear in full regalia.

sentences.zh: 默啜更遣大酋移力貪汗獻馬千匹，謝許婚，後渥禮其使。

translations.literal: Mokchur again sent the great chief Yilibahan with a thousand horses thanking them for the betrothal; the empress richly treated the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur sent the great chief Yilibahan with a thousand horses in thanks for the betrothal. The empress treated the envoy generously.

sentences.zh: 中宗始即位，入攻嗚沙，於是靈武軍大總管沙咤忠義與戰，不勝，死者幾萬人，虜遂入原、會，多取牧馬。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong first ascended he attacked Wusha; Lingwu Army supreme commander Shazha Zhongyi fought them but was unsuccessful—nearly ten thousand died—and the barbarians entered Yuan and Hui and took many pasture horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended, Mokchur attacked Wusha. Shazha Zhongyi was defeated with nearly ten thousand dead. The Turks entered Yuan and Hui and seized pasture horses.

sentences.zh: 帝詔絕昏，購斬默啜者王以國、官諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed breaking off the marriage and offered kingship and Guard General rank to whoever beheaded Mokchur.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor broke off the marriage and offered kingship and Guard General rank for Mokchur's head.

sentences.zh: 默啜殺我行人鴻臚卿臧思言，詔左屯衛大將軍張仁亶為朔方道大總管屯邊。

translations.literal: Mokchur killed our envoy Chief Minister of Guests Zang Siyan; an edict made Left Garrison Guard General Zhang Renyan supreme commander of the Shuofang route to encamp on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur killed the envoy Zang Siyan. Zhang Renyan was made supreme commander of the Shuofang route.

sentences.zh: 明年，始築三受降城於河外，障絕寇路。

translations.literal: The next year the three Surrender Reception cities were first built beyond the river to block raiding routes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the three Surrender Reception cities were built beyond the river to block raiding routes.

sentences.zh: 久之，以唐休璟代屯。

translations.literal: After long time Tang Xiujing replaced him in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Tang Xiujing replaced him on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 睿宗初立，又請和親，詔取宋王成器女為金山公主下嫁。

translations.literal: When Ruizong first succeeded he again requested marriage; an edict took Prince of Song Chengqi's daughter Princess Jinshan for marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded Mokchur again sought marriage. Princess Jinshan, daughter of Prince Chengqui of Song, was betrothed to him.

sentences.zh: 會左羽林大將軍孫佺等與奚戰冷陘，為奚所執，獻諸默啜，默啜殺之，更以刑部尚書郭元振代休璟。

translations.literal: When Left Forest Guard General Sun Yan and others fought the Xi at Lengling they were captured by the Xi and presented to Mokchur, who killed them; Minister of Punishments Guo Yuanzhen replaced Xiujing.
translations.idiomatic: General Sun Yan and others were captured by the Xi at Lengling and handed to Mokchur, who killed them. Guo Yuanzhen replaced Xiujing.

sentences.zh: 玄宗立，絕和親。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong succeeded he ended marriage alliances.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong succeeded he ended marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃遣子楊我支特勒入宿衛，固求昏，以蜀王女南和縣主妻之，下書諭尉可汗。

translations.literal: Mokchur then sent his son Yang Wozhi tegin to serve on palace guard, urgently requesting marriage; the Prince of Shu's daughter Princess Nanhe was given him as wife and a letter was sent instructing the khan.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur sent his son Yang Wozhi tegin to palace guard and pressed for marriage. Princess Nanhe of Shu was given as his wife.

sentences.zh: 明年，使子移涅可汗引同俄特勒、火拔頡利發石失畢精騎攻北庭，都護郭虔瓘擊之，斬同俄城下，虜奔解。

translations.literal: The next year his son Yinen Khan led Tong'e tegin, Hubo Irli Fa, and Shibi elite cavalry to attack Beiting; Protector Guo Qianzhen struck them and beheaded Tong'e below the walls; the barbarians fled in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his son Yinen Khan led Tong'e tegin and elite cavalry against Beiting. Guo Qianzhen beheaded Tong'e below the walls and routed them.

sentences.zh: 火拔不敢歸，攜妻子來奔，拜左武衛大將軍、燕山郡王，號其妻為金山公主，賜賫優縟。

translations.literal: Hubo dared not return, came fleeing with wife and children, was appointed Left Martial Guard General and Prince of Yanshan Commandery, his wife styled Princess Jinshan, and gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Hubo dared not return and fled with his family. He was made Left Martial Guard General and Prince of Yanshan; his wife was styled Princess Jinshan and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 楊我支死，詔宗親三等以上吊其家。

translations.literal: When Yang Wozhi died an edict ordered third-rank clansmen and above to mourn at his house.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wozhi died, third-rank clansmen and above were ordered to mourn at his house.

sentences.zh: 是時突厥再上書求昏，帝未報。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks again sent a letter requesting marriage; the emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks again requested marriage by letter. The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 初，景雲中，默啜西滅娑葛，遂役屬契丹、奚，因虐用其下。

translations.literal: At first in the Jingyun era Mokchur destroyed Suoge in the west and then made the Khitan and Xi serve and submit, thereby cruelly exploiting his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era Mokchur destroyed Suoge in the west and subjugated the Khitan and Xi, cruelly exploiting his subjects.

sentences.zh: 既年老，愈昏暴，部落怨畔。

translations.literal: As he aged he grew ever more muddled and violent and tribes resented and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: As he aged he grew more brutal. Tribes resented and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十姓左五咄陸、右五弩失畢俟斤皆請降。

translations.literal: The ten surnames' left five Tulu and right five Nushibi irkin all requested to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The ten surnames—the five Tulu on the left and five Nushibi on the right—all sought to submit.

sentences.zh: 葛邏祿、胡屋、鼠尼施三姓，大漠都督特進朱斯，陰山都督謀落匐雞，玄池都督蹋實力胡鼻率眾內附；

translations.literal: The Geluolu, Huwu, and Shunishi three surnames, Grand Protector of the Great Desert Special Grand Master Zhu Si, Grand Protector of the Yin Mountains Mulu Fuge, and Grand Protector of the Dark Pool Tabishi Hubi led their hosts to submit internally;
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu, Huwu, and Shunishi, with Grand Protectors Zhu Si, Mulu Fuge, and Tabishi Hubi, submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 詔處其眾於金山。

translations.literal: An edict settled their hosts at the Altai Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: They were settled at the Altai Mountains.

sentences.zh: 以右羽林軍大將軍薛訥為涼州鎮軍大總管，節度赤水、建康、河源等軍，屯涼州，以都督楊執一副之：右衛大將軍郭虔瓘為朔州鎮軍大總管，節度和戎、大武、并州之北等軍，屯并州，以長史王晙副之。

translations.literal: Right Forest Guard General Xue Ne was made grand commander of the Liangzhou garrison army, commanding Chishui, Jianchang, Heyuan, and other armies, encamping at Liangzhou with Protector Yang Zhiyi as deputy; Right Guard General Guo Qianzhen was made grand commander of the Shuozhou garrison army, commanding Herong, Dawu, and armies north of Bing Prefecture, encamping at Bing Prefecture with Chief Administrator Wang Jun as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne was made grand commander at Liangzhou with Yang Zhiyi as deputy. Guo Qianzhen was made grand commander at Bing Prefecture with Wang Jun as deputy.

sentences.zh: 撫新附，檢鈔暴。

translations.literal: They soothed the newly submitted and inspected and restrained violence.
translations.idiomatic: They pacified the new submitters and restrained raids.

sentences.zh: 默啜屢擊葛邏祿等，詔在所都護、總管掎角應援。

translations.literal: Mokchur repeatedly struck the Geluolu and others; edicts ordered protectorate generals everywhere to coordinate pincer support.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur repeatedly attacked the Geluolu. Protectorate commanders were ordered to support them.

sentences.zh: 虜勢浸削。

translations.literal: Barbarian power gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: Turkish power gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 其婿高麗莫離支高文簡，與𨁂|⻊夾跌都督思太，吐谷渾大酋慕容道奴，郁射施大酋鶻屈頡斤、悉頡力，高麗大酋高拱毅，合萬餘帳相踵款邊，詔內之河南；

translations.literal: His son-in-law Goguryeo Moliji Gao Wenjian, Ba (Tiele) Protector Si Tai, Tuyuhun great chief Murong Daonu, Yujue great chiefs Huqu Irkin and Xi Irli, and Goguryeo great chief Gao Gongyi—in all more than ten thousand tents—came in succession to submit at the border; an edict settled them south of the river;
translations.idiomatic: His son-in-law Gao Wenjian of Goguryeo, Ba Protector Si Tai, Murong Daonu of Tuyuhun, Huqu Irkin and Xi Irli of Yujue, and Gao Gongyi of Goguryeo—more than ten thousand tents—submitted in succession and were settled south of the river.

sentences.zh: 引拜文簡左衛大將軍、遼西郡王，思太特進、右衛大將軍兼𨁂|⻊夾跌都督、樓煩郡公，道奴左武衛將軍兼刺史、雲中郡公，鶻屈頡斤左驍衛將軍兼刺史、陰山郡公，悉頡力左武衛將軍兼刺史、雁門郡公，拱毅左領軍衛將軍兼刺史、平城郡公，將軍皆員外置，賜各有差。

translations.literal: Wenjian was appointed Left Guard General and Prince of Liaoxi Commandery; Si Tai Special Grand Master, Right Guard General and concurrent Ba Protector, Duke of Loufan Commandery; Daonu Left Martial Guard General and concurrent prefect, Duke of Yunzhong Commandery; Huqu Irkin Left Martial Guard General and concurrent prefect, Duke of Yinshan Commandery; Xi Irli Left Martial Guard General and concurrent prefect, Duke of Yanmen Commandery; Gongyi Left Army Guard General and concurrent prefect, Duke of Pingcheng Commandery—all generals were supernumerary appointments with gifts differing in degree.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjian was made Left Guard General and Prince of Liaoxi; Si Tai Special Grand Master, Right Guard General, Ba Protector, and Duke of Loufan; Daonu Left Martial Guard General and Duke of Yunzhong; Huqu Irkin Left Martial Guard General and Duke of Yinshan; Xi Irli Left Martial Guard General and Duke of Yanmen; Gongyi Left Army Guard General and Duke of Pingcheng—all supernumerary, with gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 默啜討九姓，戰磧北，九姓潰，人畜皆死，思結等部來降，帝悉官之。

translations.literal: Mokchur attacked the Nine Surnames; fighting north of the desert the Nine Surnames were routed; people and livestock all died; Sijie and other divisions came to submit and the emperor all gave them offices.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur attacked the Nine Surnames north of the desert and routed them. The Sijie and others submitted and received offices.

sentences.zh: 拜薛訥朔方道行軍大總管，太僕卿呂延祚、靈州刺史杜賓客佐之，備邊。

translations.literal: Xue Ne was appointed supreme commander of the Shuofang mobile campaign route with Vice Minister of Imperial Stud Lu Yanzuo and Ling Prefecture Inspector Du Binke assisting to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne was made supreme commander of the Shuofang route with Lu Yanzuo and Du Binke to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 詔金山、大漠、陰山、玄池都督等共圖取默啜，班賞格，賜物諭之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grand protectors of Jinshan, Great Desert, Yin Mountains, and Dark Pool jointly to plan capturing Mokchur; reward regulations were promulgated and gifts sent to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand protectors of Jinshan, Great Desert, Yin Mountains, and Dark Pool were ordered to capture Mokchur, with published rewards.

sentences.zh: 默啜又討九姓拔野古，戰獨樂河，拔野古大敗，默啜輕歸不為備，道大林中，拔曳固殘眾突出，擊默啜，斬之，乃與入蕃使郝靈佺傳首京師。

translations.literal: Mokchur again attacked the Nine Surname Bayegu; fighting at the Dule River the Bayegu were greatly defeated; Mokchur returned lightly without precautions; in a great forest Bayegu remnant troops suddenly burst out, struck Mokchur, and beheaded him; together with the envoy to the barbarians Hao Lingqian they sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur attacked the Bayegu at the Dule River and routed them. Returning carelessly through a forest, Bayegu remnants ambushed and beheaded him. The envoy Hao Lingqian sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿子闕特勒合故部，攻殺小可汗及宗族略盡，立其兄默棘連，是為毗伽可汗。

translations.literal: Kutlug's son Kül Tigin gathered the old divisions, attacked and killed the lesser khan and clansmen nearly to extinction, and established his elder brother Mojilian—this was Bilge Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug's son Kül Tigin rallied the old tribes, killed the lesser khan and nearly all the royal clan, and enthroned his brother Mojilian as Bilge Khan.

sentences.zh: 25%◎突厥下毗伽可汗毗伽可汗毗伽可汗默棘連|默棘連，本謂「小殺」者，性仁友，自以立非己功，讓於闕特勒，特勒不敢受，遂嗣位，實開元四年。

translations.literal: Mojilian—subsection Turks Part 2, Bilge Khan—originally called 'lesser she,' was benevolent and friendly by nature; believing enthronement was not his own achievement he yielded to Kül Tigin; Tigin dared not accept and he therefore succeeded—in fact the fourth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian—called "lesser she"—was benevolent by nature. Believing the throne was not his own achievement, he yielded to Kül Tigin, who refused. Mojilian succeeded—in Kaiyuan 4.

sentences.zh: 以特勒為左賢王，專制其兵。

translations.literal: Tigin was made Left Wise King with sole command of their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kül Tigin was made Left Wise King with sole command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 初，默啜死，闕特勒盡殺其用事臣，惟暾欲谷者以女婆匐為默棘連可敦，獨免，廢歸其部。

translations.literal: At first when Mokchur died Kül Tigin killed all his active ministers; only Ton Yugu was spared because his daughter Bopo was Mojilian's khatun—he was dismissed and returned to his division.
translations.idiomatic: When Mokchur died Kül Tigin killed his ministers. Only Ton Yugu was spared because his daughter Bopo was Mojilian's khatun. He was dismissed to his tribe.

sentences.zh: 後突騎施蘇祿自為可汗，突厥部種多貳，默棘連乃召暾欲谷與謀國，年七十餘，眾尊畏之。

translations.literal: Later when the Turgesh Suluk proclaimed himself khan many Turkish divisions wavered; Mojilian therefore summoned Ton Yugu to counsel on state affairs—he was over seventy and all revered and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turgesh Suluk proclaimed himself khan many Turks wavered. Mojilian recalled Ton Yugu, over seventy and universally revered, to counsel on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄而𨁂|⻊夾跌思太等自河曲歸之。

translations.literal: Soon Ba Si Tai and others returned from the river bend to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Si Tai of the Ba tribe and others returned from the river bend.

sentences.zh: 始，降戶之南也，單于副都護張知運盡斂其兵，戎人怨怒；

translations.literal: At first when surrendered households moved south Deputy Protector of the Chanyu Zhang Zhiyun confiscated all their weapons and the warriors resented and raged;
translations.idiomatic: When surrendered households moved south, Deputy Protector Zhang Zhiyun confiscated all their weapons and they grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 及姜晦為巡邊使，遮訴禁弓矢無以射獵為生，晦悉還之。

translations.literal: When Jiang Hui became border inspection envoy they petitioned that forbidding bows and arrows left them no means to hunt for livelihood; Hui fully returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Border inspector Jiang Hui restored their bows when they petitioned that the ban left them unable to hunt.

sentences.zh: 乃共擊張知運，禽之，將送突厥；

translations.literal: They jointly struck Zhang Zhiyun, captured him, and were about to send him to the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Zhang Zhiyun, captured him, and prepared to deliver him to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 朔方行軍總管薛訥、將軍郭知運追之，眾潰，釋知運去。

translations.literal: Shuofang mobile campaign supreme commander Xue Ne and General Guo Zhiyun pursued them; the host scattered and released Zhiyun.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ne and Guo Zhiyun pursued. The rebels scattered and released Zhiyun.

sentences.zh: 思太等分為二隊北走，王晙又破其左隊。

translations.literal: Si Tai and others divided into two columns fleeing north; Wang Jun again defeated their left column.
translations.idiomatic: Si Tai and others fled north in two columns. Wang Jun defeated the left column.

sentences.zh: 默棘連既得降胡，欲南盜塞，暾欲谷曰：「不可，天子英武，人和歲豐，未有間，且我兵新集，不可動也。

translations.literal: Mojilian having obtained the surrendered Hu wished to raid the passes south; Ton Yugu said: "It cannot be done—the Son of Heaven is heroic, the people harmonious and the year abundant, there is no opening, and moreover our troops are newly gathered and cannot move."
translations.idiomatic: Having gained the surrendered Hu, Mojilian wished to raid the frontier. Ton Yugu said: "We cannot. The emperor is formidable, the realm prosperous, and our armies are newly gathered."

sentences.zh: 」默棘連又欲城所都，起佛、老廟，暾欲谷曰：「突厥眾不敵唐百分一，所能與抗者，隨水草射獵，居處無常，習於武事，強則進取，弱則遁伏，唐兵雖多，無所用也。

translations.literal: Mojilian again wished to fortify his capital and erect Buddhist and Daoist temples; Ton Yugu said: "Turkish hosts are not one hundredth of Tang's; what lets us resist is following water and grass to hunt, dwelling without fixed place, practiced in martial affairs—strong then advance and seize, weak then flee and hide—Tang troops though many are useless."
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian wished to build a capital and erect Buddhist and Daoist temples. Ton Yugu said: "We are not one hundredth of Tang's strength. Our strength is mobility—following pasture, hunting, advancing when strong and fleeing when weak. Tang's vast armies cannot touch us."

sentences.zh: 若城而居，戰一敗，必為彼禽。

translations.literal: If they fortify cities and dwell therein, one defeat and they will surely be captured by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If they build cities and settle in them, one defeat and they will be captured.

sentences.zh: 且佛、老教人仁弱，非武強術。

translations.literal: Moreover Buddhism and Daoism teach people benevolence and weakness—not arts of martial strength."
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism teach gentleness, not martial strength."

sentences.zh: 」默棘連當其策，即遣使者請和。

translations.literal: Mojilian followed his counsel and immediately sent envoys requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian took his advice and sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 帝以不情，答而不許。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it insincere, replied but did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed the overture insincere and refused.

sentences.zh: 俄下詔伐之，乃以拔悉蜜右驍衛大將軍金山道總管處木昆執米啜、堅昆都督右武衛大將軍骨篤祿毗伽可汗、契丹都督李失活、奚都督李大酺、突厥默啜子左賢王墨特勒、左威衛將軍右賢王阿史那毗伽特勒、燕山郡王火拔石失畢等蕃漢士悉發，凡三十萬，以御史大夫、朔方道大總管王晙統之，期八年秋並集稽落水上，使拔悉蜜、奚、契丹分道掩其牙，捕默棘連。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered a campaign; Baximi Right Martial Guard General and Jinshan route supreme commander Chumukun Zhimi Qie, Kirghiz Protector and Right Martial Guard General Gutulu Bilge Khan, Khitan Protector Li Shihuo, Xi Protector Li Datong, Mokchur's son Left Wise King Mo tegin, Left Guard General Right Wise King Ashina Bilge tegin, Prince of Yanshan Commandery Hubo Shibi, and all barbarian and Chinese troops were mobilized—in all three hundred thousand—under Censor-in-Chief and Shuofang route supreme commander Wang Jun, to assemble on the Jiluo River in the eighth year's autumn; Baximi, Xi, and Khitan were to strike the headquarters by separate routes and capture Mojilian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized three hundred thousand men under Wang Jun—including Baximi, Kirghiz, Khitan, Xi, and Turkish princes—to converge on the Jiluo River in autumn of the eighth year and capture Mojilian by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 默棘連大恐，暾欲谷曰：「拔悉蜜在北庭，與二蕃相距遠，必不合。

translations.literal: Mojilian was greatly afraid; Ton Yugu said: "Baximi is at Beiting, far from the two barbarian peoples—they surely will not unite."
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian was terrified. Ton Yugu said: "Baximi at Beiting is too far from the other tribes—they will not unite."

sentences.zh: 晙與張嘉貞有隙，必相執異，亦必不能來。

translations.literal: Jun and Zhang Jiazhen have a rift—they will surely hold each other in check and also surely cannot come."
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Zhang Jiazhen are at odds—they will not cooperate and may not come at all."

sentences.zh: 即皆能來，我當前三日悉眾北徙，彼糧竭自去。

translations.literal: Even if all can come, I shall three days beforehand move the entire host north; when their grain is exhausted they will leave on their own."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they all come, we move north three days ahead. When their supplies run out they will withdraw."

sentences.zh: 拔悉蜜輕而好利，當先至，擊之可取也。

translations.literal: Baximi is light and greedy for profit—they will arrive first; strike them and they can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Baximi is rash and greedy. They will arrive first—we can defeat them."

sentences.zh: 」俄而拔悉蜜果引眾逼突厥牙，知晙等不至，乃引卻，突厥欲擊之，暾欲谷曰：「兵千里遠出，士殊死鬥，鋒不可當也。

translations.literal: Soon Baximi indeed led troops pressing the Turkish headquarters; learning Jun and others would not come they withdrew; the Turks wished to strike them; Ton Yugu said: "Troops coming a thousand li will fight desperately—their edge cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Baximi pressed the Turkish camp but withdrew when Jun failed to appear. The Turks wanted to attack, but Ton Yugu said: "They marched a thousand li and will fight desperately—we should not meet them head-on."

sentences.zh: 不如躡之，邀近而取之。

translations.literal: Better to follow them and intercept when they are near and take them."
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow and ambush them when they are near."

sentences.zh: 」距北庭二百里，乃分兵由它道襲拔其城，即急擊拔悉蜜，眾走趨北庭，無所歸，悉禽之。

translations.literal: Two hundred li from Beiting they divided troops by another route to raid and seize their city, then swiftly struck Baximi; the host fled toward Beiting with nowhere to return—all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li from Beiting they seized Baximi's city by a detour, then routed Baximi's army. The survivors fled to Beiting and were all captured.

sentences.zh: 還出赤亭，掠涼州，都督楊敬述使官屬盧公利、元澄等勒兵討捕，暾欲谷曰：「敬述若城守，當與和。

translations.literal: Returning they emerged at Chiting and raided Liang Prefecture; Protector Yang Jingshu sent officials Lu Gongli and Yuan Cheng to lead troops to pursue and capture; Ton Yugu said: "If Jingshu holds the city we should make peace."
translations.idiomatic: On the return they raided Liang Prefecture. Yang Jingshu sent Lu Gongli and Yuan Cheng against them. Ton Yugu said: "If Jingshu holds his walls we should negotiate."

sentences.zh: 如兵出，吾且決戰，必有功。

translations.literal: If troops come out we shall fight decisively and surely gain merit."
translations.idiomatic: If he sallies out we will fight and win."

sentences.zh: 」澄令於軍曰：「裸臂持滿外註。

translations.literal: Cheng ordered in the army: "Bare arms, draw bows fully, and aim outward."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng ordered his men: "Bare your arms, draw full bows, and aim outward."

sentences.zh: 」會大寒裂膚，士手不能張弓矢，由是大敗，元澄走，敬述坐以白衣檢校涼州事，突厥遂大振，盡有默啜餘眾。

translations.literal: Severe cold split the skin; soldiers' hands could not open bows and arrows; thereby they were greatly defeated; Yuan Cheng fled; Jingshu was punished by serving in plain clothes as acting Liang Prefecture affairs; the Turks then flourished greatly and possessed all Mokchur's remnant host.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter cold split their skin; men could not draw their bows. Tang forces were routed. Cheng fled and Jingshu was demoted. The Turks revived and absorbed Mokchur's remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 明年，固乞和，請父事天子，許之。

translations.literal: The next year he urgently begged for peace and asked to treat the Son of Heaven as a father; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he begged for peace and asked to treat the emperor as a father. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又連歲遣使獻方物求婚。

translations.literal: Again for successive years he sent envoys presenting local products and requesting marriage.
translations.idiomatic: For years he sent tribute and marriage requests.

sentences.zh: 是時天子東巡泰山，中書令張說謀益屯以備突厥，兵部郎中裴光庭曰：「封禪以告成功，若復調發，不可謂成功者。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was touring Mount Tai in the east; Secretariat Director Zhang Yue plotted to increase garrisons against the Turks; Ministry of War Director Pei Guangting said: "The feng and shan rites announce success—if we mobilize again we cannot call it success."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor toured Mount Tai, Zhang Yue proposed reinforcing garrisons. Pei Guangting objected: "The feng and shan rites celebrate success—fresh mobilization would contradict that."

sentences.zh: 」說曰：「突厥雖請和，難以信結也。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Though the Turks request peace, it is hard to bind them with trust."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue replied: "Turkish peace offers cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 且其可汗仁而愛人，下為之用，闕特勒善戰，暾欲谷沈雄，愈老而智，李靖、世勣流也，三虜方協，知我舉國東巡，有如乘間，何以禦之？

translations.literal: Moreover their khan is benevolent and loves people—subordinates serve him; Kül Tigin is skilled in battle; Ton Yugu is deep and bold, wiser as he ages—men of Li Jing and Li Shiji's stamp; the three barbarians now cooperate—knowing our whole state tours east, if they seize the moment how can we withstand them?"
translations.idiomatic: Their khan is benevolent and beloved; Kül Tigin is a fierce warrior; Ton Yugu grows wiser with age—rivals to Li Jing and Li Shiji. With all three united, they could strike while we tour the east."

sentences.zh: 」光庭即請以使召其大臣入衛，乃遣鴻臚卿袁振往諭帝意。

translations.literal: Guangting then requested summoning their great ministers to palace guard by envoy; Yuan Zhen of the Chief Minister of Guests was sent to explain the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting proposed summoning Turkish ministers to court as hostages. Yuan Zhen was sent to explain the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 默棘連置酒與可敦、闕特勒、暾欲谷坐帳中，謂振曰：「吐蕃，犬出也，唐與為昏；

translations.literal: Mojilian set wine and with the khatun, Kül Tigin, and Ton Yugu sat in the tent and told Zhen: "Tibet is born of dogs—Tang marries to them;"
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian feasted with his khatun, Kül Tigin, and Ton Yugu and told Yuan Zhen: "Tibetans are dogs, yet Tang gives them princesses;"

sentences.zh: 奚、契丹，我奴而役也，亦尚主；

translations.literal: the Xi and Khitan are my slaves whom I employ—yet they too receive imperial daughters;"
translations.idiomatic: the Xi and Khitan are my slaves, yet they too receive princesses;"

sentences.zh: 獨突厥前後請，不許，云何？

translations.literal: only the Turks have repeatedly requested and been refused—how is this?"
translations.idiomatic: yet the Turks alone are repeatedly refused. Why?"

sentences.zh: 」振曰：「可汗，天子子也，子而昏，可乎？

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Khan, the Son of Heaven is a son—can a son marry his own?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen replied: "The Son of Heaven is like a son to his people—can a son marry within the family?"

sentences.zh: 」默棘連曰：「不然，二蕃皆賜姓，而得尚主，何不可云？

translations.literal: Mojilian said: "Not so—the two barbarians were granted surnames and could receive imperial daughters—why may it not be said?"
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian retorted: "Those tribes were granted surnames and received princesses. Why not us?"

sentences.zh: 且公主亦非帝女，我不敢有所擇，但屢請不得，為諸國笑。

translations.literal: Moreover the princess is not the emperor's daughter—I dare not be choosy; but repeated requests denied make us the laughingstock of all states."
translations.idiomatic: And we do not demand the emperor's own daughter—we only ask not to be the laughingstock of the world."

sentences.zh: 」振許為請，默棘連遣大臣阿史德頡利發入獻，遂從封禪。

translations.literal: Zhen promised to request it; Mojilian sent the great minister Ashina Irli Fa to present tribute and then followed the feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen promised to petition. Mojilian sent Ashina Irli Fa with tribute to attend the feng and shan ceremony.

sentences.zh: 有詔四夷諸酋皆入仗佩弓矢，會兔起帝馬前，帝一發斃之，頡利發奉兔頓首賀曰：「陛下神武超絕，若天上則臣不知，人間無有也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all barbarian chiefs to enter the guard bearing bows and arrows; a hare started before the emperor's horse and the emperor shot it dead with one arrow; Irli Fa presented the hare and bowed in congratulation: "Your Majesty's divine martial prowess is supreme—if in Heaven your servant knows not, among men there is none."
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian chiefs entered guard with bows. A hare bolted before the emperor's horse; he killed it with one shot. Irli Fa prostrated himself: "Your Majesty's archery surpasses all mortal men."

sentences.zh: 」詔問：「饑欲食乎？

translations.literal: An edict asked: "Are you hungry and wish to eat?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Are you hungry?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「仰觀弧矢之威，使十日不食猶為飽。

translations.literal: He replied: "Beholding the might of bow and arrow, even ten days without food I would still be full."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Seeing Your Majesty's archery, I could fast ten days and still feel sated."

sentences.zh: 」因令仗內馳射。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was ordered to gallop and shoot within the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then invited to demonstrate his riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 扈封畢，厚宴賜遣之，然卒不許和親。

translations.literal: After escort duties at the feng rites were complete they were richly feasted, gifted, and sent away—yet marriage alliance was ultimately not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony they were feasted and sent home—but marriage was still denied.

sentences.zh: 自是比年遣大臣入朝，吐蕃以書約與連和鈔邊，默棘連不敢從，封上其書，天子嘉之，引使者梅錄啜宴紫宸殿，詔朔方西受降城許互市，歲賜帛數十萬。

translations.literal: From this for successive years great ministers entered court; Tibet sent letters proposing joint raids on the border; Mojilian dared not follow and sealed the letter and sent it up—the Son of Heaven praised this, summoned the envoy Meluo Qie to feast in Zichen Hall, decreed mutual markets at Shuofang's western Surrender Reception city, and yearly bestowed several hundred thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Turkish ministers came annually. Tibet proposed joint raids; Mojilian refused and forwarded the letter. The emperor rewarded him, feasted envoy Meluo Qie, opened markets at the western Surrender Reception city, and granted silk yearly.

sentences.zh: 十九年，闕特勒死，使金吾將軍張去逸、都官郎中呂向奉璽詔吊祭，帝為刻辭於碑，仍立廟像，四垣圖戰陣狀，詔高手工六人往，繪寫精肖，其國以為未嘗有，默棘連視之，必悲梗。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Kül Tigin died; Golden Guard General Zhang Quyi and Director of Offices Lu Xiang were sent bearing imperial seals to mourn and sacrifice; the emperor composed an inscription for the stele and also erected a temple image; the four walls pictured battle scenes; an edict sent six master craftsmen to paint with exact likeness—their state thought it had never been seen; Mojilian viewing it was always grief-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Kül Tigin died. Zhang Quyi and Lu Xiang were sent to mourn. The emperor inscribed a stele and erected a temple with battle scenes painted on the walls. Mojilian wept whenever he saw it.

sentences.zh: 默棘連請昏既勤，帝許可，於是遣哥解栗必來謝，請昏期。

translations.literal: Mojilian's marriage requests had been diligent; the emperor granted approval; thereupon Geli Bi came to give thanks and set the marriage date.
translations.idiomatic: Mojilian's marriage petitions were granted. Geli Bi came to give thanks and set the date.

sentences.zh: 俄為梅錄啜所毒，忍死殺梅錄啜，夷其種，乃卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was poisoned by Meluo Qie; enduring death he killed Meluo Qie and exterminated his clan, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was poisoned by Meluo Qie. Dying, he killed Meluo Qie and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 帝為發哀，詔宗正卿李佺吊祭，因立廟，詔史官李融文其碑。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him; an edict ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Li Quan to mourn and sacrifice; a temple was erected; an edict ordered Historian Li Rong to compose the stele text.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, sent Li Quan to sacrifice, erected a temple, and had Li Rong compose the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 國人共立其子為伊然可汗。

translations.literal: The people jointly established his son as Yiran Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes enthroned his son as Yiran Khan.

sentences.zh: 伊然可汗立八年，卒。

translations.literal: Yiran Khan reigned eight years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yiran Khan reigned eight years and died.

sentences.zh: 凡遣使三入朝。

translations.literal: In all he sent envoys three times to court.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to court three times.

sentences.zh: 其弟嗣立，是為星伽骨咄祿可汗，使右金吾衛將軍李質持冊為登利可汗。

translations.literal: His younger brother succeeded—this was Qapaghan Kutlug Khan; Right Golden Guard General Li Zhi was sent bearing investiture to make him Dengli Khan.
translations.idiomatic: His brother succeeded as Qapaghan Kutlug Khan. Li Zhi invested him as Dengli Khan.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使伊難如朝正月，獻方物，曰「禮天可汗如禮天，今新歲獻月，願以萬壽獻天子」云。

translations.literal: The next year envoy Yinanru came for the first month court, presenting local products, saying: "We honor the Heaven-Khan as Heaven—now at the new year we present the moon—we wish to offer long life to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next year envoy Yinanru came for New Year with tribute: "We honor the Heaven-Khan as we honor Heaven—we bring the new moon's greeting and wish the Son of Heaven long life."

sentences.zh: 可汗幼，其母婆匐與小臣飫斯達幹亂，遂預政，諸部不協。

translations.literal: The khan was young; his mother Bopo and the minor official Yus Dagan caused disorder and therefore participated in government—the various divisions were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The young khan's mother Bopo and the official Yus Dagan meddled in government and divided the tribes.

sentences.zh: 登利從父分掌東西兵，號左右殺，士之精勁皆屬。

translations.literal: Dengli's paternal uncles separately commanded eastern and western troops—styled Left and Right She— all elite warriors submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Dengli's uncles commanded east and west armies as Left and Right She, holding the finest warriors.

sentences.zh: 可汗與母誘斬西殺，奪其兵，左殺懼，即攻登利可汗，殺之。

translations.literal: The khan and his mother lured and killed the West She and seized his troops; the Left She was afraid and attacked Dengli Khan and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The khan and his mother killed the West She and seized his army. The Left She attacked and killed Dengli Khan.

sentences.zh: 左殺者，判闕特勒也，遂立毗伽可汗子，俄為骨咄葉護所殺，立其弟，旋又殺之，葉護乃自為可汗。

translations.literal: The Left She was Pan Kül Tigin; he established Bilge Khan's son, soon killed by Kutlug Yabghu who established his brother then killed him too—Yabghu then made himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: The Left She was Pan Kül Tigin. He enthroned Bilge's son, who was killed by Kutlug Yabghu. Yabghu killed two khans in succession and made himself khan.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，其大部回紇、葛邏祿、拔悉蜜並起攻葉護，殺之，尊拔悉蜜之長為頡跌伊施可汗，於是回紇、葛邏祿自為左右葉護，亦遣使者來告。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao the great divisions Uyghur, Geluolu, and Baximi jointly attacked Yabghu and killed him, honoring the Baximi chief as Elteber Yishi Khan; thereupon Uyghur and Geluolu made themselves Left and Right Yabghu and also sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the Uyghurs, Geluolu, and Baximi killed Yabghu and made the Baximi chief Elteber Yishi Khan. The Uyghurs and Geluolu became Left and Right Yabghu and notified Tang.

sentences.zh: 國人奉判闕特勒子為烏蘇米施可汗，以其子葛臘哆為西殺。

translations.literal: The people supported Pan Kül Tigin's son as Wusu Mish Khan and made his son Geladuo West She.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes made Pan Kül Tigin's son Wusu Mish Khan, with Geladuo as West She.

sentences.zh: 帝使使者諭令內附，烏蘇不聽，其下不與，拔悉蜜等三部共攻烏蘇米施，米施遁亡。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys urging submission; Wusu refused and his subordinates would not follow; Baximi and the other three divisions jointly attacked Wusu Mish—Mish fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Tang urged Wusu Mish to submit; he refused. Baximi and the other tribes attacked him and he fled.

sentences.zh: 其西葉護阿布思及葛臘哆率五千帳降，以葛臘哆為懷恩王。

translations.literal: West Yabghu Abu Si and Geladuo led five thousand tents to submit; Geladuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Cherishing Grace.
translations.idiomatic: West Yabghu Abu Si and Geladuo surrendered with five thousand tents. Geladuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Cherishing Grace.

sentences.zh: 三載，拔悉蜜等殺烏蘇米施，傳首京師，獻太廟。

translations.literal: In the third year Baximi and others killed Wusu Mish, sent the head to the capital, and presented it at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 Baximi killed Wusu Mish and sent his head to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 其弟白眉特勒鶻隴匐立，是為白眉可汗。

translations.literal: His younger brother White-Eyebrow tegin Helong Fu established himself—this was White-Eyebrow Khan.
translations.idiomatic: His brother White-Eyebrow tegin Helong Fu became White-Eyebrow Khan.

sentences.zh: 於是突厥大亂，國人推拔悉蜜酋為可汗，詔朔方節度使王忠嗣以兵乘其亂，抵薩河內山，擊其左阿波達幹十一部，破之，獨其右未下，而回紇、葛邏祿殺拔悉蜜可汗，奉回紇骨力裴羅定其國，是為骨咄祿毗伽闕可汗。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turks fell into great disorder; the people pushed the Baximi chief as khan; an edict ordered Shuofang Military Commissioner Wang Zhongsi to exploit the chaos, reach the Sa River and Inner Mountain, strike the Left Apo Taghan's eleven divisions and break them—the right was not yet taken when Uyghur and Geluolu killed the Baximi khan and established the Uyghur chief Gulipeiluo to settle the state—this was Kutlug Bilge Que Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Turkish chaos followed. Wang Zhongsi struck eleven divisions of the Left Apo Taghan. Before he finished, the Uyghurs and Geluolu killed the Baximi khan and enthroned Gulipeiluo as Kutlug Bilge Que Khan.

sentences.zh: 明年，殺白眉可汗，傳首獻。

translations.literal: The next year they killed White-Eyebrow Khan and sent the head as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they killed White-Eyebrow Khan and sent his head to court.

sentences.zh: 毗伽可汗妻骨咄祿婆匐可敦率眾自歸，天子御花萼樓宴群臣，賦詩美其事，封可敦為賓國夫人，歲給粉直二十萬。

translations.literal: Bilge Khan's wife Kutlug Bopo Khatun led the host to submit; the Son of Heaven feasted ministers at Hua'e Tower and composed poetry praising the event; the khatun was enfeoffed as Lady of Guest State with two hundred thousand in yearly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug Bopo Khatun, Bilge Khan's widow, submitted with her people. The emperor feasted at Hua'e Tower and enfeoffed her as Lady of Guest State with an annual stipend.

sentences.zh: 始突厥國於後魏大統時，至是滅。

translations.literal: The Turkish state began under Northern Wei in the Datong era—to this it perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkish state founded under Northern Wei in the Datong era was now destroyed.

sentences.zh: 後或朝貢，皆舊部九姓云，其地盡入回紇。

translations.literal: Later when tribute came it was all from the old Nine Surnames—their lands all passed to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Later tribute came only from the old Nine Surnames; their lands passed entirely to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 始其族分國於西者，曰西突厥。

translations.literal: At first where their clan divided the state in the west was called Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Where the clan had divided westward they were called the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 西突厥西突厥，其先訥都陸之孫吐務，號大葉護。

translations.literal: Western Turks Western Turks—their ancestor was Neudou's grandson Tuwu, titled Great Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks: their ancestor was Neudou's grandson Tuwu, titled Great Yabghu.

sentences.zh: 長子曰土門伊利可汗，次子曰室點蜜，亦曰瑟帝米。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Tumen Il Khan; the second son was Shidianmi, also called Sedi Mi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Tumen Il Khan; his second was Shidianmi, also called Sedi Mi.

sentences.zh: 瑟帝米之子曰達頭可汗，亦曰步迦可汗。

translations.literal: Sedi Mi's son was Datou Khan, also called Boka Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Sedi Mi's son was Datou Khan, also Boka Khan.

sentences.zh: 始與東突厥分烏孫故地有之，東即突厥，西雷翥海，南疏勒，北瀚海，直京師北七千里，由焉耆西北七日行得南庭，北八日行得北庭，與都陸、弩失畢、歌邏祿、處月、處蜜、伊吾諸種雜。

translations.literal: At first with Eastern Turks they divided the old Wusun lands—east bordered the Turks, west the Caspian, south Kashgar, north the Hanhai Desert, seven thousand li straight north of the capital; from Yanqi northwest seven days' march reached the Southern Court, north eight days the Northern Court—mixed with Tulu, Nushibi, Geluolu, Chuyue, Chumi, Yiwu, and other peoples.
translations.idiomatic: They divided the old Wusun lands with the Eastern Turks: east to the Turks, west to the Caspian, south to Kashgar, north to the desert, seven thousand li from the capital. Seven days northwest from Yanqi lay the Southern Court; eight days north the Northern Court—mixed with Tulu, Nushibi, Geluolu, and others.

sentences.zh: 其風俗大抵突厥也，言語少異。

translations.literal: Their customs were largely Turkish; language differed slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were largely Turkish, their speech slightly different.

sentences.zh: 初，東突厥木桿可汗死，舍其子大邏便，而立弟佗缽可汗。

translations.literal: At first when Eastern Turk Mughan Khan died he passed over his son Daluobian and established his younger brother Tabo Khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Turk Mughan Khan died he skipped his son Daluobian and enthroned his brother Tabo Khan.

sentences.zh: 佗缽死，先令戒其子庵羅必立大邏便，國人以其母賤，不肯立，而卒立庵羅。

translations.literal: When Tabo died he had beforehand charged his son Anluo must establish Daluobian; the people because his mother was low would not establish him and ultimately established Anluo.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo had charged his son Anluo to restore Daluobian, but the people rejected Daluobian's low-born mother and enthroned Anluo.

sentences.zh: 庵羅後以讓木桿兄子攝圖，是為沙缽略可汗。

translations.literal: Anluo later yielded to Mughan's brother's son Shetu—this was Shabolue Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Anluo later yielded to Mughan's nephew Shetu, who became Shabolue Khan.

sentences.zh: 而大邏便別為阿波可汗，自臣所部，沙缽略襲擊之，殺其母，阿波西走達頭。

translations.literal: Daluobian separately became Apo Khan, himself governing his division; Shabolue raided him and killed his mother; Apo fled west to Datou.
translations.idiomatic: Daluobian became Apo Khan over his own followers. Shabolue attacked, killed his mother, and Apo fled to Datou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，達頭為西面可汗，即授阿波兵十萬，使與東突厥戰。

translations.literal: At that time Datou was Western Khan and gave Apo a hundred thousand troops to fight Eastern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Datou, Western Khan, gave Apo a hundred thousand men to fight the Eastern Turks.

sentences.zh: 而阿波竟為沙缽略所禽。

translations.literal: Yet Apo was ultimately captured by Shabolue.
translations.idiomatic: Apo was ultimately captured by Shabolue.

sentences.zh: 及啟民可汗時，達頭可汗歲以兵相加，而隋常助啟民，故達頭敗奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In Qimin Khan's time Western Khan Datou yearly sent troops against him; Sui often aided Qimin—therefore Datou was defeated and fled to Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qimin Khan, Datou attacked yearly until Sui aid to Qimin drove him to flee to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 始，阿波既禽，國人立鞅素特勒子，是為泥利可汗。

translations.literal: At first after Apo was captured the people established Yangsu tegin's son—this was Nili Khan.
translations.idiomatic: After Apo's capture the tribes enthroned Yangsu tegin's son as Nili Khan.

sentences.zh: 達頭之奔，泥利亦敗，及死，其子達漫立，是為泥橛處羅可汗，政苛察多忌。

translations.literal: When Datou fled Nili was also defeated; at his death his son Daman succeeded—this was Nijue Chuluo Khan, whose government was harsh, scrutinizing, and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Datou fled Nili was defeated. His son Daman succeeded as Nijue Chuluo Khan, harsh and suspicious in rule.

sentences.zh: 大業中，從煬帝征高麗，賜號曷薩那可汗，妻以宗女，留其弟闕達度設畜牧於會寧郡，即自稱闕可汗。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he followed Emperor Yang's campaign against Goguryeo and was granted the title Yiwasna Khan; an imperial clanswoman was given him in marriage; his younger brother Quedu she was left herding at Huining Commandery—he styled himself Que Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye he followed Emperor Yang against Goguryeo, was titled Yiwasna Khan, and married an imperial clanswoman. His brother Quedu she herded at Huining and styled himself Que Khan.

sentences.zh: 江都亂，曷薩那從宇文化及至黎陽，遁歸長安，高祖降榻與共坐，封歸義王，以大珠獻帝，帝不受，曰：「朕所重者王之赤心，是無用也。

translations.literal: When Jiangdu fell into chaos Yiwasna followed Yuwen Huaji to Liyang then escaped back to Chang'an; Gaozu descended from the couch to sit with him and enfeoffed him Prince of Returning Righteousness; he presented a great pearl to the emperor who did not accept, saying: "What We value is the king's loyal heart—this is useless."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangdu fell Yiwasna followed Yuwen Huaji then escaped to Chang'an. Gaozu enfeoffed him Prince of Returning Righteousness. He offered a great pearl; Gaozu refused: "I value your loyalty, not gems."

sentences.zh: 」闕可汗有馬三，武德元年內屬，賜號吐烏過拔闕可汗，與李軌連和。

translations.literal: Que Khan had three thousand horses; in Wude 1 he submitted internally and was granted the title Tuwuguoba Que Khan, allying with Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Que Khan submitted in Wude 1 as Tuwuguoba Que Khan and allied with Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 隋西戎使者曹瓊據甘州誘之，俄與瓊合，共擊軌，兵不勝，走達鬥拔谷，與吐谷渾相輔車，為軌所滅。

translations.literal: Sui Western Regions envoy Cao Qiong held Ganzhou and enticed him; soon he joined Qiong and jointly struck Gui; troops were unsuccessful and fled to Dadouba Valley; mutually supporting Tuyuhun they were destroyed by Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qiong of Ganzhou enticed him. He joined Qiong against Li Gui, was defeated, fled to Dadouba Valley, and was destroyed with Tuyuhun's help.

sentences.zh: 初，曷薩那朝隋，國人皆不欲，既被留不遣，乃共立達頭孫，號射匱可汗，建廷龜茲北之三彌山，玉門以西諸國多役屬，與東突厥亢。

translations.literal: At first when Yiwasna visited Sui the people all did not wish it; once he was detained and not sent back they jointly established Datou's grandson—styled Shekui Khan—establishing headquarters at Sanmi Mountain north of Kucha; states west of Yumen mostly served and submitted; he stood equal to Eastern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiwasna was detained in Sui the tribes enthroned Datou's grandson Shekui Khan at Sanmi Mountain north of Kucha. States west of Yumen submitted; he rivaled the Eastern Turks.

sentences.zh: 射匱死，其弟統葉護嗣，是為統葉護可汗。

translations.literal: When Shekui died his younger brother Tong Yehu succeeded—this was Tong Yehu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui's brother Tong Yehu succeeded as Tong Yehu Khan.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗勇而有謀，戰輒勝，因並鐵勒，下波斯、罽賓，控弦數十萬，徙廷石國北之千泉，遂霸西域諸國，悉授以頡利發，而命一吐屯監統，以督賦入。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khan was brave and resourceful—when he fought he always won; thereby he annexed the Tiele, subjugated Persia and Kashmir, controlled several hundred thousand bowmen, moved headquarters north of Shi kingdom's Thousand Springs, and dominated the Western Regions—all were appointed irbir while one tutun supervised and collected tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu was brave and always victorious. He annexed the Tiele, conquered Persia and Kashmir, commanded hundreds of thousands of bowmen, moved his court to the Thousand Springs north of Samarkand, and dominated the west—appointing irbir and tutun to collect tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，射匱使使來，以曷薩那有世憾，請殺之，帝不許。

translations.literal: The next year Shekui sent envoys; because of hereditary enmity with Yiwasna he requested killing him—the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui's envoys asked to kill Yiwasna over old enmity; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 群臣曰：「存一人，失一國，後且為患。

translations.literal: The ministers said: "Keeping one man loses one state—later he will be a trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued: "Spare one man, lose a kingdom—he will trouble us later."

sentences.zh: 」秦王曰：「不然，人來歸我，我殺之不祥。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin said: "Not so—when a man comes to submit to us, killing him is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin objected: "He came to us—killing him brings ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 」帝又不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor again would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 宴禁中，酒酣，至中書省，縱使者戕之，不宣也。

translations.literal: Feasting in the palace, when wine was deep they went to the Secretariat and allowed the envoys to kill him—this was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace feast, when wine ran deep, they let the envoys kill Yiwasna at the Secretariat—unannounced.

sentences.zh: 射匱亦連年系貢條支巨卵、師子革等，帝厚申撫結，約與並力討東突厥。

translations.literal: Shekui also for successive years sent tribute of huge eggs from Tiaozhi, lion skins, and the like; the emperor richly soothed and bound them, covenanting jointly to strike Eastern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui sent tribute of Tiaozhi giant eggs and lion skins. The emperor cultivated alliance against the Eastern Turks.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗請期，頡利大懼，乃與和，約毋相伐也。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khan requested a date; Jieli was greatly afraid and made peace, covenanting not to attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu set a date to attack; Jieli made peace and pledged not to fight.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗來請昏，帝與群臣謀：「西突厥去我遠，緩急不可杖，可與昏乎？

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khan came requesting marriage; the emperor consulted ministers: "Western Turks are far from us—in urgency we cannot rely on them—may we marry?"
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu sought marriage. The emperor asked: "The Western Turks are far—can we rely on them in crisis?"

sentences.zh: 」封德彜曰：「計今之便，莫若遠交而近攻，請聽昏以怖北狄，待我既定，而後圖之。

translations.literal: Feng Deyi said: "Of expedients now none surpass distant alliance and near attack—please permit marriage to intimidate the northern Di; wait until we are settled then plan against them."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi advised: "Ally with the far to strike the near—grant marriage to frighten the northern Turks, then deal with them later."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃許昏，詔高平王道立至其國，統葉護可汗喜，遣真珠統俟斤與道立還，獻萬釘寶鈿金帶、馬五千匹以藉約。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore granted marriage; an edict ordered Prince of Gaoping Dao Li to reach their state; Tong Yehu Khan was pleased and sent Zhenzhu Tong Irkin with Dao Li back, presenting a ten-thousand-nail precious-inlaid gold belt and five thousand horses to seal the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage was granted. Prince Dao Li went west. Tong Yehu sent Zhenzhu Tong Irkin with five thousand horses to seal the pact.

sentences.zh: 會東突厥歲犯邊，西道梗澀，又頡利遣謂曰：「若迎唐公主，必假我道，我且留之。

translations.literal: When Eastern Turks yearly raided the border the western route was blocked; moreover Jieli sent saying: "If you welcome the Tang princess you must borrow my road—I shall detain her."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Turkish raids blocked the route. Jieli warned: "If you fetch the Tang princess through my lands I will seize her."

sentences.zh: 」統葉護可汗病之，未克昏。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khan resented this and could not complete the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu resented this and the marriage failed.

sentences.zh: 方負其強，不以恩結下，眾怨，多叛去，其諸父莫賀咄殺之，帝欲賫玉帛焚祭其國，會亂，不果至。

translations.literal: Just then relying on his strength he did not bind subordinates with grace—masses resented and many rebelled and left; his various uncles Moheduo killed him; the emperor wished to send jade and silk to burn and sacrifice for his state—disorder came and it was not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant and graceless, he lost his followers. His uncle Moheduo killed him before Tang could send funerary offerings.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄立，是為屈利俟毗可汗，遣使者來獻。

translations.literal: Moheduo succeeded—this was Qulisi Bi Khan—and sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo became Qulisi Bi Khan and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 俟毗可汗初分統突厥為小可汗，既稱大可汗，國人不附。

translations.literal: Bi Khan had first divided Turks as lesser khans; having proclaimed himself great khan the people did not attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Having proclaimed himself great khan after ruling a lesser division, Bi Khan lost the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部自推泥孰莫賀設為可汗，泥孰辭不受。

translations.literal: The Nushibi division themselves pushed Nishu Mohe she as khan; Nishu declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Nushibi pushed Nishu Mohe she as khan; he refused.

sentences.zh: 會統葉護可汗子咥力特勒避莫賀咄亂，亡在康居，泥孰迎立之，為乙毗缽羅肆葉護可汗，與俟毗可汗分王其國，挐鬥不解，各遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu Khan's son Dilitegin avoiding Moheduo's disorder was exiled in Kangju; Nishu welcomed and established him as Yipi Boluo Siye Hu Khan; with Bi Khan they divided the state and struggled without resolution—each sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu's son Dilitegin, exiled in Kangju, was enthroned by Nishu as Yipi Boluo Siye Hu Khan. He and Bi Khan divided the realm and fought endlessly.

sentences.zh: 太宗追憐曷薩那死非罪，為贈上柱國，具禮以葬。

translations.literal: Taizong grieving that Yiwasna died though guiltless posthumously awarded Upper Pillar of State and buried him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, grieving Yiwasna's unjust death, posthumously made him Upper Pillar of State and gave him full burial rites.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，俟毗可汗請昏，不許，詔曰：「突厥方亂，君臣未定，何遽昏為？

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan Bi Khan requested marriage—not granted; an edict said: "Turks are just in disorder—ruler and ministers not yet settled—how can we hastily marry?"
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 4 Bi Khan sought marriage. The emperor refused: "The Turks are in turmoil—how can we marry now?"

sentences.zh: 各敕其部毋相侵。

translations.literal: Each was ordered to command his division not to invade each other.
translations.idiomatic: Each was ordered to keep his division from attacking the others.

sentences.zh: 」由是西域諸國悉叛之，國大虛耗，眾悉附肆葉護可汗，雖俟毗之部亦稍稍去，共以兵擊俟毗，俟毗走保金山，為泥孰所殺，奉肆葉護為大可汗。

translations.literal: Thereupon all states of the Western Regions rebelled against him; the state was greatly depleted; the masses all attached to Siye Hu Khan; even Bi Khan's division gradually left; jointly with troops they struck Bi Khan; Bi Khan fled to hold the Altai Mountains and was killed by Nishu; they elevated Siye Hu as great khan.
translations.idiomatic: All the Western Regions rebelled. The state was drained. Tribes rallied to Siye Hu Khan; even Bi Khan's followers deserted. They attacked Bi Khan, who fled to the Altai and was killed by Nishu. Siye Hu became great khan.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護已立，即北討鐵勒、薛延陀，為延陀所敗。

translations.literal: Once Siye Hu was established he immediately campaigned north against the Tiele and Xueyantuo and was defeated by the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Siye Hu immediately marched north against the Tiele and Xueyantuo and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 性猜愎，狹於統下。

translations.literal: His nature was suspicious and obstinate; he was narrow toward those he governed.
translations.idiomatic: He was suspicious, obstinate, and harsh toward his subjects.

sentences.zh: 小可汗乙利者，於國最有功，肆葉護聽讒，種夷之，眾皆沮駭。

translations.literal: Lesser khan Yili had the greatest merit in the state; Siye Hu listened to slander and had him killed; the masses were all discouraged and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser khan Yili had done the most for the state. Siye Hu listened to slander and had him executed. The tribes were dismayed.

sentences.zh: 又忌泥孰，陰圖殺之，泥孰亡入焉耆。

translations.literal: He also envied Nishu and secretly plotted to kill him; Nishu fled and entered Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: He also plotted against Nishu, who fled to Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，沒卑達幹與弩失畢部諸豪謀執廢肆葉護，葉護輕騎走康居，憂死。

translations.literal: Before long Meibei Taghan and the Nushibi division's magnates plotted to seize and depose Siye Hu; Siye Hu fled with light cavalry to Kangju and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Meibei Taghan and Nushibi leaders deposed Siye Hu. He fled to Kangju and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 國人迎泥孰於焉耆，立之，是為咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: The people welcomed Nishu from Yanqi and established him—this was Tulu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes welcomed Nishu from Yanqi and enthroned him as Tulu Khan.

sentences.zh: 可汗父莫賀設，本隸統葉護者，武德時來朝，太宗與之盟，約為昆弟。

translations.literal: The khan's father Mohe she had originally submitted to Tong Yehu Khan; in Wude he came to court; Taizong allied with him, covenanting as sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu's father Mohe she had served Tong Yehu Khan. In Wude he came to court and Taizong swore brotherhood with him.

sentences.zh: 死而泥孰代之，或曰伽那設。

translations.literal: At his death Nishu replaced him—or he is called Gana she.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Nishu succeeded—or he is called Gana she.

sentences.zh: 既立，遣使詣闕，不敢當可汗號。

translations.literal: Once established he sent envoys to court and dared not assume the khan title.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he sent envoys to court but declined the title of khan.

sentences.zh: 帝詔鴻臚少卿劉善因持節冊號吞阿婁拔利邲咄陸可汗，賜鼓纛，段彩巨萬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister of Guests Liu Shanyin bearing credentials to invest him as Tun Aluobili Tulu Khan, granting drums, banners, and brocades by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Liu Shanyin to invest him as Tulu Khan with drums, banners, and lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 泥孰遣使謝。

translations.literal: Nishu sent envoys to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Nishu sent envoys in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 它日，太上皇宴使者兩儀殿，謂長孫無忌曰：「今蠻夷率服，古亦有乎？

translations.literal: Another day the retired emperor feasted envoys in Liangyi Hall and said to Zhangsun Wuji: "Now the barbarians all submit—is there precedent in antiquity?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day the retired emperor feasted envoys and asked Zhangsun Wuji: "Has antiquity ever seen such universal submission?"

sentences.zh: 」無忌上千萬歲壽，太上皇喜，以酒屬帝，帝頓首謝，亦奉觴上太上皇壽。

translations.literal: Wuji toasted long life; the retired emperor was pleased and handed wine to the emperor; the emperor bowed in thanks and also raised a cup to toast the retired emperor's long life.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji offered long life. The retired emperor passed wine to Taizong, who bowed and returned the toast.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗死，弟同俄設立，是為沙缽羅咥利失可汗，贈三遣使奉方物，遂請昏，帝慰而不俞。

translations.literal: When Tulu Khan died his younger brother Tong'e she succeeded—this was Shaboluo Dilishi Khan; thrice he sent envoys with local products and requested marriage; the emperor comforted him but did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu's brother Tong'e she became Shaboluo Dilishi Khan. He sent tribute thrice and sought marriage; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 可汗分其國為十部，部以一人統之，人授一箭，號十設，亦曰十箭。

translations.literal: The khan divided his state into ten divisions; each division was governed by one man; each man was given one arrow—they were called Ten She, also Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the realm into ten divisions, each led by one man with one arrow—the Ten She or Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 為左、右：右五咄陸部，置五大啜，居碎葉東；

translations.literal: They were divided left and right: the right five Tulu divisions had five great chuo, dwelling east of Suyab;
translations.idiomatic: The right held five Tulu divisions with five great chuo, east of Suyab;

sentences.zh: 右五弩失畢部，置五大俟斤，居碎葉西。

translations.literal: the right five Nushibi divisions had five great irkin, dwelling west of Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: the left five Nushibi divisions had five great irkin, west of Suyab.

sentences.zh: 其下稱一箭曰一部落，號十姓部落云。

translations.literal: Subordinates called one arrow one tribe—styled the Ten Surname Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Each arrow was one tribe—the Ten Surname Tribes.

sentences.zh: 然不為眾悅賴，其部統吐屯以兵襲之，咥利失率左右戰，統吐屯不勝去。

translations.literal: Yet he was not pleasing and trusted by the masses; his division's tutun attacked him with troops; Dilishi led the left and right to fight; Tutun was unsuccessful and left.
