translations.idiomatic: Unpopular, he was attacked by his tutun. Dilishi fought back; the tutun fled.

sentences.zh: 咥利失與其弟步利設奔焉耆。

translations.literal: Dilishi and his younger brother Buli she fled to Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Dilishi and his brother Buli she fled to Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 阿悉吉闕俟斤與統吐屯召國人謀立欲谷設為大可汗，以咥利失為小可汗。

translations.literal: Axijie Que Irkin and Tutun summoned the people to plan establishing Yugu she as great khan and Dilishi as lesser khan.
translations.idiomatic: Axijie Que Irkin and the tutun planned to make Yugu she great khan and Dilishi lesser khan.

sentences.zh: 會統吐屯被殺，欲谷設又為其俟斤所破，咥利失乃復得故地。

translations.literal: When Tutun was killed Yugu she was again broken by his irkin; Dilishi then recovered his old lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tutun was killed and Yugu she was defeated by his irkin. Dilishi recovered his lands.

sentences.zh: 後西部卒自立欲谷設為乙毗咄陸可汗，而與咥利失交戰，殺傷不可計，乃因伊列河約諸部：河以西受令於咄陸，其東咥利失主之。

translations.literal: Later the western division independently established Yugu she as Yipi Tulu Khan and fought Dilishi—casualties beyond counting; they therefore made a covenant by the Yilie River among the divisions: west of the river obey Tulu; east Dilishi governs.
translations.idiomatic: The west made Yugu she Yipi Tulu Khan. After bloody war they divided at the Yilie River—west to Tulu, east to Dilishi.

sentences.zh: 自是西突厥又分二國矣。

translations.literal: From this the Western Turks were again divided into two states.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks were split in two.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗建廷鏃曷山西，謂之「北庭」，駁馬、結骨諸國悉附臣之，陰與咥利失部吐屯俟列發以兵攻咥利失。

translations.literal: Tulu Khan established headquarters west of Mount Zhuohe—called the Northern Court; Boma, Kirghiz, and other states all submitted; secretly with Dilishi's division Tutun Houlie Fa he attacked Dilishi with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu built the Northern Court west of Mount Zhuohe and subjugated Boma and the Kirghiz. With Tutun Houlie Fa he attacked Dilishi.

sentences.zh: 咥利失援窮，奔拔汗那而死。

translations.literal: Dilishi's support was exhausted; he fled to Ferghana and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dilishi fled to Ferghana and died.

sentences.zh: 國人立其子，是為乙屈利失乙毗可汗，逾年死。

translations.literal: The people established his son—this was Yiquli Yipi Khan—who died after a year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiquli Yipi Khan reigned one year and died.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢大酋迎伽那設之子畢賀咄葉護立之，是為乙毗沙缽羅葉護可汗。

translations.literal: The Nushibi great chief welcomed Gana she's son Bihuo Yehu and established him—this was Yipi Shaboluo Yehu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Nushibi leaders enthroned Gana she's son Bihuo Yehu as Yipi Shaboluo Yehu Khan.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔左領軍將軍張大師持節冊命，賜鼓纛，建庭雖合水北，謂之「南庭」，東薄伊列河，龜茲、鄯善、且末、吐火羅、焉耆、石、史、何、穆、康等國皆隸屬。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Left Army Guard General Zhang Dash shi bearing credentials to invest him, granting drums and banners; headquarters was built north of Suihe River—called the Southern Court—east bordering the Yilie River; Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tokhar, Yanqi, Shi, Shi kingdoms, He, Mu, Kang, and others all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong invested Shaboluo Yehu Khan and established the Southern Court north of Suihe. Kucha, Shanshan, Yanqi, Samarkand, and others submitted.

sentences.zh: 是時咄陸兵浸浸盛，與沙缽羅葉護數交戰。

translations.literal: At that time Tulu's troops gradually grew strong and he repeatedly fought Shaboluo Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu grew stronger and repeatedly fought Shaboluo Yehu.

sentences.zh: 會二可汗使者皆來，帝敕以敦睦，令各罷兵，咄陸不肯聽，遣石國吐屯攻葉護可汗，殺之，並其國。

translations.literal: When both khans' envoys came the emperor ordered cordial relations and each to cease troops; Tulu would not listen and sent the Shi kingdom tutun to attack Yehu Khan, killed him, and annexed his state.
translations.idiomatic: Both sent envoys; Taizong ordered peace. Tulu refused, killed Yehu Khan, and annexed his realm.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢不服，叛去。

translations.literal: The Nushibi would not submit and rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Nushibi rebelled and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 咄陸又擊吐火羅，取之，乃入寇伊州。

translations.literal: Tulu again attacked Tokhar, took it, and then entered to raid Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu conquered Tokhar and raided Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪以輕騎二千，自烏骨狙擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Protector of the Pacified West Guo Xiaojie with two thousand light horsemen ambushed from Wugu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaojie ambushed him with two thousand light cavalry from Wugu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 咄陸以處月、處蜜兵圍天山而不克，孝恪追北，拔處月俟斤之城，抵遏索山，斬千餘級，降處蜜部而歸。

translations.literal: Tulu with Chuyue and Chumi troops besieged Tianshan but could not take it; Xiaojie pursued north, took the Chuyue irkin's city, reached E Suo Mountain, beheaded more than a thousand, and accepted the submission of the Chumi division before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu failed to take Tianshan. Xiaojie pursued, took a Chuyue city, and accepted Chumi's submission.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗性很傲，留使者元孝友等不遣，妄曰：「我聞唐天子才武，我今討康居，爾視我與天子等否？

translations.literal: Tulu Khan was by nature very arrogant; he detained the envoy Yuan Xiaoyou and others without sending them back, falsely saying: "I hear the Tang Son of Heaven is talented in war—I am now attacking Kangju—do you see me as equal to the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant Tulu detained envoy Yuan Xiaoyou and boasted: "I am attacking Kangju—am I the equal of your Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與共攻康居，道米國，即襲破之，系虜其人，取貲口不以與下，其將泥孰啜怒，奪取之，咄陸斬以徇。

translations.literal: He then jointly attacked Kangju; passing the Mi kingdom he suddenly raided and broke it, bound and captured its people, took wealth and captives without giving to subordinates; his general Nishu Quluo was angry, seized them; Tulu executed him as warning.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Kangju, sacked the Mi kingdom, and hoarded the booty. General Nishu Quluo seized it; Tulu executed him.

sentences.zh: 泥孰啜之將胡祿屋舉兵襲咄陸可汗，多殺士，國大亂，將歸保吐火羅，大臣勸其返國，不從，率眾去，度葉水，及石國，左右亡去略盡，乃保可賀敦城。

translations.literal: Nishu Quluo's general Huluju raised troops and raided Tulu Khan, killing many soldiers; the state fell into great disorder; about to return to guard Tokhar, ministers urged him to return to the state—he would not; leading the host he departed, crossed the Yeshui River, reached the Shi kingdom; left and right mostly fled; he then held Kehedun city.
translations.idiomatic: Huluju revolted and ravaged Tulu's forces. Tulu fled toward Tokhar, lost his followers, and held Kehedun city.

sentences.zh: 自輕出招叛亡，阿悉吉闕俟斤逆擊之，咄陸敗，襲取白水胡城以居。

translations.literal: Venturing out lightly to summon rebellious fugitives, Axijie Que Irkin counterattacked; Tulu was defeated and seized Baishui Hucheng to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Axijie Que Irkin defeated Tulu, who seized Baishui Hucheng.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢不欲咄陸為可汗，遣使者至闕下，請所立。

translations.literal: The Nushibi did not wish Tulu as khan and sent envoys to court requesting whom to establish.
translations.idiomatic: The Nushibi rejected Tulu and asked Tang to choose a khan.

sentences.zh: 帝遣通事舍人溫無隱持璽詔與國大臣擇突厥可汗子孫賢者授之，乃立乙屈利失乙毗可汗之子，是為乙毗射匱可汗。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Communications Officer Wen Wuyin bearing imperial seals with the state's great ministers to select a worthy descendant of the Turkish khan and grant the title; they established Yiquli Yipi Khan's son—this was Yipi Shekui Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang sent Wen Wuyin to select a Turkish prince. They enthroned Yiquli's son as Yipi Shekui Khan.

sentences.zh: 乙毗射匱既立，改館使者，悉還之長安，使弩失畢將兵攻白水胡城。

translations.literal: Once Yipi Shekui was established he changed lodging for envoys and all returned them to Chang'an; he made the Nushibi lead troops to attack Baishui Hucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui Khan returned envoys to Chang'an and sent the Nushibi against Baishui Hucheng.

sentences.zh: 咄陸勒兵自城出，鳴鼓角薄鬥，弩失畢不能軍，殺獲甚多。

translations.literal: Tulu led troops out from the city, sounded drums and horns, and pressed close in battle; the Nushibi could not maintain ranks; kills and captures were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu sallied forth and routed the Nushibi with heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 咄陸因其勝招徠舊部，皆曰：「戰千人，存一人，我猶不從也。

translations.literal: Tulu by this victory summoned and drew old divisions; all said: "A thousand fought and one survived—we still will not follow."
translations.idiomatic: Tulu tried to rally old followers, but they refused: "After a thousand fought, one survived—we will not follow."

sentences.zh: 」咄陸自知眾怨，乃走吐火羅。

translations.literal: Tulu knowing the masses resented him then fled to Tokhar.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was hated, Tulu fled to Tokhar.

sentences.zh: 乙毗射匱遣使貢方物，且請昏，帝令割龜茲、於闐、疏勒、朱俱波、蔥嶺五國為聘禮，不克昏。

translations.literal: Yipi Shekui sent envoys presenting local products and requesting marriage; the emperor ordered ceding Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Zhujubo, and Congling five states as betrothal gifts—the marriage could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui sought marriage; Taizong demanded five states as bride-price. The marriage failed.

sentences.zh: 於是阿史那賀魯反，盡得可汗部落。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ashina Helu rebelled and completely obtained the khan's tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu rebelled and seized the khan's tribes.

sentences.zh: 賀魯阿史那賀魯賀魯者，室點蜜可汗五世孫，曳步利設射匱特勒劫越子也。

translations.literal: Helu Ashina Helu—Helu was the fifth-generation grandson of Shidianmi Khan, son of Yebu she Shekui tegin Jieyue.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu was fifth-generation grandson of Shidianmi Khan, son of Shekui tegin Jieyue of Yebu she.

sentences.zh: 始，阿史那步真來歸國，咄陸可汗以賀魯為葉護，代步真，居多邏斯川，直西州北千五百里，統處月、處蜜、姑蘇、歌邏祿、弩失畢五姓之眾。

translations.literal: At first when Ashina Buzhen came to submit to the state Tulu Khan made Helu yabghu replacing Buzhen, dwelling at Duolosi River, straight fifteen hundred li north of Xizhou, governing the masses of five surnames—Chuyue, Chumi, Gusu, Geluolu, and Nushibi.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu had made Helu yabghu over five tribes at Duolosi River, fifteen hundred li north of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 咄陸之走吐火羅也，乙毗射匱以兵迫逐，賀魯無常居，部多散亡。

translations.literal: When Tulu fled to Tokhar, Yipi Shekui pressed in pursuit; Helu had no fixed residence and divisions mostly scattered and were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Tulu fled, Shekui pursued. Helu wandered and his tribes scattered.

sentences.zh: 有執舍地、處木昆、婆鼻三種者，以賀魯無罪，往請可汗，可汗怒，欲誅執舍地等，三種乃舉所部數千帳，與賀魯皆內屬，帝優撫之。

translations.literal: There were three peoples—Zhishede, Chumukun, and Boni—who because Helu was guiltless went to petition the khan; the khan was angry and wished to execute Zhishede and others; the three peoples therefore led several thousand tents of their divisions and with Helu all submitted internally; the emperor treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Three tribes petitioned for Helu; the khan threatened them. They defected with Helu and Tang treated them well.

sentences.zh: 會討龜茲，請先馳為向導，詔授昆丘道行軍總管，宴嘉壽殿，厚賜予，解衣衣之。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Kucha came they requested to ride ahead as guides; an edict appointed him supreme commander of the Kunqiu mobile campaign route; feasting at Jiaoshou Hall he was richly gifted; robes were removed to clothe him.
translations.idiomatic: Helu guided the Kucha campaign and was made Kunqiu route commander, richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 擢累左驍衛將軍、瑤池都督，處其部於庭州莫賀城，密招攜散，廬幕益眾。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Martial Guard General and Yaochi Protector; his division was settled at Mohe city in Ting Prefecture; he secretly summoned and drew scattered followers; tents and camps daily multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Martial Guard General and Yaochi Protector at Mohe city, he gathered scattered followers.

sentences.zh: 方帝崩，即謀取西、庭二州，刺史駱弘義以聞，高宗遣通事舍人喬寶明馳撫，因令賀魯遣子咥運入宿衛。

translations.literal: Just as the emperor died he plotted to take Xi and Ting prefectures; Prefect Luo Hongyi reported; Gaozong sent Communications Officer Qiao Baoming hastening to soothe and thereby ordered Helu to send his son Dieyun to palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozong's accession Helu plotted against Xi and Ting. Gaozong sent Qiao Baoming and took Helu's son Dieyun as hostage.

sentences.zh: 咥運中悔，劫於勢，不得去，拜右驍衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Dieyun midway regretted but was constrained by circumstances and could not leave; he was appointed Right Martial Guard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Dieyun was trapped and made Right Martial Guard Commandant.

sentences.zh: 帝遣還，咥運即勸賀魯引而西，取咄陸可汗故地，建牙於千泉，自號沙缽羅可汗，遂統咄陸、弩失畢十姓。

translations.literal: The emperor sent him back; Dieyun then urged Helu to lead westward, take Tulu Khan's old lands, establish headquarters at Thousand Springs, style himself Shaboluo Khan, and thereby govern the ten surnames of Tulu and Nushibi.
translations.idiomatic: Sent home, Dieyun urged Helu west to Thousand Springs as Shaboluo Khan over the ten surnames.

sentences.zh: 咄陸有五啜，曰處木昆律啜、胡祿屋闕啜、攝舍提暾啜、突騎施賀邏施啜、鼠尼施處半啜。

translations.literal: Tulu had five chuo: Chumukun Lüchuo, Huluju Quechuo, Shesheti Tunchuo, Turgesh Heluoshichuo, and Shunishi Chubanchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu's five chuo were Chumukun, Huluju, Shesheti, Turgesh, and Shunishi.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢有五俟斤，曰阿悉結闕俟斤、哥舒闕俟斤、拔塞幹暾沙缽俟斤、阿悉結泥孰俟斤、哥舒處半俟斤。

translations.literal: Nushibi had five irkin: Axijie Que Irkin, Geshu Que Irkin, Bassegan Tunchabo Irkin, Axijie Nishu Irkin, and Geshu Chuban Irkin.
translations.idiomatic: Nushibi's five irkin were Axijie, Geshu, Bassegan, Axijie Nishu, and Geshu Chuban.

sentences.zh: 而胡祿屋闕，賀魯婿也。

translations.literal: Among them Huluju Que was Helu's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Huluju Que was Helu's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 阿悉結闕俟斤最盛強，勝兵至數十萬。

translations.literal: Axijie Que Irkin was strongest—battle-ready troops reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Axijie Que Irkin was strongest, with hundreds of thousands of warriors.

sentences.zh: 以咥運為莫賀咄葉護。

translations.literal: Dieyun was made Moheduo Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: Dieyun was made Moheduo Yabghu.

sentences.zh: 遂寇庭州，敗數縣，殺掠數千人去。

translations.literal: He then raided Ting Prefecture, defeated several counties, killed and plundered several thousand before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Helu raided Ting Prefecture, ravaged counties, and withdrew after killing thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔左武衛大將軍梁建方、右驍衛大將軍契何力為弓月道行軍總管，右驍衛將軍高德逸、右武衛將軍薩孤吳仁副之，發府兵三萬，合回紇騎五萬擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Martial Guard General Liang Jianfang and Right Martial Guard General Qibi Heli as supreme commanders of the Gongyue mobile campaign route with Right Martial Guard General Gao Deyi and Right Martial Guard General Sa'gu Wuren as deputies, mobilizing thirty thousand prefectural troops plus fifty thousand Uyghur horsemen to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jianfang and Qibi Heli were sent with eighty thousand men against Helu.

sentences.zh: 駱弘義獻計曰：「安中國以信，馭夷狄以權，理有變通也。

translations.literal: Luo Hongyi offered a plan: "To secure China use trust; to control the Yi and Di use power—reason has flexibility."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongyi argued: "Rule China with trust, control barbarians with expedient force."

sentences.zh: 賀魯保一城，方寒積雪，謂唐兵必不來，宜乘此一舉滅之。

translations.literal: Helu holds one city; now cold and snow accumulate—they think Tang troops surely will not come; we should exploit this one stroke to destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: Helu holds one city and thinks winter excludes Tang armies—we should strike now."

sentences.zh: 遷延及春，且生變，縱不率連諸國，必遠跡遁去。

translations.literal: Delay until spring and changes will arise; even if he does not lead allied states he will flee far away."
translations.idiomatic: Delay until spring and he will escape or rally allies."

sentences.zh: 且兵本誅賀魯，而處蜜、處木昆等亦各欲自免，若留不進，彼與賀魯復合矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the army's purpose is to execute Helu, yet Chumi, Chumukun, and others each wish to save themselves—if we halt and do not advance they will rejoin Helu."
translations.idiomatic: Our target is Helu; Chumi and Chumukun will rejoin him if we hesitate."

sentences.zh: 今雖嚴冬風勁，兵苦皸墮，又不可久留費邊糧，使賊得堅黨附、賒死期也。

translations.literal: Now though deep winter winds are fierce and soldiers suffer cracked skin, we also cannot long remain wasting frontier grain, letting the bandits solidify factions and buy time."
translations.idiomatic: Winter is harsh, but prolonged delay strengthens Helu."

sentences.zh: 請寬處月、處蜜等罪，專誅賀魯，除禍務本，不可先治枝葉也。

translations.literal: Please pardon Chuyue, Chumi, and others' crimes, exclusively execute Helu, remove the calamity and attend to the root—we cannot first treat branches and leaves."
translations.idiomatic: Pardon Chuyue and Chumi; strike Helu alone—the root, not the branches."

sentences.zh: 願發射脾、處月、處蜜、契等兵，賫一月食，急趨之，大軍住憑洛水上為之景助，此驅戎狄攻豺狼也。

translations.literal: I wish to dispatch Shepi, Chuyue, Chumi, Qi, and other troops with one month's rations to rush against them; the main army holding the Pingluo River as distant support—this drives the Rong to attack wolves."
translations.idiomatic: Send tribal allies with one month's rations while the main army holds Pingluo River in support."

sentences.zh: 且戎人藉唐兵為羽翼，今胡騎出前，唐兵躡後，賀魯窮矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the barbarians rely on Tang troops as wings—now Hu horsemen advance in front and Tang troops follow behind—Helu is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian cavalry in front and Tang behind will corner Helu."

sentences.zh: 」天子然其奏，詔弘義佐建方等經略之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved his memorial and ordered Hongyi to assist Jianfang and others in planning operations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and had Hongyi assist Jianfang.

sentences.zh: 處月朱邪孤註者，引兵附賊，據牢山，建方等攻之，眾潰，追行五百里，斬孤註，上首九千級，虜其帥六十，不如弘義所計。

translations.literal: Chuyue Zhu Ye Guzhu led troops attaching to the bandits, holding Mount Lao; Jianfang and others attacked them; the host scattered; pursuit ran five hundred li; Guzhu was beheaded; nine thousand heads were presented; sixty of their chiefs were captured—not as Hongyi had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ye Guzhu of the Chuyue joined Helu. Jianfang defeated him, taking nine thousand heads—not quite as Hongyi had envisioned.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，罷瑤池都督府，即處月置金滿州，又遣左屯衛大將軍程知節為蔥山道行軍大總管，率諸將進討。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui the Yaochi Protectorate was abolished; at the Chuyue Jinman Prefecture was established; Left Garrison Guard General Cheng Zhijie was again sent as supreme commander of the Congshan mobile campaign route leading generals to advance and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 4 the Yaochi Protectorate was abolished; Cheng Zhijie was sent against Helu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，咄陸可汗死，其子真珠葉護請討賀魯自效，為賀魯所拒，不得前。

translations.literal: That year Tulu Khan died; his son Zhenzhu Yehu requested to attack Helu to prove loyalty but was rejected by Helu and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu died; his son Zhenzhu Yehu offered to attack Helu but was blocked.

sentences.zh: 明年，知節擊歌邏祿、處月，斬千級，收馬萬計。

translations.literal: The next year Zhijie struck the Geluolu and Chuyue, beheading a thousand, capturing ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Zhijie defeated the Geluolu and Chuyue, taking a thousand heads and ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 副將周智度擊處木昆城，拔之，斬馘三萬。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Zhou Zhidu attacked Chumukun city, took it, and beheaded or captured thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhidu took Chumukun city with thirty thousand kills.

sentences.zh: 前軍蘇定方擊賀魯別帳鼠尼施於鷹娑川，斬首虜獲馬甚眾，賊棄鎧仗彌野。

translations.literal: Advance commander Su Dingfang struck Helu's separate camp Shunishi at Yingsuo River, beheading and capturing horses in great numbers; bandits abandoned armor littering the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang routed Helu's Shunishi camp at Yingsuo River.

sentences.zh: 會副總管王文度不肯戰，降怛篤城，取其財，屠之，知節不能制。

translations.literal: Deputy supreme commander Wang Wendu refused to fight, surrendered Dudu city, took its wealth, and slaughtered it; Zhijie could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wendu refused battle, sacked Dudu city, and Cheng Zhijie could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，擢定方伊麗道行軍大總管，率燕然都護任雅相、副都護蕭嗣業、左驍衛大將軍瀚海都督回紇婆閏等窮討。

translations.literal: At the start of Xianqing, Dingfang was promoted supreme commander of the Yili mobile campaign route, leading Yanran Protector Ren Yaxiang, Deputy Protector Xiao Siye, Left Martial Guard General Hanhai Protector Uyghur Poyan, and others in exhaustive pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 1 Su Dingfang was made Yili supreme commander to pursue Helu.

sentences.zh: 詔右屯衛大將軍阿史那彌射、左屯衛大將軍阿史那步真為流沙道安撫大使，分出金山道，俟斤嫩獨祿等萬餘帳迎降。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Right Garrison Guard General Ashina Mishe and Left Garrison Guard General Ashina Buzhen as pacification commissioners of the Liusha route, dividing from the Jinshan route; Irkin Nendulu and others with more than ten thousand tents came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Mishe and Buzhen were sent on the Liusha route; Nendulu and others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 定方以精騎至曳咥河西，擊處木昆，破之。

translations.literal: Dingfang with elite cavalry reached west of Yidie River and struck Chumukun, breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang's elite cavalry broke Chumukun west of Yidie River.

sentences.zh: 賀魯舉十姓兵十萬騎來拒，定方以萬人當之，虜見兵少，以騎繞唐軍。

translations.literal: Helu led a hundred thousand horsemen of the ten surnames to resist; Dingfang with ten thousand opposed them; the barbarians seeing few troops surrounded Tang forces with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Helu brought a hundred thousand horsemen; Dingfang met him with ten thousand. The Turks surrounded the Tang line.

sentences.zh: 定方令步卒據原，欑槊外註，自以騎陣於北。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered infantry to hold the plain, halberds pointed outward; he himself with cavalry formed ranks to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang planted infantry with halberds outward and cavalry to the north.

sentences.zh: 賀魯先擊原上軍，三犯，軍不動。

translations.literal: Helu first attacked the forces on the plain; three assaults—the army did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Helu assaulted the infantry three times without breaking them.

sentences.zh: 定方縱騎乘之，虜大潰，追奔數十里，俘斬三萬人，殺其大酋都搭達幹等二百人。

translations.literal: Dingfang unleashed cavalry against them; the barbarians were greatly routed; pursuit ran several tens of li; captives and beheadings thirty thousand; great chiefs including Dutada Taghan two hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang's cavalry routed them—thirty thousand killed, two hundred chiefs slain.

sentences.zh: 明日躡北，五弩失畢皆降。

translations.literal: The next day pursuing north, the five Nushibi all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the five Nushibi submitted.

sentences.zh: 五咄陸聞賀魯敗，趨南道降步真。

translations.literal: The five Tulu hearing Helu was defeated hurried south to submit to Buzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The five Tulu submitted to Buzhen.

sentences.zh: 定方命嗣業、婆閏趨邪羅斯川追虜，任雅相提降兵踵後。

translations.literal: Dingfang ordered Siye and Poyan to hurry to Talas River pursuing the barbarians; Ren Yaxiang led submitted troops following behind.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang sent Siye and Poyan to Talas; Yaxiang followed with submitted troops.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，軍中請須霽，定方曰：「今晦風冽，虜謂我不能師，掩其不虞可也，緩則遠矣，省日兼功，上策也。

translations.literal: Encountering great snow the army requested waiting for clear weather; Dingfang said: "Now dark wind is bitter; the barbarians think we cannot field troops—surprise their unpreparedness; delay and they flee far; save days and combine achievements—this is the upper strategy."
translations.idiomatic: In heavy snow Dingfang insisted on marching: "Helu thinks we cannot fight in winter—surprise him."

sentences.zh: 」於是晝夜進，收所過人畜，至雙河，與彌射、步真會，軍飽氣張，距賀魯牙二百里，陣而行，抵金牙山。

translations.literal: Thereupon day and night they advanced, collecting people and livestock passed along the way; reaching Shuanghe they met Mishe and Buzhen; the army fed and spirits rose; two hundred li from Helu's headquarters they marched in formation, reaching Jinyá Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They marched day and night to Shuanghe, joined Mishe and Buzhen, and reached Jinyá Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賀魯眾適獵，定方兵縱破其牙，俘數萬人，獲鼓纛器械，賀魯跳度伊麗水。

translations.literal: Helu's host happened to be hunting; Dingfang's troops burst and broke his headquarters, capturing tens of thousands, obtaining drums, banners, and weapons; Helu leaped across the Ili River.
translations.idiomatic: Helu was hunting when Dingfang stormed his camp. Helu fled across the Ili River.

sentences.zh: 嗣業次千泉，彌射至伊麗，處月、處蜜諸部皆下。

translations.literal: Siye halted at Thousand Springs; Mishe reached the Ili; Chuyue, Chumi, and all divisions submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Siye reached Thousand Springs; Mishe the Ili; Chuyue and Chumi submitted.

sentences.zh: 次雙河，賀魯先以步失達幹據柵戰，彌射攻之，潰，定方追賀魯至碎葉水，盡奪其眾。

translations.literal: At Shuanghe Helu had first had Bushida Taghan hold the palisade and fight; Mishe attacked and they collapsed; Dingfang pursued Helu to Suyab water and completely seized his host.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuanghe Mishe broke Bushida Taghan's line. Dingfang pursued Helu to Suyab and seized his army.

sentences.zh: 賀魯、咥運將奔鼠耨設，至石國蘇咄城，馬不進，眾饑，賫寶入城，且市馬，城主伊涅達幹迎之，既入，拘送石國。

translations.literal: Helu and Dieyun were about to flee to Shunou she; reaching the Shi kingdom's Sudu city horses would not advance; the host was hungry; carrying treasure they entered the city to buy horses; the city lord Yiniedagan welcomed them; once inside he detained and sent them to the Shi kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Helu fled toward Shunou she but was trapped at Sudu city and delivered to the Shi kingdom.

sentences.zh: 會彌射子元爽與嗣業兵至，取之。

translations.literal: Mishe's son Yuanshuang and Siye's troops arrived and took them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang and Siye's troops captured them.

sentences.zh: 乃悉散諸部兵，開道置驛，收露胔，問人疾苦，賀魯所掠悉還之民，西域平。

translations.literal: Thereupon all division troops were dispersed; roads were opened and posts established; exposed corpses were gathered; people's hardships were inquired after; what Helu had plundered was all returned to the people—the Western Regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang restored plundered property and pacified the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 賀魯謂嗣業曰：「我，亡虜也，先帝厚我，我則背之，今天降怒罰，尚何道？

translations.literal: Helu told Siye: "I am a destroyed captive; the former emperor treated me generously and I turned my back—now Heaven sends angry punishment—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Helu told Siye: "I betrayed the emperor who favored me. Heaven's punishment is just—what can I say?"

sentences.zh: 且聞漢法殺人必都市，我願就死昭陵，謝罪於先帝也。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear Han law requires executing killers in the capital—I wish to die at Zhaoling and apologize to the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: I hear Han law executes criminals in the capital. Let me die at Zhaoling and apologize to the former emperor."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「先帝賜賀魯二千帳主之，今罪人既得，獻昭陵其可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The former emperor granted Helu two thousand tents to govern—now the guilty man is obtained—can he be presented at Zhaoling?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The former emperor entrusted Helu with two thousand tents. Can we present this captive at Zhaoling?"

sentences.zh: 」許敬宗曰：「古者，軍凱還則飲至於廟。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong said: "In antiquity when the army returned victorious they drank at the temple."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong said: "Victorious armies traditionally offered wine at the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 若諸侯，獻馘天子，未聞獻於陵。

translations.literal: For feudal lords presenting severed ears to the Son of Heaven—I have not heard of presenting at a tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords presented captives to the Son of Heaven—not at a tomb."

sentences.zh: 然陛下奉園寢與宗廟等，可行不疑。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty treats the garden tomb as equal to the ancestral temple—this may be done without doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty treats the imperial tomb like the ancestral temple—proceed without hesitation."

sentences.zh: 」於是執而獻昭陵，赦不誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was seized and presented at Zhaoling and pardoned from execution.
translations.idiomatic: Helu was presented at Zhaoling and spared execution.

sentences.zh: 賀魯已滅，裂其地為州縣，以處諸部。

translations.literal: Once Helu was destroyed his lands were divided into prefectures and counties to settle the various divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Helu's lands were divided into prefectures to settle the tribes.

sentences.zh: 木昆部為匐延都督府，突騎施索葛莫賀部為嗢鹿都督府，突騎施阿利施部為絜山都督府，胡祿屋闕部為鹽泊都督府，攝舍提暾部為雙河都督府，鼠尼施處半部為鷹娑都督府，又置昆陵、濛池二都護府以統之。

translations.literal: Chumukun division became Fuyan Protectorate; Turgesh Suoge Mohe division Wulu Protectorate; Turgesh Alishi division Jiexian Protectorate; Huluju Que division Yanbo Protectorate; Shesheti Tun division Shuanghe Protectorate; Shunishi Chuban division Yingsuo Protectorate; Kunling and Mengchi grand protectorates were also established to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Protectorates were established for Chumukun, Turgesh, Huluju, Shesheti, Shunishi, and others under Kunling and Mengchi grand protectorates.

sentences.zh: 其所役屬諸國皆置州，西盡波斯，並隸安西都護府。

translations.literal: All subject states were established as prefectures—west to Persia—all under the Protectorate of the Pacified West.
translations.idiomatic: Subject states west to Persia became prefectures under the Pacified West Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 以阿史那彌射為興昔亡可汗，兼驃騎大將軍、昆陵都護，領五咄陸部，阿史那步真為繼往絕可汗，兼驃騎大將軍、濛池都護，領五弩失畢部，各賜帛十萬，以光祿卿盧承慶持冊命之。

translations.literal: Ashina Mishe was made Xingxiwang Khan, concurrent Flying Cavalry General and Kunling Protector governing the five Tulu divisions; Ashina Buzhen was made Jiwangjue Khan, concurrent Flying Cavalry General and Mengchi Protector governing the five Nushibi divisions—each granted a hundred thousand bolts of silk; Director of Imperial Banquets Lu Chengqing was sent bearing investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Mishe became Xingxiwang Khan over the five Tulu; Buzhen became Jiwangjue Khan over the five Nushibi, each with a hundred thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 賀魯死，詔葬頡利冢旁，紀其概於石。

translations.literal: When Helu died an edict ordered burial beside Jieli's tomb with his outline recorded on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Helu was buried beside Jieli with an epitaph on stone.

sentences.zh: 阿史那彌射，亦室點蜜可汗五世孫，世為莫賀咄葉護。

translations.literal: Ashina Mishe was also fifth-generation grandson of Shidianmi Khan; for generations Moheduo Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe was also fifth-generation grandson of Shidianmi Khan, hereditary Moheduo Yabghu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遣使者持節立彌射為奚利邲咄陸可汗，賜鼓纛。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan envoys were sent bearing credentials to establish Mishe as Xili Tulu Khan, granting drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan Mishe was invested as Xili Tulu Khan with drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 族兄步真謀殺彌射，欲自立，彌射不能國，即舉所部處月、處蜜等入朝，拜右監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Clansman Buzhen plotted to kill Mishe wishing to establish himself; Mishe could not maintain his state and immediately led his division Chuyue, Chumi, and others to court, appointed Right Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhen plotted against Mishe, who fled to court with Chuyue and Chumi and became Right Gate Guard General.

sentences.zh: 而步真遂自為咄陸葉護，眾不厭，去之，亦與族人來朝，拜左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Buzhen then made himself Tulu Yabghu; the masses were displeased and left him; he also came to court with clansmen, appointed Left Garrison Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhen made himself Tulu Yabghu, lost his followers, and came to court as Left Garrison Guard General.

sentences.zh: 彌射從帝征高麗有功，封平壤縣伯，遷右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Mishe followed the emperor's Liaodong campaign with merit, enfeoffed Baron of Pyongyang, promoted Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe served in Liaodong, was enfeoffed Baron of Pyongyang, and promoted Right Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 及平賀魯，乃與步真皆為可汗，得補所部刺史以下。

translations.literal: When Helu was pacified he and Buzhen both became khans and could appoint prefectural governors and below within their divisions.
translations.idiomatic: After Helu's defeat both became khans with power to appoint officials in their divisions.

sentences.zh: 是歲，彌射擊真珠葉護於雙河，斬之，殺闕啜二人。

translations.literal: That year Mishe struck Zhenzhu Yehu at Shuanghe, beheaded him, and killed two quechuo.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mishe killed Zhenzhu Yehu at Shuanghe and two quechuo.

sentences.zh: 彌射、步真無綏御材，下多怨，於是思結都曼率疏勒、朱俱波、喝槃陀三國叛，擊破於闐，詔左驍衛大將軍蘇定方討之，都曼兵保馬頭川。

translations.literal: Mishe and Buzhen lacked talent to soothe and govern; subordinates mostly resented; thereupon Sijie Duman of the Sijie led Kashgar, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo three states in rebellion, broke Khotan; an edict ordered Left Martial Guard General Su Dingfang to suppress them; Duman's troops held Matou River.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe and Buzhen failed to govern; Sijie Duman rebelled with three states and broke Khotan. Su Dingfang was sent against him at Matou River.

sentences.zh: 五年，定方傅其城，擊降之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Dingfang assaulted his city and struck until he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Dingfang took Duman's city and forced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，彌射、步真以兵從䫻海道總管蘇海政討龜茲，步真怨彌射，且欲並其部，乃誣以謀反。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 Mishe and Buzhen followed Hanhai route supreme commander Su Haizheng to suppress Kucha; Buzhen resented Mishe and wished to annex his division; he falsely accused him of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 Mishe and Buzhen joined Su Haizheng against Kucha. Buzhen falsely accused Mishe of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 海政不能察，即集軍吏計議先發誅之，因稱詔發所賫賜可汗首領，彌射以麾下至，悉收斬之。

translations.literal: Haizheng could not discern it; he immediately gathered army officers to plan launching first to execute him; thereby claiming an edict to distribute gifts bestowed on khan chiefs—when Mishe arrived below his banner all were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Haizheng believed the accusation and executed Mishe and his chiefs under false pretense of distributing gifts.

sentences.zh: 其部鼠尼施、拔塞幹叛走，海政追平之。

translations.literal: Their divisions Shunishi and Bassegan rebelled and fled; Haizheng pursued and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Shunishi and Bassegan rebelled; Haizheng pursued and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 步真死幹封時。

translations.literal: Buzhen died in the Qianfeng era.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhen died in Qianfeng.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年，以西突厥部酋阿史那都支為左驍衛大將軍兼匐延都督，以安輯其眾。

translations.literal: In Xianheng 2 Western Turkish division chief Ashina Duzhi was made Left Martial Guard General and concurrent Fuyan Protector to soothe and settle his host.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 2 Ashina Duzhi was made Left Martial Guard General and Fuyan Protector.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，都支自號十姓可汗，與吐蕃連和，寇安西，詔吏部侍郎裴行儉討之。

translations.literal: In Yifeng Duzhi styled himself Ten Surname Khan, allied with Tibet, and raided Anxi; an edict ordered Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Xingjian to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yifeng Duzhi allied with Tibet and raised Anxi. Pei Xingjian was sent against him.

sentences.zh: 行儉請毋發兵，可以計取。

translations.literal: Xingjian requested not to mobilize troops—he could take them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian proposed taking Duzhi by stratagem without mobilizing troops.

sentences.zh: 即詔行儉冊送波斯王子，並安撫大食，若道兩蕃者。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Xingjian to invest and escort the Persian prince and also pacify the Arabs—as if traveling through both barbarian states.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to invest the Persian prince and pacify the Arabs, passing through both realms.

sentences.zh: 都支果不疑，率子弟止謁，遂禽之，召執諸部渠長，降別帥李遮匐以歸，調露元年也。

translations.literal: Duzhi indeed did not suspect; leading sons and younger brothers he stopped to pay respects and was seized; he summoned and detained chieftains of all divisions; submitted the separate commander Li Zhebi and returned—in Tiaolu 1.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi was captured when he came to pay respects. Xingjian detained the chiefs and returned with Li Zhebi—in Tiaolu 1.

sentences.zh: 西姓自是益衰，其後二部人日離散。

translations.literal: The Western surname from this daily grew weaker; afterward the two divisions' people daily scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Western Turkish power waned as the two divisions scattered.

sentences.zh: 遂擢彌射子元慶為左玉鈐衛將軍，步真子步利設斛瑟羅為右玉鈐衛將軍，盡襲父所領及可汗號。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mishe's son Yuanqing was promoted Left Jade Bell Guard General; Buzhen's son Buli she Huseluo Right Jade Bell Guard General—inheriting all their fathers governed and khan titles.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe's son Yuanqing and Buzhen's son Huseluo inherited their fathers' titles and domains.

sentences.zh: 元慶累拜鎮國大將軍、行左威衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Yuanqing was repeatedly promoted to General of Pacifying the State and Acting Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing rose to General of Pacifying the State and Acting Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 武後擅命，率諸蕃長請賜睿宗氏曰武，更號斛瑟羅曰竭忠事主可汗。

translations.literal: Empress Wu on her own authority led various barbarian chiefs to request granting Ruizong's clan the surname Wu; Huseluo was renamed Jiezhong Shizhu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had tribal chiefs request the Wu surname for Ruizong's clan and renamed Huseluo Jiezhong Shizhu Khan.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，元慶坐謁皇嗣，為來俊臣所誣，要斬，流其子獻於振州。

translations.literal: In Changshou Yuanqing was executed for visiting the crown prince—framed by Lai Junchen, cut in half at the waist; his son Xian was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Changshou Yuanqing was executed by Lai Junchen for visiting the crown prince; his son Xian was exiled.

sentences.zh: 其明年，西突厥部立阿史那俀子為可汗，與吐蕃寇，武威道大總管王孝傑與戰冷泉、大領谷，破之；

translations.literal: The next year a Western Turkish division established Ashina Chizi as khan and with Tibet raided; Wuwei route supreme commander Wang Xiaojie fought them at Lengquan and Daling Valley and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ashina Chizi was made khan and raided with Tibet; Wang Xiaojie defeated them at Lengquan and Daling Valley;

sentences.zh: 碎葉鎮守使韓思忠又破泥熟俟斤及突厥施質汗、胡祿等，因拔吐蕃泥熟沒斯城。

translations.literal: Suyab garrison commander Han Sizhong again defeated Nishu Irkin and Turgesh Zhi Khan and Huluju, thereby taking Tibet's Nishu Meisi city.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sizhong defeated Nishu Irkin and took Tibet's Nishu Meisi city.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，以斛瑟羅為左衛大將軍兼平西軍大總管，令撫鎮國人。

translations.literal: In Shengli 2 Huseluo was made Left Guard General and concurrent Pacified Western Army supreme commander, ordered to soothe the submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengli 2 Huseluo was made Left Guard General and Pacified Western Army commander.

sentences.zh: 是時烏質勒兵張甚，斛瑟羅不敢歸，與其部人六七萬內遷，死長安，擢子懷道為右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzhile's troops were very strong; Huseluo dared not return; with sixty or seventy thousand of his division he migrated internally; he died in Chang'an; his son Huaidao was promoted Right Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile was too strong; Huseluo migrated with sixty thousand followers and died in Chang'an. His son Huaidao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 長安中，以阿史那獻為右驍衛大將軍，襲興昔亡可汗、安撫招慰十姓大使、北庭大都護。

translations.literal: In Chang'an Ashina Xian was made Right Martial Guard General, inheriting Xingxiwang Khan, Pacification Commissioner of the Ten Surnames, and Grand Protector of Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an Ashina Xian became Right Martial Guard General, Ten Surname Khan, and Beiting Protector.

sentences.zh: 四年，以懷道為十姓可汗兼濛池都護。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Huaidao was made Ten Surname Khan and concurrent Mengchi Protector.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Huaidao became Ten Surname Khan and Mengchi Protector.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢獻磧西節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Xian was promoted Western Desert Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xian was made Western Desert Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十姓部落都擔叛，獻擊斬之，傳首闕下，收碎葉以西帳落三萬內屬，璽書嘉慰。

translations.literal: Ten Surname tribal chief Dudan rebelled; Xian struck and beheaded him, sent the head to court, accepted more than thirty thousand tents west of Suyab internally—imperial letter praised and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Xian killed the rebel Dudan and accepted thirty thousand tents west of Suyab.

sentences.zh: 葛邏祿、胡屋、鼠尼施三姓已內屬，為默啜侵掠，以獻為定遠道大總管，與北庭都護湯嘉惠等掎角。

translations.literal: Geluolu, Huwu, and Shunishi three surnames had submitted but were raided by Mokchur; Xian was made Dingyuan route supreme commander coordinating with Beiting Protector Tang Jiahui.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was sent to coordinate with Beiting against Mokchur's raids on submitted tribes.

sentences.zh: 於是突騎施陰幸邊隙，故獻乞益師，身入朝，玄宗不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Turgesh secretly hoped for border openings; therefore Xian requested additional troops and personally entering court—Xuanzong did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: The Turgesh sought opportunity; Xian asked for reinforcements and to come to court—Xuanzong refused.

sentences.zh: 詔左武衛中郎將王惠持節安慰。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Martial Guard Commandant Wang Hui bearing credentials to comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui was sent to reassure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 方冊拜突騎施都督車鼻施啜蘇祿為順國公，而突騎施已圍撥換、大石城，將取四鎮。

translations.literal: Just as investiture was to be conferred on Turgesh Protector Chebi Shichuo Suluk as Duke of Shunguo—the Turgesh had already besieged Bo Huan and Dashicheng, about to take the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Suluk was to be made Duke of Shunguo—but the Turgesh besieged Bo Huan and Dashicheng, threatening the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 會嘉惠拜安西副大都護，即發三姓葛邏祿兵與獻共擊之。

translations.literal: When Jiahui became Deputy Protector of Anxi he immediately mobilized three-surname Geluolu troops jointly with Xian to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiahui mobilized Geluolu troops with Xian to attack.

sentences.zh: 帝將詔王惠與相經略，宰相臣璟、臣頲曰：「突騎施叛，葛邏祿攻之，此夷狄自相殘，非朝廷出也。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to order Wang Hui to coordinate strategy; chancellors Song Jing and Zhang Shuo said: "The Turgesh rebel and the Geluolu attack them—this is barbarians destroying each other—not the court's affair."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Song and Zhang argued: "Let the Turgesh and Geluolu fight each other—it is not our fight."

sentences.zh: 大者傷，小者滅，皆我之利。

translations.literal: The great injured and the small destroyed—both are our profit."
translations.idiomatic: Whether the strong are hurt or the weak destroyed, we profit."

sentences.zh: 方王惠往撫慰，不可參以兵事。

translations.literal: Wang Hui is going to comfort—military affairs must not be mixed in."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui goes to soothe—not to fight."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was halted.

sentences.zh: 獻終以娑葛強狠不能制，亦歸死長安。

translations.literal: Xian ultimately because Suoge was strong and fierce could not control him and also returned to die in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to control Suoge, Xian returned to Chang'an and died.

sentences.zh: 突騎施吐火仙之敗，始以懷道子昕為十姓可汗、開府儀同三司、濛池都護，冊其妻涼國夫人李為交河公主，遣兵護送。

translations.literal: After Turgesh Tuhuoxian's defeat Huaidao's son Xin was first made Ten Surname Khan, Palace Attendant of First Rank, and Mengchi Protector; his wife Lady of Liang State Li was made Princess Jiaohe; troops were sent to escort.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuhuoxian's fall Xin was made Ten Surname Khan; Princess Jiaohe was sent with an escort.

sentences.zh: 昕至碎葉西俱蘭城，為突騎施莫賀達幹所殺，交河公主與其子忠孝亡歸，授左領軍衛員外將軍，西突厥遂亡。

translations.literal: Xin reached Julan city west of Suyab and was killed by Turgesh Moheda Taghan; Princess Jiaohe and her son Zhongxiao fled back; appointed Left Army Guard supernumerary general—the Western Turks then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was killed at Julan city; Princess Jiaohe fled home. The Western Turks perished.

sentences.zh: 突騎施烏質勒突騎施烏質勒突騎施烏質勒，西突厥別部也。

translations.literal: Turgesh Wuzhile Turgesh Wuzhile Turgesh Wuzhile was a separate division of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Turgesh Wuzhile was a separate division of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 自賀魯破滅，二部可汗皆先入侍，虜無的君。

translations.literal: Since Helu's destruction both division khans had first entered court service; the barbarians had no fixed ruler.
translations.idiomatic: After Helu's fall both khans served at court; the steppe had no fixed ruler.

sentences.zh: 烏質勒隸斛瑟羅，為莫賀達幹。

translations.literal: Wuzhile submitted to Huseluo as Moheda Taghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile served Huseluo as Moheda Taghan.

sentences.zh: 斛瑟羅政殘，眾不悅，而烏質勒能撫下，有威信，諸胡順附，帳落浸盛，乃置二十都督，督兵各七千，屯碎葉西北。

translations.literal: Huseluo's government was cruel; the masses were displeased; Wuzhile could soothe subordinates and had prestige and trust; various Hu willingly attached; tents daily grew strong; he therefore established twenty grand protectors each commanding seven thousand troops garrisoned northwest of Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: Huseluo was cruel; Wuzhile won loyalty, established twenty grand protectors with seven thousand men each northwest of Suyab.

sentences.zh: 稍攻得碎葉，即徙其牙居之，謂碎葉川為大牙，弓月城、伊麗水為小牙，其地東鄰北突厥，西諸胡，東直西、庭州，盡並斛瑟羅地。

translations.literal: Gradually attacking he obtained Suyab and moved his headquarters there—calling the Suyab River the great headquarters, Gongyue city and Ili waters the lesser headquarters; his territory east bordered the Northern Turks, west various Hu, east straight to Xi and Ting prefectures—completely annexing Huseluo's lands.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Suyab as his capital, with secondary seats at Gongyue and the Ili, annexing Huseluo's domain.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，遣子遮弩來朝，武後厚加慰撫。

translations.literal: In Shengli 2 he sent his son Zhenu to court; Empress Wu richly comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengli 2 his son Zhenu came to court and was warmly received.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，封懷德郡王。

translations.literal: In Shenlong he was enfeoffed Prince of Huaide Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong he was enfeoffed Prince of Huaide Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是歲，烏質勒死，其子嗢鹿州都督娑葛為左驍衛大將軍，襲封爵。

translations.literal: That year Wuzhile died; his son Wulu Prefecture Protector Suoge was Left Martial Guard General, inheriting the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile died; his son Suoge inherited as Left Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 是時勝兵三十萬，詔十姓可汗阿史那懷道持節冊命，賜宮人四。

translations.literal: At that time battle-ready troops numbered three hundred thousand; an edict ordered Ten Surname Khan Ashina Huaidao bearing credentials to invest him, granting four palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge commanded three hundred thousand warriors; Huaidao invested him with four palace women.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遣使者入謝，中宗為御前殿，列萬騎羽林二仗，引見勞賜。

translations.literal: In Jinglong envoys came to give thanks; Zhongzong personally held court in the front hall, arrayed ten thousand Flying Cavalry and Feathered Forest guards in two formations, received and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong Zhongzong received Turgesh envoys with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 俄與其將厥啜忠節交怨，兵相加暴。

translations.literal: Soon he quarreled with his general Juechuo Zhongjie; troops mutually attacked violently.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge quarreled with general Zhongjie and they fought.

sentences.zh: 娑葛訟忠節罪，請內之京師。

translations.literal: Suoge sued Zhongjie's crimes and requested he be brought internally to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge accused Zhongjie and asked that he be brought to court.

sentences.zh: 忠節以千金賂宰相宗楚客等，願無入朝，請導吐蕃擊娑葛以報。

translations.literal: Zhongjie bribed chancellor Zong Chuke and others with a thousand gold, wishing not to enter court, requesting to guide Tibet to strike Suoge in revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie bribed Zong Chuke to stay out of court and bring Tibet against Suoge.

sentences.zh: 楚客方專國，即以御史中丞馮嘉賓持節經制。

translations.literal: Chuke was then monopolizing state affairs; he immediately sent Censor-in-Chief Feng Jiabin bearing credentials to regulate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke sent Feng Jiabin to mediate.

sentences.zh: 嘉賓與忠節書疏反復，娑葛邏得之，遂殺嘉賓，使弟遮弩率兵盜塞。

translations.literal: Jiabin's letters back and forth with Zhongjie were obtained by Suoge's scouts; he then killed Jiabin and sent his younger brother Zhenu leading troops to raid the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge intercepted Jiabin's correspondence, killed him, and sent Zhenu to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 安西都護牛師獎與戰火燒城，師獎敗，死之，表索楚客頭以徇。

translations.literal: Protector of the Pacified West Niu Shijiang fought at Huoshaocheng; Shijiang was defeated and died, memorializing requesting Chuke's head for public display.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Shijiang died fighting at Huoshaocheng and demanded Chuke's head.

sentences.zh: 大都護郭元振表娑葛狀直，當見赦，詔許，西土遂定。

translations.literal: Grand Protector Guo Yuanzhen memorialized that Suoge's case was justified and should be pardoned; an edict granted it—the western lands were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen argued Suoge was justified; he was pardoned and the west was settled.

sentences.zh: 既而與遮弩分治其部，遮弩恨眾少，叛歸默啜，請為鄉導反攻其兄。

translations.literal: Afterward he and Zhenu divided governance of his division; Zhenu resented having few followers, rebelled and submitted to Mokchur, requesting to be guide to counterattack his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenu, resentful of a smaller share, defected to Mokchur to attack Suoge.

sentences.zh: 默啜留遮弩，自以兵二萬擊娑葛，禽之。

translations.literal: Mokchur detained Zhenu and personally with twenty thousand troops struck Suoge and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur kept Zhenu and captured Suoge with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 默啜歸語遮弩曰：「汝兄弟不相協，能盡心事我乎？

translations.literal: Mokchur on returning told Zhenu: "Your brothers do not cooperate—can you fully serve me?"
translations.idiomatic: Mokchur asked Zhenu: "Your brothers could not cooperate—will you serve me faithfully?"

sentences.zh: 」兩殺之。

translations.literal: He killed both.
translations.idiomatic: He killed them both.

sentences.zh: 突騎施別種車鼻施啜蘇祿者，裒拾餘眾，自為可汗。

translations.literal: Turgesh separate branch Chebi Shichuo Suluk gathered remnant followers and made himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi Shichuo Suluk of the Turgesh rallied remnants and made himself khan.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿善撫循其下，部種稍合，眾至二十萬，於是復雄西域。

translations.literal: Suluk was skilled at soothing and guiding subordinates; divisions gradually reunited; the host reached two hundred thousand; he then again dominated the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Suluk reunited the Turgesh to two hundred thousand and again dominated the west.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，始來朝，授右武衛大將軍、突騎施都督，卻所獻不受。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 5 he first came to court; appointed Right Martial Guard General and Turgesh Protector; returned gifts were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 Suluk came to court as Turgesh Protector; his gifts were declined.

sentences.zh: 以武衛中郎將王惠持節拜蘇祿左羽林大將軍、順國公，賜錦袍、鈿帶、魚袋七事，為金方道經略大使。

translations.literal: Left Guard Commandant Wang Hui was sent bearing credentials to invest Suluk Left Forest Guard General and Duke of Shunguo, granting brocade robes, inlaid belt, and seven fish bags—as Jinfang route pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui invested Suluk as Duke of Shunguo and Jinfang route commissioner.

sentences.zh: 然詭猾，不純臣於唐，天子羈系之，進號忠順可汗。

translations.literal: Yet he was cunning and slippery—not a pure subject of Tang; the Son of Heaven restrained him and advanced his title to Loyal and Submissive Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning and not fully loyal, Suluk was titled Loyal and Submissive Khan.

sentences.zh: 其後閱一二歲，使者納贄，帝以阿史那懷道女為交河公主妻之。

translations.literal: Afterward every year or two envoys brought tribute; the emperor gave Ashina Huaidao's daughter as Princess Jiaohe in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor married Huaidao's daughter to him as Princess Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 是歲，突騎施鬻馬於安西，使者致公主教於都護杜暹，暹怒曰：「阿史那女敢宣教邪？

translations.literal: That year the Turgesh sold horses at Anxi; the envoy delivered the princess's instruction to Protector Du Xian; Xian angrily said: "Ashina's daughter dares deliver instructions?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Turgesh sold horses at Anxi, Du Xian flogged the envoy who bore Princess Jiaohe's orders.

sentences.zh: 」笞其使，不報。

translations.literal: He flogged the envoy and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿怒，陰結吐蕃舉兵掠四鎮，圍安西城。

translations.literal: Suluk was angry, secretly allied with Tibet and raised troops raiding the Four Garrisons, besieging Anxi city.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Suluk allied with Tibet, raided the Four Garrisons, and besieged Anxi.

sentences.zh: 暹方入當國，而趙頤貞代為都護，乘城久之，出戰又敗。

translations.literal: Xian had just entered the chancellorship; Zhao Yizhen replaced him as protector; he held the city long; sallying to fight he was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian became chancellor; Zhao Yizhen held Anxi but was defeated sallying out.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿略人畜，發囷貯，徐聞暹已宰相，乃引去；

translations.literal: Suluk plundered people and livestock, opened granaries and stores; slowly hearing Xian was already chancellor he then withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: Suluk plundered and opened granaries, then withdrew on hearing Du Xian was chancellor;

sentences.zh: 即遣首領葉支阿布思來朝，玄宗召見，饗之。

translations.literal: He immediately sent chief Yezhi Abu Si to court; Xuanzong summoned and feasted him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Abu Si to court; Xuanzong feasted him.

sentences.zh: 會東突厥使者亦來，與爭長曰：「突騎施國小，且突厥臣，不宜居上。

translations.literal: When Eastern Turkish envoys also came they disputed precedence saying: "The Turgesh state is small and moreover Turkish subjects—they should not sit above."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Turkish envoys disputed rank: "The Turgesh are small and were Turkish subjects—they should not sit above us."

sentences.zh: 」蘇祿使者曰：「宴乃為我，不可下。

translations.literal: Suluk's envoy said: "The feast is for us—we cannot sit below."
translations.idiomatic: Suluk's envoy replied: "This feast is for us—we will not sit below."

sentences.zh: 」遂設東西幄，而蘇祿使者西席，乃克宴。

translations.literal: Thereupon east and west canopies were set and Suluk's envoy took the western seat—only then could the feast proceed.
translations.idiomatic: East and west seats were arranged with the Turgesh in the west seat before the feast could proceed.

sentences.zh: 始，蘇祿愛治其人，性勤約，每戰有所得，盡以予下，故諸族附悅之，為盡力，又交通吐蕃、突厥，二國皆以女妻之，遂立三國女並為可敦，以數子為葉護。

translations.literal: At first Suluk loved governing his people; his nature was diligent and frugal; whenever battle gained anything he entirely gave to subordinates—therefore various tribes attached and pleased served him with full effort; he also communicated with Tibet and the Turks—both states gave him daughters in marriage; he therefore established three states' daughters all as khatuns and several sons as yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: Suluk was generous in victory and married daughters of Tibet and the Turks, making three khatuns and several yabghu sons.

sentences.zh: 費日廣而無素儲，晚年愁窶不聊，故鹵獲稍留不分，下始貳矣；

translations.literal: Expenses daily grew yet he had no regular stores; in later years he was impoverished and distressed; therefore plunder was somewhat retained undistributed—subordinates began to waver;
translations.idiomatic: In old age he hoarded booty and lost the loyalty of his followers;

sentences.zh: 又病風，一支攣，不事事。

translations.literal: He also suffered wind illness; one limb was contracted; he did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also suffered paralysis and neglected affairs.

sentences.zh: 於是大首領莫賀達幹、都摩支二部方盛，而種人自謂娑葛後者為「黃姓」，蘇祿部為「黑姓」，更相猜讎。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great chiefs Moheda Taghan and Dumozhi two divisions were flourishing while tribesmen calling themselves Suoge's descendants were "Yellow Surname" and Suluk's division "Black Surname"—mutually suspicious and hostile.
translations.idiomatic: Moheda Taghan and Dumozhi rose while Yellow and Black surnames feuded.

sentences.zh: 俄而莫賀達幹、都摩支夜攻蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: Soon Moheda Taghan and Dumozhi attacked Suluk by night and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Moheda Taghan and Dumozhi assassinated Suluk.

sentences.zh: 都摩支又背達幹立蘇祿子吐火仙骨啜為可汗，居碎葉城，引黑姓可汗爾微特勒保怛邏斯城，共擊達幹。

translations.literal: Dumozhi again betrayed Taghan and established Suluk's son Tuhuoxian Guchuo as khan dwelling at Suyab city; leading Black Surname Khan Erwei tegin he held Talas city and jointly struck Taghan.
translations.idiomatic: Dumozhi enthroned Tuhuoxian at Suyab; Black and Yellow factions warred.

sentences.zh: 帝使磧西節度使蓋嘉運和撫突騎施、拔汗那西方諸國。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Western Desert Military Commissioner Gai Jiayun to harmonize and soothe the Turgesh, Ferghana, and western states.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jiayun was sent to pacify the Turgesh and western states.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達幹與嘉運率石王莫賀咄吐屯、史王斯謹提共擊蘇祿子，破之碎葉城。

translations.literal: Moheda Taghan with Jiayun led Shi King Moheduo Tutun and Shi King Sijin Ti jointly to strike Suluk's son, breaking them at Suyab city.
translations.idiomatic: Taghan and Jiayun with Shi and Shi kings defeated Tuhuoxian at Suyab.

sentences.zh: 吐火仙棄旗走，禽之，並其弟葉護頓阿波。

translations.literal: Tuhuoxian abandoned his banner and fled; he was captured along with his younger brother Yabghu Dunabo.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhuoxian fled but was captured with his brother Dunabo.

sentences.zh: 疏勒鎮守使夫蒙靈詧挾銳兵與拔汗那王掩怛邏斯城，斬黑姓可汗與其弟撥斯，入曳建城，收交河公主及蘇祿可敦、爾微可敦而還，又料西國散亡數萬人，悉與拔汗那王。

translations.literal: Kashgar garrison commander Fu Menglingzha led sharp troops with the Ferghana king to mask Talas city, beheading the Black Surname Khan and his younger brother Bosi; entered Yejian city; recovered Princess Jiaohe and Suluk's khatun and Erwei khatun and returned; also assessed scattered western peoples numbering tens of thousands—all given to the Ferghana king.
translations.idiomatic: Menglingzha and the Ferghana king took Talas, killed the Black Surname Khan, recovered Princess Jiaohe, and resettled tens of thousands with Ferghana.

sentences.zh: 諸國皆降。

translations.literal: All the states submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All the states submitted.

sentences.zh: 處木昆匐延闕律啜等諸部皆上書謝曰：「生於荒裔，國亂王薨，更相攻屠。

translations.literal: The Chumukun, Fuyan, Queleichuo, and other divisions all submitted memorials of apology, saying: "Born in the wild borderlands, when the state was in turmoil and the king died, we attacked and slaughtered one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Chumukun, Fuyan, Queleichuo, and other divisions all sent memorials of apology: "Born in remote borderlands, after the kingdom fell into chaos and our king died, we turned on one another in slaughter.

sentences.zh: 賴天子遣嘉運將兵誅暴拯危，願得稽首聖顏，以部落附安西，永為外臣。

translations.literal: Relying on the Son of Heaven sending Jiayun to lead troops to punish violence and rescue peril, we wish to prostrate before the sacred countenance and attach our tribes to the Protectorate-General of Anxi, forever serving as outer subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the Son of Heaven, who sent Jiayun with troops to punish the violent and restore order, we wish to kowtow before your sacred countenance and submit our tribes to the Anxi Protectorate as perpetual outer subjects.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢闕律啜為右驍衛大將軍，冊石王為順義王，加拜史王為特進，顯酬其功。

translations.literal: The next year Queleichuo was promoted to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard; the Stone Prince was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunyi; the Shi Prince was additionally appointed Special Advance — openly rewarding their merit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Queleichuo was promoted to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guard, the Stone Prince was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunyi, and the Shi Prince was further appointed Special Advance — a public reward for their service.

sentences.zh: 嘉運俘吐火仙骨啜獻太廟，天子赦以為左金吾衛員外大將軍、脩義王，頓阿波為右武衛員外將軍。

translations.literal: Jiayun captured Tuhuoxian Guchuo and presented him at the imperial temple; the Son of Heaven pardoned him and made him Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard and Prince of Xiuyi; Dun'abo was made Supernumerary General of the Right Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun captured Tuhuoxian Guchuo and presented him at the imperial temple. The emperor pardoned him, appointing him Supernumerary Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard and Prince of Xiuyi, and made Dun'abo Supernumerary General of the Right Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 以阿史那懷道子昕為十姓可汗，領突騎施所部，莫賀達幹怒曰：「平蘇祿，我功也。

translations.literal: Ashina Huaidao's son Xin was made khan over the Ten Surnames to command the Turgesh divisions; Mohadagan angrily said: "It was I who pacified Sulu — the credit is mine.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Huaidao's son Xin was installed as khan of the Ten Surnames to command the Turgesh tribes. Mohadagan protested angrily: "I was the one who pacified Sulu. The credit belongs to me.

sentences.zh: 今立昕，謂何？

translations.literal: Now you install Xin — what does that mean?
translations.idiomatic: And now you install Xin instead — what is that supposed to mean?

sentences.zh: 」即誘諸落叛。

translations.literal: He thereupon incited the various tribes to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He then incited the various tribes to rebel.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉運招諭，乃率妻子及纛官首領降，遂命統其眾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jiayun to summon and persuade him; he then led his wife, children, and banner-chieftain leaders to submit, and was thereupon ordered to command his multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jiayun to negotiate with him. Mohadagan then submitted with his family and tribal chieftains and was appointed to command his followers.

sentences.zh: 後數年，復以昕為可汗，遣兵護送。

translations.literal: Several years later Xin was again made khan, and troops were dispatched to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Xin was again installed as khan, with troops sent to escort him.

sentences.zh: 昕至俱闌城，為莫賀咄所殺。

translations.literal: When Xin reached Julancheng he was killed by Mohaduo.
translations.idiomatic: Xin reached Julancheng, where Mohaduo killed him.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄自為可汗，安西節度使夫蒙靈詧誅斬之，以大纛官都摩支闕頡斤為三姓葉護。

translations.literal: Mohaduo declared himself khan; Anxi Military Governor Fumeng Lingcha executed him, and made the great banner-chieftain Tumozhi Quejiejin yabghu over the Three Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Mohaduo declared himself khan. Anxi Military Governor Fumeng Lingcha executed him and installed the great banner-chieftain Tumozhi Quejiejin as yabghu of the Three Surnames.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，突騎施部更以黑姓伊里底蜜施骨咄祿毗伽為可汗，數通使貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao the Turgesh division again made the Black Surname Ilidimishigudulubili khan; envoys and tribute were repeatedly sent.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the Turgesh tribes again installed Ilidimishigudulubili of the Black Surname as khan and sent envoys and tribute on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 十二載，黑姓部立登里伊羅蜜施為可汗，亦賜詔冊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Black Surname division installed Dengli Yiluomishi as khan, and an edict of investiture was also granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Black Surname tribes installed Dengli Yiluomishi as khan, and the court issued an investiture edict.

sentences.zh: 至德後，突騎施衰，黃、黑姓皆立可汗相攻，中國方多故，不暇治也。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era the Turgesh declined; both the Yellow and Black surnames each installed khans and attacked one another; China meanwhile had many troubles and had no leisure to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era the Turgesh declined. Both the Yellow and Black surnames installed rival khans and fought one another, while the court, embroiled in domestic crises, had no time to intervene.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，黑姓可汗阿多裴羅猶能遣使者入朝。

translations.literal: During the Qianyuan era the Black Surname khan Aduopeiluo still could dispatch envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan era the Black Surname khan Aduopeiluo still managed to send envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 大歷後，葛邏祿盛，徙居碎葉川，二姓微，至臣役於葛祿，斛瑟羅餘部附回鶻。

translations.literal: After the Dali era the Karluk grew powerful, moved to dwell on the Suyab River, the two surnames weakened, until they became subjects serving the Karluk; the remnant divisions of Kunsolo attached to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dali era the Karluk grew powerful and moved to the Suyab River. Weakened, the two surnames became subject to the Karluk, while the remnant tribes of Kunsolo joined the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 及其破滅，有特厖勒居焉耆城，稱葉護，餘部保金莎領，眾至二十萬。

translations.literal: When they were broken and destroyed, Tilmoch lived in the city of Karasahr and styled himself yabghu; the remnant divisions held Jinsaling, their multitude reaching two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Karluk fell, Tilmoch occupied Karasahr and styled himself yabghu. The remaining tribes held Jinsaling, their numbers reaching two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：隋季世，虛內以攻外，生者罷道路，死者暴原野，天下盜賊共攻而亡之。

translations.literal: Commentary: In the late Sui, they emptied the interior to attack abroad — the living exhausted the roads, the dead lay exposed in the wild fields; bandits throughout the realm jointly attacked and destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In the late Sui the empire drained its interior to wage foreign campaigns. The living exhausted themselves on the roads; the dead littered the fields. Bandits rose everywhere and together overthrew the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 當此時，四夷侵，中國微，而突厥最強，控弦者號百萬，華人之失職不逞皆往從之，槊之謀，導之入邊，故頡利自以為強大古無有也。

translations.literal: At this time the four barbarians invaded, China was weakened, and the Turks were strongest — those who drew the bow were said to number a million; Chinese who had lost their posts and would not submit all went to follow them, planning with spears, guiding them across the border; therefore Qilibi considered his strength such as had never existed in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the frontier peoples pressed in while China weakened. Among them the Turks were strongest — their bowmen were said to number a million. Disgraced Chinese outcasts rallied to them, plotting invasions and guiding them across the border. Qilibi believed himself mightier than any ruler in history.

sentences.zh: 高祖初即位，與和，因數出軍助討賊，故詭臣之，贈予不可計。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first ascended the throne he made peace with them, and because he repeatedly sent troops to help suppress rebels, he therefore spoke craftily to them as ministers and gave gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first took the throne he made peace with the Turks and repeatedly sent troops to help suppress rebels. He therefore flattered them and lavished gifts beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 虜見利而動，又與賊連和，殺掠吏民，於是掃國入寇，薄渭橋，騎壒蒙京師。

translations.literal: The barbarians, seeing profit, moved; they again allied with rebels, killing and plundering officials and people — thereupon they swept the realm in invasion, pressed close to Weiqiao Bridge, and cavalry dust obscured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing opportunity, the Turks allied with rebels and slaughtered and plundered officials and civilians. They then invaded in force, advancing to Weiqiao Bridge until the dust of their cavalry obscured the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗身勒兵，顯責而陰間之，戎始內阻。

translations.literal: Taizong personally led troops, openly rebuking them while secretly sowing division among them — the barbarians first showed internal obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally led his troops, rebuking the Turks openly while secretly sowing discord among them. Internal divisions began to appear among the invaders.

sentences.zh: 不三年，縛頡利獻北闕下，霆掃風除，其國遂墟。

translations.literal: Within three years Qilibi was bound and presented below the northern gate; like thunder sweeping and wind clearing, their state was then reduced to ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years Qilibi was bound and presented at the northern gate. Like a thunderbolt sweeping clean, their state was reduced to ruin.

sentences.zh: 自《詩》、《書》以來，伐暴取亂，蔑如帝神且速也，秦漢比之，陋矣。

translations.literal: Since the Odes and Documents, in punishing the violent and taking the disorderly, none has been swift and divine like the Emperor — compared to Qin and Han, how crude!
translations.idiomatic: Since the days of the Book of Songs and Book of Documents, no ruler has punished the violent and overthrown disorder with such divine speed. Qin and Han pale by comparison.

sentences.zh: 然帝數暴師不告勞，料敵無遁情，善任將，必其功，蓋黃帝之兵也。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor repeatedly exposed his armies without complaining of hardship, gauged the enemy with no hidden sentiment, well employed generals and assured their merit — this was perhaps the army of the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor repeatedly mobilized his armies without complaint, assessed the enemy with clear-eyed precision, entrusted capable generals and ensured they received credit for their victories — a style of warfare worthy of the Yellow Emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 而突厥乃以失德抗有道，浸衰當始興，雖運之盛衰屬於天，而其亡信有由矣！

translations.literal: But the Turks, having lost virtue, resisted the Way — declining just as [Tang] was rising; though the waxing and waning of fortune belongs to Heaven, their destruction truly had its cause!
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had lost virtue and resisted the righteous empire, declining just as Tang was rising. Though the rise and fall of dynasties belongs to Heaven, their fall had clear causes of their own.
